# CurveBook — Full Reference Documentation

> CurveBook is a free, open-source biostatistics, nonlinear regression, and scientific graphing application for macOS, Windows, and Linux. It runs offline with zero telemetry and opens .pzfx and .prism data files.

- Website: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/
- Online Manual: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/index.html
- Concise Index: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/llms.txt
- Source Code: https://github.com/HauserGroup/curvebook

## Quick Facts

| Property | Details |
| --- | --- |
| License | Dual-licensed under MIT OR Apache-2.0 |
| Platforms | macOS, Windows, Linux (plus FreeBSD preview) |
| Implementation | Pure Rust, independently implemented from peer-reviewed scientific literature |
| Privacy & network | Offline-first, zero telemetry, no outbound network connections, no auto-updater |
| Formats read | `.curvebook`, `.curvebook.d/`, `.cbtemplate`, `.pzfx`, `.prism`, `.csv`/`.tsv`, `.xlsx` |
| Formats written | `.curvebook`, `.curvebook.d/`, `.cbtemplate`, `.csv`/`.tsv`, `SVG`, `PDF`, `PNG`, `TIFF`, `EMF` |
| Interfaces | Desktop GUI (`curvebook`), headless CLI (`curvebook-cli`), local stdio MCP server (`curvebook-cli mcp`) |
| Source code | https://github.com/HauserGroup/curvebook |

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/get-started.html

# Get Started & Installation

CurveBook ships standalone desktop (`curvebook`) and headless CLI/MCP (`curvebook-cli`) binaries built in pure Rust with zero telemetry and zero runtime network egress.

---

## Which File Do I Need? (System Requirements & Beta Assets) {#system-requirements}

Every Beta release attaches one installer package per supported desktop platform/architecture under the naming scheme `curvebook-<version>-<os>-<arch>.<ext>`. Desktop packages bundle both the desktop GUI (`curvebook`) and the headless CLI/MCP executable (`curvebook-cli`); FreeBSD ships as a Tier 2 CLI-only archive:

| Platform | Beta Release Asset(s) | Notes & Omitted Formats (`R0.28`) |
|---|---|---|
| **macOS** | `curvebook-<version>-macos-universal.dmg` | macOS 11+ (`arm64` Apple Silicon and `x86_64` Intel universal binary); Developer ID signed & Apple-notarized (`R8.10`). Bundles `CurveBook.app` and `curvebook-cli` (no separate macOS CLI `.zip`). |
| **Windows** | `curvebook-<version>-windows-x64.msi`<br>`curvebook-<version>-windows-arm64.msi` | Windows 10/11 (`x64` / `arm64`). Currently **unsigned** pending code signing (`R8.11`). Windows `x86` (32-bit) and `-portable.zip` are dropped; Microsoft Store MSIX (`R8.9`) is a separate Store channel alternative. |
| **Linux** | `curvebook-<version>-linux-x86_64.AppImage`<br>`curvebook-<version>-linux-aarch64.AppImage` | Wayland / X11 desktop + bundled `curvebook-cli`. Requires FUSE v2 (`libfuse2`) or `--appimage-extract`. `.AppImage.zsync`, `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.tar.gz`, and Flatpak packages are omitted. |
| **FreeBSD (Tier 2 · CLI)** | `curvebook-<version>-freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` | Tier 2 CLI-only tarball for `x86_64` (`curvebook-cli` + local MCP; no desktop GUI). |
| **Shared Verification & Attribution** | `SHA256SUMS.txt`<br>`THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.html` | Published alongside every GitHub Release for checksum verification and dependency licence disclosure. |

> [!NOTE]
> The browser WebAssembly bundle (`curvebook-web`) is deferred until CurveBook `1.0` (`R0.28`, `R11`) and is not published in Beta releases.

---

## Installing Beta Release Packages {#installing-packages}

Download release assets from [CurveBook Releases](https://github.com/HauserGroup/curvebook/releases) (never the automatic GitHub "Source code" archive unless compiling from source).

### macOS (`universal.dmg`) {#install-macos}

1. Open `curvebook-<version>-macos-universal.dmg`.
2. Drag **CurveBook.app** into **Applications** (`/Applications/CurveBook.app`).
3. Beta `.dmg` releases are Developer ID signed and Apple-notarized (`R8.10`).
4. **Adding the bundled CLI (`curvebook-cli`) to `PATH`:** Beta macOS releases bundle `curvebook-cli` directly inside `/Applications/CurveBook.app/Contents/MacOS/curvebook-cli`. Either pass that full path in scripts and MCP client configs or add the `MacOS` directory to `PATH` in `~/.zshrc`:

```zsh
export PATH="/Applications/CurveBook.app/Contents/MacOS:$PATH"
```

Verify installation with `curvebook-cli --version`.

### Windows (`x64` / `arm64` `.msi`) {#install-windows}

1. Run `curvebook-<version>-windows-x64.msi` (or `curvebook-<version>-windows-arm64.msi` on Windows on ARM).
2. **Unsigned Beta SmartScreen & Store note:** Beta Windows `.msi` installers are currently **unsigned** (`R8.11` pending). After verifying `SHA256SUMS.txt` and `gh attestation verify` below, click **More info** -> **Run anyway** when Windows Defender SmartScreen shows *"Windows protected your PC"*.
   - **Windows 11 Smart App Control:** Systems running Smart App Control in enforcement mode block unsigned installers at the OS level until Authenticode signing lands (`R8.11`) or a signed Microsoft Store **MSIX** distribution ships under `R8.9` as a Store channel alternative.
3. By default, the MSI installs per-user under `%LocalAppData%\Programs\CurveBook` (exposing `curvebook.exe` and `curvebook-cli.exe`). Administrators performing machine-wide silent deployment pass `ALLUSERS=1` to `msiexec`. Cross-context user vs. machine duplicate installs are rejected until the opposite scope is uninstalled.
4. **Upgrading from Alpha `x86`:** Windows `x86` is no longer published for Beta, and upgrading directly from an Alpha `x86` `.msi` to Beta `x64` has not yet been runner-verified; uninstall any Alpha `x86` copy manually before installing `x64`.

### Linux (`x86_64` / `aarch64` `.AppImage`) {#install-linux}

1. Mark the downloaded AppImage executable and run it:

```sh
chmod +x curvebook-<version>-linux-x86_64.AppImage
./curvebook-<version>-linux-x86_64.AppImage
```

2. Run the bundled headless CLI directly via `--appimage-extract` or extract into a stable folder on systems without `libfuse2`:

```sh
./curvebook-<version>-linux-x86_64.AppImage --appimage-extract
./squashfs-root/usr/bin/curvebook-cli --version
```

See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md#linux-fuse) if FUSE v2 is unavailable.

### FreeBSD Tier 2 CLI-Only (`x86_64` `.tar.gz`) {#install-freebsd}

Extract the Tier 2 CLI-only archive and run `bin/curvebook-cli` (no desktop GUI is included on FreeBSD):

```sh
tar -xzf curvebook-<version>-freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz
```

---

## Verifying Checksums & Build Attestations {#verifying-downloads}

This section is the complete user guide for verifying Beta downloads. Download both your installer package and `SHA256SUMS.txt` from the same release tag into the same working directory before running the checks below:

- **Checksum (`SHA256SUMS.txt`):** Confirms the downloaded archive was not corrupted in transit.
- **Sigstore Build Provenance (`gh attestation verify`):** Confirms `SHA256SUMS.txt` (and every individual release file) was built by CurveBook's GitHub Actions release workflow from a recorded commit (requires the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) `gh`, signed in via `gh auth login`). Verify provenance at least once, because a checksum alone cannot protect against a tampered file paired with a tampered `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

1. **Verify `SHA256SUMS.txt` build provenance:**

```sh
gh attestation verify SHA256SUMS.txt \
  --repo HauserGroup/curvebook \
  --signer-workflow HauserGroup/curvebook/.github/workflows/release.yml
```

   For tag-built releases, also pin the release tag by appending `--source-ref refs/tags/v<version>`. Keep `--signer-workflow` included so `gh` accepts attestations only from `release.yml`.

2. **Verify your downloaded file's SHA-256 checksum against `SHA256SUMS.txt`:**

   - **macOS** (prints `OK` next to the matched file):

     ```sh
     shasum -a 256 --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS.txt
     ```

   - **Linux** (prints `OK` next to the matched file):

     ```sh
     sha256sum --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS.txt
     ```

   - **FreeBSD** (replace `<version>` if needed; exits with status `0` silently on match and reports mismatches):

     ```sh
     f=curvebook-<version>-freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz
     sha256 -c "$(awk -v f="$f" '$2 == f { print $1 }' SHA256SUMS.txt)" "$f"
     ```

   - **Windows PowerShell** (replace the filename for `arm64` if needed; prints `True` on match):

     ```powershell
     $f = "curvebook-<version>-windows-x64.msi"
     $expected = (Select-String -Path SHA256SUMS.txt -SimpleMatch "  $f").Line.Split(" ")[0]
     (Get-FileHash $f -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -eq $expected.ToUpper()
     ```

3. **Alternative — verify a downloaded installer directly via Sigstore:**

```sh
gh attestation verify <downloaded-file> \
  --repo HauserGroup/curvebook \
  --signer-workflow HauserGroup/curvebook/.github/workflows/release.yml
```

> [!NOTE]
> Linux `.AppImage` and FreeBSD `.tar.gz` assets ship without separate GPG/Minisign signature files because every release asset (and `SHA256SUMS.txt`) carries a public Sigstore provenance attestation (`R8.10`). If any verification step fails, do **not** run the installer — delete the file, re-download from [CurveBook Releases](https://github.com/HauserGroup/curvebook/releases), and report persistent mismatches via [Privacy & Security](privacy-security.md#security-reporting).


### What a Passing Check Means {#verification-meaning}

- The file's SHA-256 hash matches an attestation signed by `.github/workflows/release.yml` in `HauserGroup/curvebook`. The attestation names the commit and ref the release was built from.
- Without `--signer-workflow`, `gh` accepts an attestation from *any* workflow in the repository, so keep that option.
- It does not mean an operating system trusts the file. OS trust signing is separate (`R8.10` and `R8.11` in the roadmap): from Beta onward, macOS `.dmg` downloads are Developer ID signed and notarized, whereas Windows `.msi` (`x64` and `arm64`, following `R0.28` retirement of `x86` and `-portable.zip`) ships unsigned until `R8.11`.

### If a Check Fails {#verification-fails}

Do not open or install the file. Download it again from the release page and repeat the check. If it still fails, report it as described in [SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md).

---

## Fonts & `CURVEBOOK_FONTS_DIR` {#fonts}

CurveBook contains **zero bundled binary font files** in its source tree (`cargo xtask assets`) and relies by default on standard OS TrueType/OpenType system fonts (e.g., `Arial Unicode.ttf` / `Arial.ttf` / `AppleGothic.ttf` / `Monaco.ttf` on macOS, `NotoSansCJK` / `DejaVuSans` / `LiberationSans` on Linux/FreeBSD, `arial.ttf` / `consola.ttf` on Windows) paired with a minimal clean-room fallback vector font metrics engine and Core-14 PDF metrics.

- **Custom font directory (`CURVEBOOK_FONTS_DIR`):** Set `CURVEBOOK_FONTS_DIR` to a directory containing `.ttf` / `.otf` files (loaded lexicographically ahead of OS fallbacks for desktop canvas measurement, SVG embedding, and TrueType PDF embedding).
- **Explicit single font (`--ttf-font <path>`):** Pass `--ttf-font <path>` to `curvebook` to validate and load a specific TrueType/SFNT font at startup.

---

## Updating & Uninstalling {#updating-and-uninstalling}

### Updating Without an Auto-Updater {#updating}

Because CurveBook enforces **zero background network egress** ([Privacy & Security](privacy-security.md#zero-egress)), it never checks for updates automatically or phones home. To update:

1. Download and verify the new release package from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/HauserGroup/curvebook/releases).
2. Replace `CurveBook.app` on macOS, replace the `.AppImage` on Linux (or `.tar.gz` directory on FreeBSD), or run the new `.msi` on Windows (which preserves your remembered install folder and scope).
3. Your saved preferences, keyboard shortcuts, and recovery directory stay preserved in your OS configuration folder ([Settings, Shortcuts & Storage Paths](settings.md#storage-paths)).

### Uninstalling Cleanly {#uninstalling}

- **macOS:** Move `/Applications/CurveBook.app` to Trash and remove any `PATH` export line added to `~/.zshrc`; optionally remove `~/Library/Application Support/CurveBook`.
- **Windows:** Uninstall **CurveBook** from **Settings -> Apps -> Installed apps** (or `msiexec /x`); optionally delete `%APPDATA%\CurveBook` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CurveBook`.
- **Linux / FreeBSD:** Delete the `.AppImage` (and optional extracted `squashfs-root/`) or FreeBSD tarball folder; optionally remove `~/.config/curvebook` and `~/.local/share/curvebook`.

See [Desktop GUI Quick Start](desktop-gui.md) or [Automation: MCP](automation/mcp.md) to launch your first workspace.

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/desktop-gui.html

# Desktop GUI Getting Started (Beta)

The CurveBook desktop GUI (`curvebook`) runs a declarative `egui 0.37` / `wgpu` + AccessKit workspace pairing a curated 8-menu bar (`File`, `Edit`, `View`, `Insert`, `Data`, `Analyze`, `Graph`, `Help`), OKLab/OKLCH perceptual themes (`Light`, `Dark`, `HighContrast`), `ActionRank`-prioritized contextual toolbars (`⋯` overflow on compact windows), draggable splitters, live split data-and-graph comparison, and multi-panel figure layout composition.

> [!NOTE]
> **Beta documentation boundary (`R12.7`):** This page is the Beta desktop quick-start covering the primary interactive workspace and dialogs. The comprehensive menu-by-menu **Using the App** user guide (`R12.7`) and step-by-step workflow tutorials (`R12.2`) follow after Beta alongside recorded cross-OS manual walkthroughs (`R10.13`, `R10.24`).

See [Get Started & Installation](get-started.md) for platform packages and checksum verification.

---

## 1. Launching & Starting a Project (`Welcome & New Data Table`) {#launch-and-welcome}

When launching `curvebook` without an existing `.curvebook` argument (or starting a new workspace), CurveBook presents the 3-pane **Welcome & New Data Table** Workspace Hub (`WelcomeWizardState`) with four starting modes:

- **Empty Data Table:** Choose any of CurveBook's [structured table archetypes](tables.md#table-archetypes) (`XY`, `Column`, `Grouped`, `Contingency`, `Survival`, `Parts of Whole`, `Multiple Variables`, `Nested`), configure X-column format (`Numbers`, `Dates`, `Sequence`, `None`), and choose raw replicate subcolumns or pre-summarized entry (`Mean + SD + N`, `Mean + SEM + N`, error limits, quartiles).
- **Tutorial Sample Data:** Instantiate built-in clean-room scientific sample datasets to inspect populated tables, analyses, and graphs immediately.
- **`.cbtemplate` Templates:** Open a saved reusable template carrying preconfigured analyses, parameter rules, graphs, and layouts ready for new observations.
- **Clone Pipeline:** Duplicate an existing sheet family structure (`sheet.clonePipeline`) onto new raw data.

The two-tier top chrome features the curated 8-menu bar (`File`, `Edit`, `View`, `Insert`, `Data`, `Analyze`, `Graph`, `Help` — using native macOS menus or `--in-window-menus`), a Sheet-Adaptive Contextual Action Strip ordered by `ActionRank` (`Primary`, `Secondary`, `Overflow`), the `Cmd/Ctrl+K` Command Palette, and **Workspace Presets** (`Default`, `Data Prep`, `Modeling`, `Publication`, `Compact`). Optional launch flags (`curvebook --help`) include `--portable-dir <dir>`, `--rulers`, `--in-window-menus`, `--ttf-font <path>`, and `--new-instance`.

---

## 2. Entering Data, Exclusions & Quick Statistics {#data-and-exclusions}

1. Edit data cells directly in the Data grid (toggle row titles on `Column` tables via **View › Row Titles**), paste delimited clipboard text (`Cmd/Ctrl+V`), or open/import `.curvebook`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.pzfx`, `.prism`, or `.xlsx` files via **File › Open…**, **File › Import**, or file drag-and-drop. Importing `.prism`, `.pzfx`, or `.xlsx` into an open project with existing sheets or unsaved changes opens a replace-or-merge confirmation modal (**Add to current project** vs. **Open as new project**), and any non-fatal import warnings are shown in the **Import Warnings** panel (reopenable from the status bar or **File › Import › Import Warnings…**).
2. Selecting any numeric cell range updates the footer **Quick Statistics** readout live (`n`, `excl`, `mean`, `SD`, `SEM`, `median`, `sum`; see [Calculators & Quality-of-Life Capabilities](qol.md#quick-statistics)).
3. Toggle non-destructive observation exclusions (`Cmd/Ctrl+E`) or attach audit provenance tags (**Edit › Exclude Selection with Auditable Reason...**, `Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+E`; [`QOL-3`](concepts.md#cell-exclusions)) without deleting underlying values.
4. Create derived columns using [`=` Calculated Variables](tables.md#calculated-variables) directly in `MultipleVariables` tables (`Manage Variables…` renames, merges, orders, or pins categorical reference levels).

---

## 3. Running an Analysis, Creating Graphs & Live Split Comparison {#analysis-and-split-graph}

Run a statistical test, curve fit, or table transform from **Analyze › Analyze...** (`Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+A`), the toolbar **Analyze** CTA, or the Command Palette (`Cmd/Ctrl+K`):

- CurveBook attaches a linked `ResultSheet` under **Analyses** (with multi-tab tables, [`QOL-7` diagnostics-only assumption banner](qol.md#active-qol), and [`QOL-6` Copy Methods & Statistical Reporting](qol.md#active-qol)) and updates dependent **Graphs** automatically through the reactive DAG.
- Use **Transform / Normalize** with **Create a new graph of the results** checked to generate a graph (such as a normalized vertical-label heatmap) alongside derived data, or use **Insert › New Graph… (`Create Graph`)** to create single-series graphs across every dataset at once with a shared Y-axis title.
- In the **Portfolio Gallery**, use `Shift+Click` or `Cmd/Ctrl+Click` to select multiple graphs and invoke **Apply Style From…** (`Graph › Apply Style From…`) to clone selected formatting facets across targets in one undo step.
- Copy a rectangular cell range in any `ResultSheet` and choose **Right-click › Paste Table** on a `GraphSheet` to place a live `EmbeddedResultTable`, then customize transposing, headers, typography, and borders in **Format Embedded Table…** (`Graph › Layout › Format Embedded Table…`).
- Open **Format Graph…** or **Format Axes…** (or the Trailing Inspector dock, `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+I`) to configure opacity presets, independent **Show data points** and **Show fitted curve** checkboxes, Left Y / Right Y2 assignment, horizontal offsets, `Column`/`Grouped` horizontal orientation, Kaplan–Meier metric/staircase/error modes, pooled Forest diamond visibility, heatmap label orientations, `TickDirection`, `AbsoluteDecimal` labels, and transparent/solid page fills.
- Toggle **View › Toggle Split Data + Graph Workspace** (`Cmd/Ctrl+\`, `QOL-4`) with a draggable splitter to display a `Graph` alongside your `Data` or `Result` sheet: edits, cell exclusions, and model parameter tweaks immediately redraw the fitted curve and bands, with two-way cell/point brushing (`QOL-5`) and vertex hover readouts on longitudinal spaghetti plots.

![CurveBook light theme egui split workspace showing Project Navigator, Family tree, XY data table, live 4PL nonlinear dose–response curve fit with confidence bands, and Graph Inspector](../images/workspace-split-fit.png)

![CurveBook light theme egui split workspace showing multi-tab One-Way ANOVA multiple comparisons, QOL-7 assumption diagnostic banner and Interpret inspector, and linked Column graph with Compact Letter Display and significance brackets](../images/workspace-anova-results.png)

---

## 4. Composing Multi-Panel Page Layouts & Embedded Images {#page-layouts}

Switch to the **Layouts** section in the Project Navigator (or **Graph › Layout…**) to arrange multiple `GraphSheet`s, live tables, and images onto a physical page canvas (`LayoutSpec`, `MAX_LAYOUT_ITEMS = 64`):

- **Scaling, Alignment & Z-Order:** Apply [journal column-width presets](graphs.md#page-layouts) (`SingleColumn88mm`, `ColumnAndHalf130mm`, `DoubleColumn180mm`), align axis origins (**Graph › Layout › Align Plot Origins**), open **Equalize Scaling…** (`Match Smallest`, `Match Largest`, or `Explicit %`) to normalize inner plot scaling factors across panels, and reorder panel Z-stacking (**Bring to Front**, **Bring Forward**, **Send Backward**, **Send to Back**) with transparent `paper_fill: None` foreground overlays/insets.
- **Embedded Images & Canvas Grid:** Insert **PNG**, **JPEG**, or **TIFF** images via **Insert › Image…** (`rfd` file picker) or paste with `Cmd/Ctrl+V`, resize from corner handles (`Shift` unlocks aspect ratio), rotate (`Shift` snaps in 15° steps), edit 4-edge crop and borders in **Format Image…**, and toggle non-exported guides via **View › Canvas Grid**.
- **OKLab/OKLCH Themes & CVD Preview:** Switch `Light`, `Dark`, and `HighContrast` OKLab/OKLCH themes in [Settings & Languages](settings.md), and toggle live [CVD / grayscale canvas preview](graphs.md#palettes-and-cvd) (`QOL-9`). Broken upstream references display explicit dashed broken-link glyphs.

![CurveBook dark theme egui multi-panel Page Layout workspace with physical millimeter rulers, significance brackets, embedded summary table, and Page Layout Composer](../images/workspace-layout-dark.png)

---

## 5. Saving Projects, Templates & Publication Exports {#saving-and-exporting}

- **Save Project (`.curvebook` or `.curvebook.d/`):** **File › Save** and **File › Save As…** write atomic deterministic `.curvebook` ZIP archives (with forward-version overwrite refusal), alongside CRC-verified crash-recovery WAL journals between saves ([Files, Storage & Interchange](files.md)). Create persistent milestone snapshots via **File › Checkpoints › Create Checkpoint…**.
- **Import & Warnings (`File › Import`):** Import `.csv`/`.tsv`, `.pzfx`, `.prism`, and `.xlsx` files via **File › Import** or drag-and-drop. When importing `.prism`, `.pzfx`, or `.xlsx` into a project with existing sheets or unsaved changes, the replace-or-merge confirmation modal offers **Add to current project** alongside **Open as new project**. Non-fatal warnings open the **Import Warnings** panel, which can be reopened from the status bar or **File › Import › Import Warnings…**.
- **Export Figures (`File › Export`):** Use **File › Export** (figure export) or **File › Print…** to generate publication **SVG 1.1**, **`%PDF-1.7`** (sRGB / CMYK / Grayscale, optional glyph outlining), high-DPI **PNG** / **TIFF** (`LZW` / `Deflate` / uncompressed), Windows **`.emf`**, or multi-flavor OS clipboard vector/raster copies.
- **Export Data, Results & Reports (`File › Export`):**
  - **CSV Table…**, **CSV Results…**, and **Export All Data Tables…** open the CSV export options dialog to select delimiter, decimal separator (defaulting to the active locale preset), and (for results) all tabs in tidy format or a single tab; saving with a `.tsv` extension automatically selects the tab (`\t`) delimiter. **Export All Data Tables…** prompts for an output folder and writes one delimited file per `DataSheet`, named from the sanitized table title.
  - **JSON Results…** writes structured analysis output (`analysis.exportJson`).
  - **Save Methods Report…** writes the active result's methods summary (`result.generateReport`) to `.md`, `.txt`, or `.tex` based on the chosen extension (while **Analyze › Copy Methods & Statistical Reporting** remains available for clipboard export).

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/mcp-for-beginners.html

# Using CurveBook with Your AI Assistant

CurveBook includes both a full **[desktop app](reference/desktop-gui.md)** (`CurveBook`) and a built-in **MCP (Model Context Protocol)** server (`curvebook-cli mcp`) so you can drive analyses from a local AI assistant in plain English and inspect or refine the same `.curvebook` project in the desktop GUI.

Every Beta installer bundles both `curvebook` (desktop app) and `curvebook-cli` (CLI & MCP server) inside the same package, and everything runs locally on your computer with zero telemetry or cloud uploads.

> **Using CurveBook directly without AI?** Follow [Get Started](reference/get-started.md) to install the desktop app and browse the [Desktop App Guide](reference/desktop-gui.md).

---

## What You Need

1. **CurveBook installed** from the [Releases page](https://github.com/HauserGroup/curvebook/releases) (follow [Get Started](reference/get-started.md) to install and verify your download).
2. **An AI desktop app that supports MCP**, such as Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, or any other local MCP client.
3. **A folder for your data** — for example `Documents/MyResearchData` — where you keep your CSV/data files and `.curvebook` projects.

---

## Step 1: Locate `curvebook-cli` on Your Computer

Each CurveBook installer places `curvebook-cli` alongside the desktop application:

- **macOS:** Drag `CurveBook.app` from the `.dmg` into `/Applications`. The bundled CLI binary is at:
  ```text
  /Applications/CurveBook.app/Contents/MacOS/curvebook-cli
  ```
- **Windows:** Run the `.msi` installer (Per-User default). The bundled CLI binary is at:
  ```text
  %LocalAppData%\Programs\CurveBook\curvebook-cli.exe
  ```
  *(If you chose a machine-wide install for all users, use `%ProgramFiles%\CurveBook\curvebook-cli.exe`.)*
- **Linux:** Make the `.AppImage` executable and extract the bundled binaries once so your AI assistant can invoke `curvebook-cli` directly without unpacking the AppImage on every launch:
  ```sh
  chmod +x curvebook-<version>-linux-x86_64.AppImage
  ./curvebook-<version>-linux-x86_64.AppImage --appimage-extract
  ```
  *(Use `aarch64` instead of `x86_64` on ARM64 Linux.)* The CLI binary is inside the extracted directory at:
  ```text
  <path-to-extracted-folder>/squashfs-root/usr/bin/curvebook-cli
  ```
- **Contributors / source checkouts / FreeBSD:** Build with `cargo build --release -p curvebook-cli` and point your AI client to `target/release/curvebook-cli` inside your checkout (see [docs/mcp.md](mcp.md)).

---

## Step 2: Connect CurveBook to Your AI App (One-Time Setup)

Open your AI assistant's MCP settings file:

- **Claude Desktop (macOS):** `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` *(or **Settings → Developer → Edit Config**)*
- **Claude Desktop (Windows):** `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` *(or **Settings → Developer → Edit Config**)*
- **Other MCP clients (Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, etc.):** Open your client's `mcp.json` or MCP server configuration screen.

Add a `"curvebook"` entry matching your OS, replacing `YOURNAME` and the `--workdir` folder path with your real username and project folder.

### macOS

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "curvebook": {
      "command": "/Applications/CurveBook.app/Contents/MacOS/curvebook-cli",
      "args": [
        "mcp",
        "--workdir",
        "/Users/YOURNAME/Documents/MyResearchData"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### Windows

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "curvebook": {
      "command": "C:\\Users\\YOURNAME\\AppData\\Local\\Programs\\CurveBook\\curvebook-cli.exe",
      "args": [
        "mcp",
        "--workdir",
        "C:\\Users\\YOURNAME\\Documents\\MyResearchData"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

> **Note:** Use double backslashes (`\\`) inside Windows JSON strings, and write out your real Windows username (`YOURNAME`) instead of `%LocalAppData%` because most JSON configs do not expand environment variables.

### Linux

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "curvebook": {
      "command": "/home/YOURNAME/Applications/squashfs-root/usr/bin/curvebook-cli",
      "args": [
        "mcp",
        "--workdir",
        "/home/YOURNAME/Documents/MyResearchData"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Save the config file and **fully quit and reopen your AI app** so it detects the new `"curvebook"` server.

> **Why `--workdir`?** `--workdir` locks file access strictly to that folder and its subfolders. CurveBook will not read or write files outside it.

---

## Step 3: Run Your First Analysis in Plain English

Open a fresh chat in your AI app and paste a request like this:

> Use CurveBook to create a Column table comparing two groups:
> - Control: 10.2, 9.8, 10.5, 10.0, 10.1
> - Treated: 14.1, 13.8, 14.5, 13.9, 14.2
>
> Run a Welch's t-test, show me the summary statistics and P-value, create a box-and-whisker graph showing individual points, export the graph as `comparison.png` and `comparison.pdf`, and save the project as `first-example.curvebook`.

Your assistant will call CurveBook's tools locally, print the *t*-test summary and *P*-value in chat, and write `comparison.png`, `comparison.pdf`, and `first-example.curvebook` inside your `--workdir` folder.

---

## Step 4: Open `first-example.curvebook` in the CurveBook Desktop App

Projects created by an AI assistant use the exact same native `.curvebook` format as the desktop app:

1. Launch **CurveBook** (from `/Applications` on macOS, the Start Menu on Windows, or your `.AppImage` on Linux).
2. Choose **File › Open…** (`Cmd+O` on macOS / `Ctrl+O` on Windows & Linux) — or drag `first-example.curvebook` from your `--workdir` folder onto the CurveBook window — and open `first-example.curvebook`.
3. Explore the reactive **Project Navigator** and **Family** tree on the left: click the **Data** table to inspect values, click the **ResultSheet** to review diagnostics and parameter details, or click the **Graph** to customize axes, error bars, themes, and multi-panel layouts interactively.

You can also hand files back the other way: save edits in the desktop app, then ask your AI assistant to open the updated `.curvebook` file and run follow-up fits or batch exports.

---

## Everyday Things You Can Ask For

- **Curve fitting:** *"Fit a 4-parameter logistic (EC50) dose-response curve to this XY dataset and report IC50 with 95% confidence intervals."*
- **Model comparison:** *"Compare a 3-parameter vs 4-parameter curve fit on this table using AICc and the extra sum-of-squares F-test."*
- **Multi-group & survival statistics:** *"Import `experiment.csv`, run a one-way ANOVA with Tukey post-hoc comparisons (or Kaplan-Meier log-rank survival analysis), and tell me which differences are significant."*
- **Publication figures:** *"Export every graph in `study.curvebook` as 300 DPI PNG and vector PDF."*

---

## Troubleshooting

- **Your AI app does not see CurveBook tools:** Make sure you edited the right config file, checked your `"command"` path and JSON commas/backslashes, and **fully restarted** the AI app.
- **"Access denied" / path outside `--workdir`:** CurveBook blocks file paths outside the `--workdir` directory you configured. Move data files inside that folder or update `--workdir`.
- **More MCP connection checks:** See [Troubleshooting: MCP Connection](reference/troubleshooting.md#mcp-connection).
- **Technical reference:** See [MCP Automation Reference](reference/automation/mcp.md), [Control & Batch Automation](reference/automation/control-and-batch.md), and [docs/mcp.md](mcp.md).

---

## Your Data Stays Private

- CurveBook has **no network telemetry** and never sends spreadsheets or projects to external servers (`cargo xtask telemetry`).
- Everything runs offline inside the `--workdir` folder you choose (see [Privacy & Security](reference/privacy-security.md)).
- Your AI assistant sees only the tool parameters and summary outputs shown in your chat — never arbitrary folders outside `--workdir`.

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/concepts.html

# Concepts & Document Architecture

CurveBook stores an entire statistical and graphing study inside a single deterministic project (`ProjectDocument`) organized into five typed workspace sections, connected by a reactive directed acyclic graph (DAG), and protected by non-destructive cell exclusions, bounded session undo/redo, and explicit schema versioning.

---

## Projects, Identifiers & Document Limits {#projects-identifiers-and-limits}

A `ProjectDocument` pairs a project title, persistent analysis/workspace metadata, optional checkpoints, and an ordered collection of typed sheets. All structural sizes obey explicit upper bounds enforced during editing and archive validation:

| Limit Constant | Value | Scope |
|---|---:|---|
| `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` | `7` | Active project document JSON schema version |
| `MAX_SHEETS_PER_PROJECT` | `500` | Maximum sheets across all five navigator sections in one project |
| `MAX_ROWS` | `1,000,000` | Maximum rows per individual data table |
| `MAX_DATA_SETS` | `1,024` | Maximum dataset/group/variable columns per data table |
| `MAX_SUBCOLUMNS` | `512` | Maximum replicate subcolumns per dataset (`RawReplicates(n)`) |
| `MAX_SHEET_CELLS` | `30,000,000` | Maximum total dense cells (`rows * cols * subcols`) in one table |
| `MAX_PROJECT_CELLS` | `50,000,000` | Maximum total cells across all data sheets in one project |
| `MAX_TITLE_BYTES` | `4,096` | Maximum UTF-8 byte length for project or sheet titles |
| `MAX_SHEET_ID_BYTES` | `256` | Maximum UTF-8 byte length for a `SheetId` |
| `MAX_CHECKPOINTS_PER_PROJECT` | `32` (creation) / `64` (archive ceiling) | `project.createCheckpoint` allows up to `32` per project; archive/loader validation accepts up to `64` |

Every sheet carries a stable, non-whitespace `SheetId` (distinct across the project) and a mutable display `title`.

---

## Sheet Sections & Sheet Families {#sheet-sections-and-families}

CurveBook organizes sheets into five canonical `SheetSection` navigator folders:

| Section | Sheet Type | Role in the Workspace |
|---|---|---|
| **Data** | `DataSheet` | Typed data grid holding one of the [eight table archetypes](tables.md#table-archetypes), row titles, excluded-cell masks, exclusion provenance notes, calculated-variable formulas, and linked data regions. |
| **Info** | `InfoSheet` | Free-form notes plus typed key/value experiment constants (`Text`, `Number`, `Boolean`), including standard metadata keys (`ExperimentDate`, `Experimenter`, `Protocol`, `ProjectCode`, `NotebookId`, `LotNumber`, `Instrument`, `Notes`). Can be linked upstream via `HookSource` parameters. |
| **Analyses** | `ResultSheet` | Multi-tab statistical, transform, simulation, or curve-fitting output derived from an upstream `DataSheet` (or analyzable upstream `ResultSheet`), accompanied by diagnostic checklists (`QOL-7`), hookable scalars, curve overlays, and optional `floating_notes`. |
| **Graphs** | `GraphSheet` | Publication graph specification (`GraphSpec`) referencing one or more upstream `DataSheet`s and optional `ResultSheet` overlays (fitted curves, comparison brackets, compact letter display, live $\TeX$ equation boxes). |
| **Layouts** | `LayoutSheet` | Multi-panel physical page composition (`LayoutSpec`, up to `64` `LayoutItem` panels) arranging `GraphSheet`s, live `ResultSheet` tables, embedded raster images, and supporting text/badges with physical paper sizes and journal column-width presets. |

### Sheet Families (`family_anchor_sheet_id`) {#sheet-families}

Each sheet tracks its lineage to a root `DataSheet` via `family_anchor_sheet_id`, allowing downstream `ResultSheet`s, derived `DataSheet`s (from transforms), `GraphSheet`s, and `LayoutSheet`s to be inspected together or cloned coherently via `sheet.duplicateFamily` and `sheet.clonePipeline` (see [Command Reference](../commands.md)).

---

## Reactive DAG & Recalculation Lifecycle {#reactive-dag}

Dependencies between sheets form a strict **directed acyclic graph (DAG)** evaluated by `curvebook-engine` (`crates/engine/src/dag.rs`):

```text
InfoSheet (HookSource constants) ──┐
DataSheet (raw observations)       ├──► Formula (= Calculated Variables)
                                   ├──► LinkedDataRegion (paste / transform links)
                                   ├──► ResultSheet (Transform / Stats / Fit) ──► HookSource scalars
                                   └──► GraphSheet (series + fit overlays + CLD/TeX) ──► LayoutSheet
```

- **Cycle detection:** Formula circularity, linked-region loops (`detect_link_cycles`), and cyclic `HookSource` parameter bindings are rejected with `ErrorCode::CycleDetected` before committing edits or running recalculation.
- **Dirty propagation & topological order:** Editing a cell, toggling an exclusion, updating an `InfoSheet` constant, or modifying an `AnalysisSpec` marks downstream dependents dirty and recalculates them in deterministic topological order (`project.recalculate`).
- **Freezing (`sheet.freeze` / `sheet.unfreeze`):** Sets `frozen: bool` on a sheet (`DataSheet`, `ResultSheet`, `GraphSheet`, `LayoutSheet`). A frozen `DataSheet` (`frozen: true`) rejects direct mutations with `ErrorCode::FrozenSheet`; a frozen `ResultSheet` retains its snapshot instead of recomputing when upstream data change.
- **`ResultStatus` lifecycle:** Every `ResultSheet` reports one of three statuses:
  - `Dirty`: Upstream inputs or `AnalysisSpec` parameters changed and recalculation is pending.
  - `UpToDate`: Computed tabs, scalars, pairwise comparisons, fitted curves, and checklist reflect current upstream inputs without error.
  - `Failed { code, message }`: Most recent recalculation could not succeed for current inputs (e.g., all rows excluded or singular model); `lookup_scalar` returns `None` while failed so invalid results never propagate through hooks. When valid upstream data are restored, recalculation resumes `UpToDate` results automatically.

---

## Non-Destructive Cell Exclusions & Provenance {#cell-exclusions}

Every numeric or text cell stores `excluded: bool` independently of `value: CellValue`. Marking a cell excluded:

1. Preserves the underlying raw numeric or text value in memory, `.curvebook` archives, and `.curvebook.d/` sheet CSVs (written with a leading `*` prefix such as `*12.4` when `parse_asterisk_exclusions` is active).
2. Excludes the observation from descriptive summaries, statistical tests, curve fits, transforms, and plotted points/error bars, and omits it from selection [Quick Statistics](qol.md#quick-statistics).
3. Propagates as missing in [`=` Calculated Variables](tables.md#calculated-variables).
4. Supports optional structured provenance tags via `DataSheet::exclusion_notes: Vec<CellExclusionNote>` (`QOL-3`), storing `(coord, reason_tag, note, timestamp_utc)` (`table.excludeCellsWithReason` and `table.exclusionAuditReport`) for reproducible audit trails without touching hot numerical loops.

---

## Session Undo/Redo & Named Checkpoints {#undo-and-checkpoints}

### Bounded Session Undo/Redo {#undo-redo}

Every mutating engine command executes inside `Session` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`) as an atomic undoable step (`edit.undo`, `edit.redo`), subject to three simultaneous memory-safety caps:

| Undo Bound | Value | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| `MAX_UNDO_ENTRIES` | `64` | Maximum undo steps retained in memory per open session |
| `MAX_UNDO_CELL_BUDGET` | `25,000,000` | Cumulative table cell count cap across retained undo snapshots |
| `MAX_UNDO_CHECKPOINT_BYTES_BUDGET` | `16,777,216` (`16 MiB`) | Byte budget for full serialized snapshots in the undo stack |

Undo/redo history lives only in the active session and is intentionally not written inside `.curvebook` archives. Crash resilience between saves is handled separately by the [WAL `CrashRecoveryJournal`](files.md#crash-recovery).

### Named In-File Checkpoints (`NamedCheckpoint`) {#named-checkpoints}

For persistent milestone snapshots across sessions, `ProjectDocument` supports named in-file checkpoints (`project.createCheckpoint`, `project.listCheckpoints`, `project.restoreCheckpoint`, `project.deleteCheckpoint`, up to `32` created per project via `project.createCheckpoint`, with `crates/format` permitting up to `64` on archive validation). Each `NamedCheckpoint` stores an `id`, human-readable `name`, optional `note`, UTC timestamp, and a complete validated JSON snapshot of the project at creation time (subject to `MAX_ARCHIVE_FILE_BYTES = 128 MiB` on restore). Restoring a checkpoint creates a single undoable action in the live session.

---

## Number Formatting & *P*-Value Conventions {#number-and-pvalue-formatting}

- **Data & Tick Formatting (`LocaleNumberPolicy`, `AxisTickFormat`, `TickLabelFormat`):** Graphs and tables separate stored IEEE-754 `f64` precision from display formatting. `LocaleNumberPolicy` controls decimal separators (`.` vs `,`) and thousands grouping, while numeric axis ticks (`AxisTickFormat`) support `Decimal`, `PowerOfTenSuperscript`, `ScientificE`, `Antilog`, and `EngineeringSi` (with `TickLabelFormat` adding `Categorical(CategoricalTickSource)`) without rounding underlying computed data.
- ***P*-Value Display (`PValueFormat`):** Stored per `AnalysisSpec` (`curvebook-math`):
  - Exact numeric formats: `FourDecimal` (default, floor `< 0.0001`, up to `****`), `Apa` (`.123`, floor `< .001`, up to `***`), `Nejm` (`0.123`, floor `< 0.001`, up to `***`), and `Custom { decimals, scientific_below }` (`decimals` in `1..=15` with optional positive scientific-notation cutoff).
  - Formatting affects presentation only; multiplicity procedures and hypothesis decisions operate on full unrounded IEEE-754 probabilities.

---

## Persisted Analysis Settings (`AnalysisSpec`) {#persisted-analysis-settings}

Every `ResultSheet` embeds the complete `AnalysisSpec` that generated it, recording:

- `id`, `title`, and `source_sheet_id`
- `kind: AnalysisKind` and its method-specific option struct (test selection, tails, pairing, sphericity/REML df method, multiplicity procedure, weighting scheme, fit method, parameter rules, or power targets)
- `selected_data_sets: Vec<usize>` (empty selects all compatible columns/datasets)
- `confidence_level: ConfidenceLevel` (continuous percentage `(0, 100)`, defaulting to `95%`)
- `p_value_format: PValueFormat`

Because `AnalysisSpec` travels inside both `.curvebook` / `.curvebook.d/` projects and `.cbtemplate` reusable templates, re-running (`analysis.run`), modifying parameters (`analysis.updateParams`), or retargeting to new experimental data (`analysis.retargetData`) preserves every statistical choice deterministically. See [Command Reference](../commands.md), [Automation: MCP](automation/mcp.md), and [Automation: CLI](automation/cli.md) for programmatic parameter schemas.

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/tables.html

# Data Tables, Calculated Variables & Transforms

CurveBook separates experimental structure from visual styling through eight strictly typed table archetypes (`TableKind`), an AST-verified formula language for `=` Calculated Variables, and non-destructive transform and reshaping pipelines.

---

## The Eight Table Archetypes (`TableArchetype`) {#table-archetypes}

Every `DataSheet` belongs to one `TableKind` (`crates/doc/src/archetypes.rs`):

| Table Archetype | Primary Purpose | Column & Subcolumn Layout | Key Structural Fields |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Xy` | Continuous predictor $X$ vs. response $Y$ (regression, correlation, curves, Bland–Altman, ROC, AUC) | Optional $X$ column (`Numbers`, `Dates`, `SequenceProgression`, `ElapsedTimes`, or omitted) + datasets `A, B, ...` supporting raw replicates or summary subcolumns | `x_mode`, `x_title`, `data_sets`, `y_subcolumn_mode` (`SubcolumnMode`) |
| `Column` | One-factor comparison across independent or matched groups (`t`-tests, one-way ANOVA, descriptive stats, normality, outliers, *P*-value stacks) | One column per group (`A, B, ...`); single-replicate or subcolumn summary modes | `design_hint` (`UnpairedReplicates`, `PairedRepeatedMeasures`, `PrecomputedError`), `subcolumn_mode`, `row_titles` |
| `Grouped` | Two-way / three-way / multi-factor cell design (`Row Factor × Column Factor`, optional `C`-factor slice) | Row labels as levels of Factor A; dataset columns as Factor B (or B×C) with raw replicates or summary subcolumns per cell | `row_factor_title`, `column_factor_title`, `three_way_grouping` (`Option<ThreeWayColumnGrouping>`), `subcolumn_mode` |
| `Contingency` | Cross-tabulated non-negative integer counts ($\chi^2$, Fisher exact, $2 \times 2$ risk/odds ratios, McNemar, Cochran–Armitage, $\kappa$) | Integer counts in `[row, column]`; non-negative whole numbers (`u64` semantics on analysis) | `data_sets` (category columns), `row_titles` (category rows) |
| `Survival` | Right-censored time-to-event outcomes (Kaplan–Meier, log-rank, Gehan–Breslow–Wilcoxon, trend, cohort HR) | Shared follow-up time column + cohort columns recording event/censor indicator (`1` = event, `0` = censored by default) | `time_title`, `times`, `cohorts`, `event_code`, `censored_code` |
| `PartsOfWhole` | Proportions summing to a total (parts-of-whole charts, goodness-of-fit $\chi^2$, exact binomial proportion tests) | Single value column with `slice_labels` and category percentages/counts | `slice_labels`, `data_sets` |
| `MultipleVariables` | Tidy observational data (`rows = subjects/records`, `columns = typed variables`) for GLMs, Cox PH, PCA, clustering, multifactor ANOVA, direct multi-group tests | Typed `VariableColumn`s with explicit `VariableRole` (`Continuous`, `Categorical`, `Label`, `Calculated`) and `VariableSource` (`Entered` or `Calculated { formula }`) | `variables` (`role`, `role_inferred`, `level_order`, `source`), `row_titles` |
| `Nested` | Hierarchical cluster / nested designs (fixed treatment groups containing random biological subjects/litters/wells measured across technical replicates) | Top-level treatment groups containing `NestedGroupColumn` subclusters with technical replicate subcolumns | `groups` (`Vec<NestedGroupColumn>`), `row_titles`, `row_titles_expanded` |

### Subcolumn Modes & Pre-Summarized Entry (`SubcolumnMode`) {#subcolumn-modes}

Continuous tables (`Xy`, `Column`, `Grouped`, `Nested`) support eight `SubcolumnMode` representations (`crates/doc/src/cell.rs`):

| Mode | Subcolumns | Interpretation | Analysis Compatibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Single` | `1` | Single value per row/cell | All standard analyses |
| `RawReplicates(usize)` | `n` (`1..=512`, `MAX_SUBCOLUMNS = 512`) | Individual raw technical/biological replicates (`Mean ± SD/SEM/CI` computed dynamically) | Full parametric, nonparametric, normality, residual diagnostics, ROBUST/ROUT |
| `MeanSdN` | `3` (`Mean`, `SD`, `N`) | Pre-summarized normal moments | One/two-sample *t*, one-way/Welch/Brown–Forsythe ANOVA, OLS/WLS/Deming/Nonlinear LS, Descriptive moments; rejected with `RequiresRawReplicates` for normality, ROUT/Grubbs, Kruskal–Wallis/Mann–Whitney |
| `MeanSemN` | `3` (`Mean`, `SEM`, `N`) | Pre-summarized mean, standard error, sample size ($\text{SD} = \text{SEM}\sqrt{N}$) | Same summary-capable routines as `MeanSdN` |
| `MeanCvN` | `3` (`Mean`, `%CV`, `N`) | Mean paired with coefficient of variation and sample size ($\text{SD} = |\text{Mean}|\cdot\%\text{CV}/100$) | Same parametric moment reconstruction (`supports_parametric_moments`) and plotting |
| `MeanLowHigh` | `3` (`Mean`, `-Error`, `+Error`) | Mean with lower and upper error bounds | Plotting & central-value extraction; rejected where full replicate observations or `N`/`SD` moments are required |
| `UpperLowerLimits` | `3` (`Mean`, `LowerLimit`, `UpperLimit`) | Central mean with explicit lower and upper bounds | Plotting & `ExplicitErrorBounds`; rejected by replicate fit extraction |
| `MedianIqr` | `3` (`Median`, `Q1`, `Q3`) | Median and quartile bounds for box/error plotting | Plotting; rejected by replicate/parametric fit extraction |

`ReplicateStacking` controls how replicate columns stack or collapse during plotting and summary extraction (`SideBySide` vs `Stacked`).

---

## `=` Calculated Variables & Formula Language {#calculated-variables}

Tables support live formula evaluation (`table.setCalculatedVariable`) implemented cleanly in `crates/transform/src/formula/` (`parser.rs`, `eval.rs`, `dag.rs`).

### Formula References & Constants {#formula-references}

- **Prefix:** Formulas begin with `=` (leading `=` is stripped before AST parsing).
- **Variable & Cell References:**
  - Bare identifiers (`Conc`, `logConc`, `Ctrl_1`) or bracketed names (`[Blank Sub]`) matching column/variable titles.
  - Explicit index or quoted name lookups: `col("Title")` or `col(idx)` (0-based or column letter mapping).
  - Experiment metadata constants from linked `InfoSheet`s: `Info("Key")`.
  - Row index builtins: `$row` (1-based row number) and `$index` (0-based row index).
  - Archetype aliases: `X` and `Y` on `Xy` and `Survival` tables.
- **Built-in Constants:** `pi`, `e`, `tau` ($2\pi$), `true` (`1.0`), `false` (`0.0`), `nan` (`Missing`). Matching column titles take precedence over `pi`/`e`/`tau` (exact case-sensitive match checked first for `e`).
- **Circular Dependency Guard:** Cross-column formula references form an evaluation DAG (`formula/dag.rs`); self-references or multi-column cycles fail cleanly with `ErrorCode::CycleDetected`.

### Operators & Three-Valued Logic {#formula-operators}

| Precedence | Operators | Semantics |
|---:|---|---|
| Highest | `^` | Exponentiation (right-associative; domain errors propagate as `Missing`) |
| Unary | `+`, `-`, `!` | Numeric sign flip; logical `!` maps `Missing` to `Missing`, `0.0` to `1.0`, nonzero to `0.0` |
| Multiplicative | `*`, `/`, `%` | Multiplication, division (`0` divisor -> `Missing`), floating remainder |
| Additive | `+`, `-` | Addition, subtraction |
| Comparison | `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `==`, `=`, `!=`, `<>` | Numeric and text equality/ordering (relational `<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=` are numeric; `Missing` yields `Missing`) |
| Unary Word | `NOT` | Word-form logical negation (lower binding than comparisons so `NOT x == 0` parses as `NOT (x == 0)`) |
| Conjunction | `&&`, `AND` | Strong Kleene 3-valued AND (`false && Missing -> false`; `true && Missing -> Missing`) |
| Disjunction | `||`, `OR` | Strong Kleene 3-valued OR (`true || Missing -> true`; `false || Missing -> Missing`) |

### Supported Functions & Clauses {#formula-functions}

- **Arithmetic, Rounding & Clamping:** `abs`, `sqrt`, `cbrt`, `sqr`, `pow(x, p)`, `clamp(x, lo, hi)`, `floor`, `ceil`, `round(x[, digits])`, `trunc`, `int` (alias of `floor`), `sign` / `sgn`, `min(...)`, `max(...)`, `sum(...)`, `mean(...)`.
- **Logarithmic, Exponential & Trigonometric:** `ln`, `log(x[, base])`, `log10`, `log2`, `exp`, `exp10`, `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin` / `arcsin`, `acos` / `arccos`, `atan` / `arctan`, `atan2` / `arctan2`, `sinh`, `cosh`, `tanh`.
- **Special & Statistical Transforms:** `erf`, `erfc`, `lgamma`, `logit(p)` (for $p \in (0, 1)$), `probit(p)` ($5 + \Phi^{-1}(p)$, Finney probit scale), `norm_ppf` / `norm_inv` / `qnorm` / `inv_norm`, `arcsin_sqrt(p)` ($\arcsin\sqrt{p}$ for $p \in [0, 1]$).
- **Logical & Missing-Value Handling:** `if(cond, then_expr, else_expr)` (short-circuiting only the chosen branch), `isnan(x)`, `isvalid(x)` / `is_defined(x)`, `coalesce(a, b, ...)`, variadic `and(...)`, `or(...)`, `not(x)`.
- **Whole-Column Aggregates:** `sum`, `mean`, `count` (numeric active cells), `counta` (non-empty active numeric/text cells), `sd` / `stdev`, `sem` / `stderr`, `var`, `median`, `iqr`, `min_col` / `col_min`, `max_col` / `col_max`, `geo_mean`, `percentile(col, p)` / `quantile(col, p)`.
- **Conditional `*if` Aggregates:** `countif`, `countaif`, `sumif`, `meanif`, `minif`, `maxif`, `stdevif` / `sdif`, `stderrif` / `semif`. Argument order is deterministically `(values, condition)` (or `countif(condition)` / `countif(values, condition)` where rows matching nonzero finite `condition` are included); `countaif` counts non-empty text/numeric cells matching the predicate.
- **Window Functions & SQL-Style Clauses:**
  - Window functions: `row_number()`, `rank()`, `dense_rank()`, `center(expr)`, `standardize(expr)` / `zscore(expr)`, `cumsum(expr)`, `cumprod(expr)`, `cummean(expr)`, `lag(expr[, offset[, default]])`, `lead(expr[, offset[, default]])`, `diff(expr[, offset])`, `rolling_mean(expr, window)` / `moving_avg(expr, window)`, `rolling_sum(expr, window)`.
  - Filter & Window clauses: `FILTER (WHERE <cond>)` / `WHERE <cond>` (applicable inside aggregates and `OVER (...)`), plus `OVER ([PARTITION BY ...] [ORDER BY <expr> [ASC|DESC] [NULLS FIRST|LAST]] [ROWS <frame>])` supporting `UNBOUNDED PRECEDING`, `<k> PRECEDING`, `CURRENT ROW`, `<k> FOLLOWING`, and `UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING`.
- **Evaluator Scope & Error Propagation:** Formula values are `Number(f64)`, `Text(String)`, or `Missing`. String-manipulation functions and date/calendar arithmetic functions are **not** present in the Beta formula evaluator. Empty cells, excluded cells, division by zero, out-of-domain operations (`ln(-1)`, `sqrt(-1)`, `probit(0)`), non-finite intermediates (`NaN`, `±Inf`), and unhandled type mismatches propagate deterministically as `FormulaValue::Missing` (stored as an empty `Cell`).

---

## Table Transforms, Reshaping & Simulation {#transforms-and-reshaping}

CurveBook executes derived transforms (`transform.run`, `table.convertArchetype`, `table.importPlateMap`, `table.importTidyLong`, `table.randomizeGroups`, `table.randomSampleRows`, `table.simulateDistributions`, `table.simulateXy`) without altering upstream raw cells:

| Transform / Operation | Purpose & Options | Edge Cases & Guards |
|---|---|---|
| **Math Transforms (`MathTransformPreset`)** | Per-cell preset transforms over `X` or `Y`: `Ln`, `Log10`, `Log2`, `Exp10`, `Exp`, `Reciprocal`, `Sqrt`, `Square`, `Logit`, `Probit`, `ArcsinSqrt`, `LinearScale { slope, intercept }`, `ConcentrationToNegativeLogM { molar_unit_factor }` (and arbitrary `=` Calculated Variable formulas including `2^-y` qPCR pipelines). | Non-positive inputs for `Log*`/`Reciprocal`, negative inputs for `Sqrt`, or probabilities outside `(0, 1)` for `Logit`/`Probit` yield empty missing cells or typed errors rather than `NaN`. |
| **Normalize (`NormalizeAnchor`)** | Scales each dataset between `0%` and `100%` (or `0.0`..`1.0`) defined by `zero_anchor` and `hundred_anchor` (`ColumnMin`, `ColumnMax`, `ColumnSum`, `FirstRow`, `LastRow`, `FixedValue(v)`, `ControlColumnMean { column }`, `Hooked(HookSource)`). | Rejects zero span (`y_100 == y_0`) with an error to avoid division by zero. |
| **Baseline (`BaselineOperation`)** | Subtracts or ratios designated `baseline_columns`: `Difference`, `Ratio`, `PercentChange`, or `FractionalChange`. | Zero baseline divisors in `Ratio` / `PercentChange` / `FractionalChange` omit/error on undefined denominators; excluded cells remain skipped. |
| **Row Summary & Replicate Transposition (`Transpose`, `SelectAndTransform`)** | Swaps rows and columns (`transpose_cell_grid`), subsets/reorders rows or columns, filters rows by predicate, or applies column-wise transforms while preserving cell exclusion masks. | Enforces `MAX_ROWS`, `MAX_DATA_SETS`, `MAX_IMPORT_CELLS = 10,000,000`, and remaps exclusion masks atomically. |
| **Curve Calculus (`CurveSheetOp`, `compute_sheet_auc`)** | `Smooth` (`MovingAverage`, `SavitzkyGolay`, `Lowess` of Cleveland 1979 with bisquare `6*MAD` robustness), `Differentiate` (`First` / `Second` 3-point Lagrange quadratic derivative on sorted uniform or non-uniform `X`), `Integrate` (cumulative trapezoidal area above `baseline`), and trapezoidal AUC with total/net/baseline-corrected peaks (`Yeh & Kwan 1978`). | Duplicate `X` values reject differentiation with `InvalidInput`; LOWESS `span` must lie in `(0, 1]`. |
| **Non-Destructive Archetype Conversion (`QOL-1`, `table.convertArchetype`)** | Projects among `Column`, `Grouped`, `Xy`, `MultipleVariables`, and `Contingency` with non-mutating `ConversionPreview` (`preserved_cells`, `dropped_cells`, `preserved_exclusions`, `warnings`, `lossy`). | Preserves `excluded` masks and remaps `CellExclusionNote` coordinates. Refuses lossy projections (e.g., negative/fractional entries targeting `Contingency`, collapsed subcolumns) unless `allow_lossy = true`. |
| **Microplate Mapper (`QOL-2`, `table.importPlateMap`)** | Maps `8×12` (96-well) or `16×24` (384-well) reader grids into typed `Xy`, `Column`, or `Grouped` tables by assigning concentrations ($X$), treatment groups, technical replicates, and optional blank subtraction/tagging. | Validates well grid dimensions (`8×12` or `16×24`), non-empty assignments, and cell budget limits. |
| **Tidy Long-to-Wide Pivot (`QOL-2`, `table.importTidyLong`)** | Reshapes tidy long rows `(X/Row Factor, Group Column, Optional Replicate Index, Value, Optional Exclusion Flag)` directly into typed `Xy`, `Column`, or `Grouped` replicate subcolumns. | Preserves exclusion flags from indicator column; rejects out-of-range column indices and excessive subcolumn expansions above `MAX_SUBCOLUMNS = 512`. |
| **Randomization & Row Sampling (`QOL-14`)** | `table.randomizeGroups`: seeded `Complete` or `PermutedBlock` allocation across $k \ge 2$ arms over `DeterministicRng`, emitting a schedule sheet + `InfoSheet` ARRIVE metadata. `table.randomSampleRows`: uniform or stratified $k$-of-$N$ sampling without replacement via partial Fisher–Yates. | Block sizes must be positive multiples of the summed integer allocation weights; empty strata and $k > N$ fail cleanly with typed validation errors. |
| **Monte Carlo & Distribution Simulation (`QOL-14`, `table.simulateDistributions`, `table.simulateXy`)** | Generates independent seeded columns (`Uniform`, `Normal`, `LogNormal`, `Binomial`, `Poisson`, `Exponential`) or synthetic `Xy` noisy curves (`Gaussian`, `Uniform`, `LogNormal` / multiplicative noise). | Deterministic across native and `wasm32` targets given the recorded 64-bit PRNG seed. |
| **4-Stage `ImportLinkSpec` Pipeline** | Reconciles upstream `DataSheet`, `ResultSheet`, or delimited text payloads across `filter -> reshape/transpose -> baseline -> exclude/*` while maintaining `LinkedDataRegion` provenance. | Cycle detection via Kahn's topological sort (`detect_link_cycles`) aborts circular sheet links before mutation. |

See [Concepts & Document Architecture](concepts.md), [Analysis Kinds Registry](registry/tables.html#analysis-kinds), and [Command Reference](../commands.md) for parameter schemas.

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/analyses.html

# Statistical Analyses & Transforms Reference

This reference documents every statistical, transformation, and regression `AnalysisKind` implemented in CurveBook, paired one-to-one with the generated [Analysis Kinds Registry](registry/tables.html#analysis-kinds) and [Table Archetypes](tables.md#table-archetypes). Every entry describes compatible tables, engine commands and canonical `snake_case` parameters with defaults, reported `ResultSheet` tabs and scalar keys, `QOL-7` assumption diagnostics, boundary/edge behavior, and published **Decision D1** clean-room verification oracles.

> [!NOTE]
> Under CurveBook's **QOL-7** contract, every `ChecklistItem` across all analyses sets `remediation: None`. Checklists surface assumption test metrics, sample-size thresholds, convergence statuses, and missing-data notes objectively without automatically recommending alternative tests or data transformations ([Quality of Life Capabilities](qol.md#active-qol)).

- **Global `AnalysisSpec` controls:** Every analysis stores `confidence_level` (engine commands enforce `confidence_percent` in $(1.0, 99.99]$, default `95.0`; `AnalysisSpec` validates $[0.01, 99.99]$), `p_value_format`, and `selected_data_sets` (empty selects all compatible columns unless an analysis requires explicit indices). Excluded cells are always omitted non-destructively prior to analysis ([Cell Exclusions](concepts.md#cell-exclusions)).
- **Unified execution commands:** Engine callers run [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) (or domain commands `transform.run`, `stats.run`, `fit.run`, `analysis.add`, `analysis.run`, `analysis.updateParams`, `analysis.retargetData`). Unknown option keys for a selected `AnalysisKind` are rejected cleanly (`ErrorCode::BadInput`; see [Engine Error Codes](registry/tables.html#error-codes)).
- **Shared multiplicity procedure names (`multiplicity`):** Post-hoc and row-wise procedures use canonical `snake_case` names: `none` (default unadjusted / omnibus only), `tukey_hsd`, `dunnett` (paired with `control_column`), `sidak`, `bonferroni`, `holm_sidak`, `dunnett_t3`, `games_howell`, `tamhane_t2`, `dunn_rank_sum`, `linear_trend`, `benjamini_hochberg_fdr`, `benjamini_yekutieli_fdr`, `two_stage_bky_fdr`, `newman_keuls`, and `fisher_lsd`. FDR methods interpret `threshold` as desired false discovery rate $Q$; FWER methods interpret `threshold` as family-wise $\alpha$ (default `0.05`; [Concepts: Number Formatting](concepts.md#number-and-pvalue-formatting)).

---

## Data Transforms, Reshaping & Simulation {#analysis-transform}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Applies non-destructive element-wise mathematical transforms, normalizations, baseline removals, matrix transpositions, row pruning, formula-based selection/derived columns, synthetic XY simulation, or stratified/random row sampling, emitting a linked derived [`DataSheet`](concepts.md#reactive-dag) alongside a summary `ResultSheet`. Accepts all [Table Archetypes](tables.md#table-archetypes) (`Math`, `Normalize`, `RemoveBaseline`, `Transpose`, `PruneRows`, `SelectAndTransform`, `Simulate`, `RandomSample`; see [Analysis Registry: `transform`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-transform)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `transform.run` using shorthands `math` (canonical), `transform`, `normalize`, `remove_baseline`, `baseline`, `transpose`, `prune`, `prune_rows`, `select`, `select_and_transform`, `simulate`, or `random_sample`. Canonical parameter keys span all operation modes:
  - `math`: `x_transform`, `y_transform` (`None` or preset: `log10`, `ln`, `log2`, `exp10`, `exp`, `reciprocal`, `square`, `sqrt`, `logit`, `probit`, `arcsin_sqrt`, etc.), `error_propagation` (`replicate_endpoints` or `first_order_delta_method`).
  - `normalize`: `zero_anchor`, `hundred_anchor` (`ColumnMin`, `ColumnMax`, `FirstRow`, `LastRow`, `Constant`, `Hooked`), `output_percent` (bool), `per_data_set` (bool).
  - `remove_baseline`: `baseline_columns`, `operation` (`subtract`, `divide`, `ratio_change`, `percent_change`).
  - `transpose`: `swap_row_and_column_titles` (bool).
  - `prune_rows`: `every_k_rows` (`>= 1`), `average_window` (bool).
  - `select_and_transform`: `filter_formula`, `target_archetype`, `derived_columns`.
  - `simulate`: `seed`, `row_count`, `replicates`, `x_min`, `x_max`, `equation_id`, `parameters`, `noise`.
  - `random_sample`: `seed`, `sample_size`, `stratify_column`, `proportional_allocation`.
- **Reported values:** Emits a derived [`DataSheet`](tables.md#transforms-and-reshaping) and a `MainSummary` (`summary`) `ResultTab` recording transform metadata, anchor scalars (`ZeroAnchor`, `HundredAnchor`), or sampling parameters (`sample_size`, `population_size`, `seed` when exact in `f64`). Additional utility curve transforms (`compute_auc`, Savitzky–Golay / LOWESS smoothing, numerical derivatives, integrals) are documented under [Transforms & Reshaping](tables.md#transforms-and-reshaping).
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Emits non-fatal warnings and checklist notes whenever a nonlinear transform or domain guard blanks an endpoint or derivative (for example `ln(u)` at $u \le 0$ or `MeanCvN` with zero transformed mean); sets `remediation: None`.
- **Edge cases & limits:** In [pre-summarized subcolumns](tables.md#subcolumn-modes) (`MeanSdN`, `MeanSemN`, `MeanCvN`, `MeanLowHigh`, `MedianIqr`, `UpperLowerLimits`), `FirstOrderDeltaMethod` scales spread by $|g'(\text{mean})|$ (swapping asymmetric `-Error`/`+Error` bounds when $g' < 0$ and preserving exclusion provenance notes), whereas `ReplicateEndpoints` maps $[\text{mean} - \text{SD}, \text{mean} + \text{SD}]$ through $g$ and halves the width. Equal `zero_anchor == hundred_anchor` fails with `TransformError` (`InvalidInput`), and `RandomSample` honors stratified quotas deterministically via `DeterministicRng`.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** JCGM 100:2008 / GUM §5.1.2 (delta-method uncertainty propagation); Zar (2010) (logit, probit, angular $\arcsin\sqrt{u}$ transforms); Cleveland (1979) & Savitzky–Golay (1964) / Gorry (1990) (curve smoothing); verified by `d1_normalization.rs` (`mpmath 1.3.0` 80/120-digit rational/transcendental references, `LINEAR_TOL = 1e-12`), `d1_randomization.rs`, and `d1_curve_transforms.rs`.

---

## Column Descriptive Statistics, Normality & One-Sample Tests {#analysis-descriptive-stats}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Computes column-wise sample size, location, dispersion, quantiles, geometric summaries, confidence intervals of the mean/SD/median, skewness/kurtosis, a multi-test Gaussian/lognormal normality battery, Normal Q-Q coordinates, and optional one-sample hypothesis tests against `hypothetical_value`. Compatible with `Column`, `Xy`, `Grouped`, and `MultipleVariables` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `descriptive-stats`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-descriptive-stats)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `descriptive_stats` (canonical), `descriptive`, or `column_stats`.
  - `aggregation`: `row_means` (default, collapses raw replicate subcolumns by row mean first) or `pooled_grand_sample` (pools all active replicates).
  - `custom_upper_percentile`: optional upper percentile $p_{\text{hi}} \in [50.0, 100.0)$ reporting $(100 - p_{\text{hi}}, p_{\text{hi}})$ Hyndman–Fan Type-7 quantiles (default `None`).
  - `run_normality_battery`: bool (default `true`).
  - `hypothetical_value`: optional finite null location $\mu_0$ triggering one-sample Student *t* and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (default `None`).
- **Reported values:**
  - `DescriptiveSummary` (`desc-summary` or `desc-pooled`): $N$, Minimum, 25% Percentile, Median, 75% Percentile, Maximum, Range, Mean, Std. Deviation, Std. Error of Mean, Lower/Upper `conf%` CI of Mean, `conf%` CI of SD ($\chi^2$ normal-theory variance interval), exact/interpolated binomial CI of Median, Coefficient of Variation (%CV), Geometric Mean & Geometric SD Factor (when all values $> 0$), Harmonic Mean (when no zeros/incompatible signs), Skewness ($G_1$), Excess Kurtosis ($G_2$), and lag-1 autocorrelation ($r_1$).
  - `Diagnostics` (`normality`): Shapiro–Wilk $W$ ($3 \le n \le 5000$), D'Agostino–Pearson omnibus $K^2$ ($n \ge 8$), Anderson–Darling $A^{2*}$ ($n \ge 5$), and Lilliefors Kolmogorov–Smirnov $D$ ($n \ge 5$) evaluated on both untransformed data and $\ln(Y)$ (lognormality, when strictly positive).
  - `NormalQq` (`normal-qq`): Blom (1958) plotting positions $p_i = (i - 3/8) / (n + 1/4)$ and normal/lognormal $z$ quantiles.
  - `MainSummary` (`one-sample`): When `hypothetical_value` is set, one-sample *t*-test ($t, \text{df}, P$) and Wilcoxon signed-rank test ($W, P$, Pratt 1959 zero handling and Hodges–Lehmann pseudomedian/Walsh-average CI).
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Appends Shapiro–Wilk normality `ChecklistItem` per column (`Pass` if $P > \alpha$, `Warn` if $P \le \alpha$) plus `Info` checklist notes when ignoring non-numeric text cells; strictly `remediation: None`.
- **Edge cases & limits:** On [pre-summarized subcolumns](tables.md#subcolumn-modes) (`MeanSdN`, `MeanSemN`, `MeanCvN`), `summarize_pre_summarized_points` reconstructs exact pooled Mean, SD, SEM, $N$, and CI of Mean (nonparametric quantiles, medians, Q-Q plots, and normality/Wilcoxon tests require raw values and are omitted); `ZeroVariance` suppresses *t*-statistics cleanly while reporting constant summaries; `EmptyInput` when no finite numeric cell remains.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Hyndman & Fan (1996) Type-7 quantiles; Royston (1995) AS R94 Shapiro–Wilk; D'Agostino, Belanger & D'Agostino (1990) $K^2$; Anscombe & Glynn (1983); Stephens (1986) Anderson–Darling; Lilliefors (1967) & Dallal & Wilkinson (1986); Pratt (1959) & Hollander, Wolfe & Chicken (2014); Kirkwood (1979) geometric SD; verified by NIST StRD Univariate (`nist_strd.rs` >= 14.5 LRE), `d1_reference_oracles.rs`, `d1_extended_stats_oracles.rs` (`SciPy 1.18.1` `normaltest`/`anderson` & `statsmodels 0.15.0` `normal_ad`/`lilliefors`), and `r017_lilliefors_oracles.rs`.

---

## Outlier Detection (Grubbs & ROUT) {#analysis-outlier-detection}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Screens each column independently for single or multiple univariate statistical outliers using either normal-theory Grubbs Extreme Studentized Deviate (ESD) or robust ROUT false-discovery-rate screening. Compatible with `Column`, `Xy`, `Grouped`, and `MultipleVariables` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `outlier-detection`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-outlier-detection)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `outliers` (canonical), `outlier`, `rout`, or `grubbs`.
  - **ROUT (`OutlierSpec::Rout`, default shorthand `"rout"` / `"outliers"`):** `fdr_q_percent` in $(0.0, 100.0]$ (default `1.0` for $Q = 1\%$). Note univariate column ROUT permits $Q \in (0, 100]$, whereas curve-fitting ROUT restricts $Q \in (0, 50]$.
  - **Grubbs (`OutlierSpec::Grubbs`):** `alpha` in $(0.0, 1.0)$ (default `0.05`) and `iterative` (bool, default `false` for single outlier vs `true` for sequential ESD elimination).
- **Reported values:** `MainSummary` (`outliers` — "Identified Outliers") listing `Column`, 1-based `Row Index`, observed `Value`, test `Statistic` ($G$ or $t_i = |y_i - M| / \text{RSDR}$), and `Threshold / P` (Grubbs critical $G_{\text{crit}}$ or BH adjusted $q$-value). Emits scalars `OutlierCount` per column, plus `RobustCenter` and `RSDR` under ROUT.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Grubbs assumes approximate normality of the clean core; ROUT uses the median and $68.27\%$ percentile `RSDR` across absolute deviations from the median, testing only the top $30\%$ furthest observations via Benjamini–Hochberg (1995). Checklist reports detected outlier count (`Info` if $> 0$, `Pass` if $0$, `remediation: None`) noting that experimental provenance governs whether a flagged cell should be excluded.
- **Edge cases & limits:** Grubbs requires $n \ge 3$ and returns zero outliers when $\text{SD} = 0$; `ROUT` handles $n \ge 3$ without masking multiple extreme outliers; zero-spread clean cores (`RSDR` at floating-point floor) protect against dividing by zero while still flagging points strictly away from constant mass. Non-numeric cells are ignored with an audit note.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Grubbs (1969); Rosner (1983) generalized ESD; Motulsky & Brown (2006) ROUT & Benjamini & Hochberg (1995); verified by `d1_reference_oracles.rs`, `d1_extended_stats_oracles.rs`, and `d1_edge_matrix.rs`.

---

## Two-Group & One-Sample Comparisons {#analysis-two-group-comparison}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Compares two independent columns, matched pairs, or a single column against a hypothetical location across parametric, lognormal/ratio, and nonparametric rank/distribution methods. Compatible with `Column` and `MultipleVariables` tables (using `mv_group_column` + `mv_response_column` to split a two-level factor in long tables; see [Analysis Registry: `two-group-comparison`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-two-group-comparison)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `unpaired_t` (canonical), `t_test`, `unpaired_t_test`, `welch_t`, `paired_t`, `ratio_paired_t`, `lognormal_unpaired_t`, `mann_whitney`, `wilcoxon`, `wilcoxon_matched_pairs`, `kolmogorov_smirnov`, `ks_test`, `paired_sign_test`, `sign_test`, `one_sample_t`, `one_sample_wilcoxon`. Canonical keys:
  - `method`: selects among `unpaired_t` (default), `welch_t`, `paired_t`, `ratio_paired_t`, `lognormal_unpaired_t`, `mann_whitney`, `wilcoxon_signed_rank`, `kolmogorov_smirnov`, `paired_sign_test`, `one_sample_t { hypothetical }`, `one_sample_wilcoxon { hypothetical }`.
  - `two_tailed`: bool (default `true`). Note one-tailed rank tests evaluate the tail strictly in the observed sample direction (`r35_survival_twogroup_oracles.rs`).
  - `compute_effect_sizes`: bool (default `true`): reports Cohen's $d$, Hedges' $g$, Glass's $\Delta$ with noncentral-$t$ confidence intervals, $R^2$ ($\eta^2$), plus rank-biserial correlation / Cliff's $\delta$ (`MannWhitney`, `Wilcoxon`), or matched-pair difference metrics.
  - `mv_group_column`, `mv_response_column`, `hypothetical`.
- **Reported values:** `MainSummary` tab (`two-group`, `paired-t`, `mann-whitney`, etc.) reporting group means/medians, difference/ratio of means or Hodges–Lehmann median shift (`ConfidenceInterval`), test statistic ($t, U, W, D_{\text{KS}}, S$), $\text{df}$, $P$ value, variance equality *F*-test and median-centered Levene / Brown–Forsythe test (unpaired tests), pairing correlation $r$ & $P$ (`paired_t` / `ratio_paired_t`), and requested effect sizes. For `ratio_paired_t` and `lognormal_unpaired_t`, back-transforms geometric mean ratios $\exp(\Delta \bar{y}_{\ln})$ and CIs.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Evaluates group Shapiro–Wilk normality, *F*-test / Levene homoscedasticity, pairing effectiveness ($r$, including warning if $r \le 0$ or $|r| = 1$ degenerate), Hodges–Lehmann CI achieved coverage (exact binomial / Wilcoxon distribution bounds may fall slightly below nominal `conf%` for small $n$), and non-positive values in lognormal/ratio methods (`InvalidParameter`). All checklist entries keep `remediation: None`.
- **Edge cases & limits:** Supports [pre-summarized subcolumns](tables.md#subcolumn-modes) (`MeanSdN`, `MeanSemN`, `MeanCvN`) for parametric `unpaired_t`, `welch_t`, and `one_sample_t` (`*_from_summary`, retaining exact variance *F*-test while omitting raw-only `levene_median`); exact permutation/Wilcoxon distributions apply for moderate sizes with tie-corrected normal asymptotic fallback (Pratt 1959 zero-difference handling; exact $O((m+n)\log(mn))$ order-statistic selection for Hodges–Lehmann when $m \cdot n > 40000$). Non-paired complete-case filtering skips rows where either paired column is blank/excluded with an audit checklist note.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Student (1908); Welch (1947); Satterthwaite (1946); Mann & Whitney (1947); Wilcoxon (1945); Pratt (1959); Hodges & Lehmann (1963); Moses interval; Smirnov (1948) & Hodges (1958) two-sample KS; Dixon & Mood (1946) sign test; Cohen (1988), Hedges (1981), & Steiger & Fouladi (1997) noncentral-$t$ effect-size CIs; Cliff (1993) & Wendt (1972) / Kerby (2014); Levene (1960) & Brown & Forsythe (1974a); verified by `d1_reference_oracles.rs`, `d1_extended_stats_oracles.rs`, `r35_survival_twogroup_oracles.rs`, and `wave21_r97_r912_clustering.rs`.

---

## Bland–Altman Method Comparison {#analysis-bland-altman}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Evaluates agreement between two quantitative measurement assays on matched subjects by computing pair-wise differences (`A - B` or `% difference` $100 \cdot (A - B) / ((A + B)/2)$) versus pair averages `(A + B) / 2`, estimating mean bias and $95\%$ (or `confidence_level`) Limits of Agreement ($\text{LoA} = \text{bias} \pm z_{1-\alpha/2} \cdot \text{SD}_{\text{diff}}$). Compatible with `Column`, `Xy`, and `MultipleVariables` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `bland-altman`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-bland-altman)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `bland_altman` (canonical) or `stats.bland_altman`.
  - `column_a`: 0-based index of method *A* (default `0`).
  - `column_b`: 0-based index of method *B* (default `1`).
  - `percent_difference`: bool (default `false` for absolute `A - B`; `true` for percentage difference).
  - `xy_compare_x_vs_y`: optional bool on `Xy` tables (`Some(true)` forces $X$ vs $Y_0$; `Some(false)` uses `Y[column_a]` vs `Y[column_b]`; `None` defaults to $X$ vs $Y_0$ when one $Y$ dataset exists and $Y$ datasets otherwise).
- **Reported values:**
  - `MainSummary` tab (`bland-altman`): Number of paired subjects $n$, Mean Bias with SE and `conf%` *t*-based CI, SD of differences, Lower and Upper Limits of Agreement ($\text{bias} \pm z_{1-\alpha/2} \cdot \text{SD}_{\text{diff}}$) with exact Bland–Altman (1999) asymptotic standard errors $\text{SD} \sqrt{1/n + z^2 / (2(n - 1))}$ and *t*-CIs, plus proportional-bias OLS slope/intercept/$P$ regressing difference on average.
  - `Residuals` tab: Per-pair `(Average, Difference)` coordinates for Bland–Altman scatter plotting.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Checks normality of paired differences (Shapiro–Wilk when $3 \le n \le 5000$), checks proportional bias ($P$ value of difference-vs-mean slope), and emits complete-case pair filtering notices (`remediation: None`).
- **Edge cases & limits:** Fails with `ZeroVariance` / `InvalidParameter` under `percent_difference: true` if any pair has average $(A + B)/2 = 0$; skips incomplete rows where either method is empty or excluded; rejects pre-summarized tables when raw subject pairs are required.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Bland & Altman (1986, 1999); verified against R 4.5.2 in `d1_reference_oracles.rs`, `d1_extended_stats_oracles.rs`, and `audit_twogroup_col_fixes.rs`.

---

## Multiple Row-Wise *t*-Tests & Nonparametric Tests {#analysis-multiple-row-t-tests}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Executes independent or paired two-group comparisons independently across every row of a table (common in high-throughput screening, dose/time response tables, or volcano-plot workflows), applying FWER or FDR multiplicity adjustment across all testable rows. Compatible with `Grouped`, `Xy`, `Column` (pairing replicate column blocks), and `MultipleVariables` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `multiple-row-t-tests`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-multiple-row-t-tests)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `multiple_row_t_tests` (canonical), `stats.multiple_row_t_tests`, `multiple_row_tests`, `multiple_t_tests`.
  - `paired`: bool (default `false`). Requires matched replicate subcolumns within `Grouped`/`Xy` or an even number ($\ge 4$) of selected columns in `Column` tables.
  - `nonparametric`: bool (default `false`; runs Mann–Whitney $U$ or Wilcoxon signed-rank per row when `true`).
  - `assume_equal_sd`: bool (default `true`; Student pooled variance when `true`, Welch–Satterthwaite when `false`; applies only when `!paired && !nonparametric`).
  - `multiplicity`, `threshold` (default `0.05`), `report_confidence_intervals`, `control_column` (supports `BenjaminiHochbergFdr`, `TwoStageBkyFdr`, `BenjaminiYekutieliFdr`, `HolmSidak`, `Bonferroni`, `Sidak`, or `None`).
- **Reported values:**
  - `MainSummary` & `MultipleComparisons` (`multiple-row-comparisons`) tabs: Per-row $n_A, n_B$, Mean/Median difference, $\text{SE}$, test statistic, raw unadjusted *P*, adjusted *P* or FDR *q*-value, $-\log_{10}(P)$ volcano coordinates, `Discovery?` boolean flag, and optional CI of difference.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Reports how many rows were evaluated vs skipped (due to insufficient finite replicates or degenerate zero variance in both samples) plus multiplicity control family summary (`FWER` vs `FDR`, `remediation: None`).
- **Edge cases & limits:** Strictly rejects [pre-summarized subcolumns](tables.md#subcolumn-modes) (`StatsError::RequiresRawReplicates`) across `Grouped`, `Xy`, and `Column` inputs because raw replicate cells per row are required. On `Column` tables with split-group selection, requires at least $4$ selected columns (even count when `paired: true`).
