- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Benjamini & Hochberg (1995); Benjamini, Krieger & Yekutieli (2006); Holm (1979); Šídák (1967); verified in `r35_power_multiplicity_oracles.rs`, `d1_extended_stats_oracles.rs` (`statsmodels 0.15.0` `fdr_tsbky`), and `audit_twogroup_col_fixes.rs`.

---

## Passing–Bablok Regression {#analysis-passing-bablok}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Fits Passing & Bablok (1983) nonparametric errors-in-variables linear method-comparison regression $Y = \alpha + \beta X$, resilient to outliers and measurement error in both *X* and *Y*. Compatible with `Column`, `Xy`, and `MultipleVariables` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `passing-bablok`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-passing-bablok)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `passing_bablok` (canonical) or `stats.passing_bablok`.
  - `x_column`: 0-based index of reference assay column *X* (default `0`).
  - `y_column`: 0-based index of candidate assay column *Y* (default `1`).
- **Reported values:** `MainSummary` and `ParametersAndConfidenceIntervals` tabs plus scalars (`Slope`, `Slope CI lower/upper`, `Intercept`, `Intercept CI lower/upper`, `CUSUM H`, `CUSUM statistic`, `CUSUM P value`, `N`, `Valid slopes`, `K offset`) and `Residuals` tab with fitted values and perpendicular/vertical residuals. Slope $\hat{\beta}$ is the shifted median of valid non-$-1$ pairwise slopes $S_{ij} = (y_i - y_j)/(x_i - x_j)$ with rank offset $K = \text{count}(S_{ij} < -1)$, accompanied by exact rank-based CIs and Intercept $\hat{\alpha} = \text{median}(y_i - \hat{\beta} x_i)$.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Evaluates Passing & Bablok's Kolmogorov-type CUSUM linearity test ($H$, test statistic, $P$ value) and tests whether slope $95\%$ CI excludes $1$ (proportional bias) and intercept CI excludes $0$ (systematic bias), with `remediation: None`.
- **Edge cases & limits:** Requires $n \ge 3$ complete pairs; vertical identical-$x$ ties with $y_i \ne y_j$ are handled per Passing & Bablok (excluding exact $(x_i, y_i) = (x_j, y_j)$ identical ties and dropping $S_{ij} = -1$ symmetrically); raises `ZeroVariance` when zero valid pairwise slopes or vertical-only ties remain; rejects pre-summarized XY subcolumns.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Passing & Bablok (1983), verified bit-accurately against exact rank-order & CUSUM Python 3.13 / R references in `parity_g8_barnard_pb_mi.rs`.

---

## One-Way ANOVA & Nonparametric Equivalents {#analysis-one-way-anova}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Compares $k \ge 2$ treatment groups across independent columns (`OrdinaryAnova`, heteroscedastic `BrownForsytheAndWelch`, nonparametric `KruskalWallis`) or matched repeated-measures subject rows (`RepeatedMeasures`, mixed-effects REML, nonparametric `Friedman`), with FWER/FDR post-hoc comparisons, trend tests, and Compact Letter Displays (`CLD`). Compatible with `Column` and `MultipleVariables` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `one-way-anova`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-one-way-anova)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `one_way_anova` (canonical), `anova`, `welch_anova`, `brown_forsythe`, `rm_one_way_anova`, `repeated_measures_anova`, `kruskal_wallis`, `friedman`.
  - `method`: `ordinary_anova` (default), `brown_forsythe_and_welch`, `repeated_measures`, `kruskal_wallis`, `friedman`.
  - `geisser_greenhouse`: bool (applies to `repeated_measures`).
  - `mixed_effects_reml`: bool (default `false`; engages REML automatically when repeated-measures subjects have missing cells, or explicitly on complete tables).
  - `df_method`: `kenward_roger` (default) or `satterthwaite`.
  - `residual_covariance`: `compound_symmetry` (default) or `unstructured` (log-Cholesky Pinheiro–Bates REML covariance parameterization with documented fallbacks to compound symmetry when under-identified).
  - `compute_effect_sizes`: bool (reports $\eta^2, \omega^2$, Cohen's $f$ with exact noncentral-*F* CIs, or $\varepsilon^2$ / Kendall's $W$).
  - `multiplicity`, `threshold` (default `0.05`), `report_confidence_intervals`, `control_column`.
- **Reported values:**
  - `AnovaTable` (`anova-table`, `unequal-var-anova`, `rm-one-way-anova`, `kruskal-wallis`, `friedman`): Treatment/Residual/Total SS, df, MS, $F$ (or Welch $W$ / Brown–Forsythe $F^*$ / Kruskal–Wallis $H$ / Friedman $\chi^2_F$), and $P$ value.
  - `Diagnostics`: Bartlett and Brown–Forsythe median-Levene variance homogeneity tests (ordinary/unequal-var ANOVA); Mauchly $W$, Greenhouse–Geisser $\hat{\varepsilon}$, and Huynh–Feldt $\tilde{\varepsilon}$ sphericity (RM ANOVA).
  - `ParametersAndConfidenceIntervals` & `CovarianceMatrix`: REML random-effect / error variance components or estimated unstructured residual covariance matrix.
  - `MultipleComparisons`: Pairwise mean/rank differences, SEs, raw and adjusted $P$ or $q$-values, CIs (omitted for `NewmanKeuls` where simultaneous CIs are undefined), and Piepho (2004) CLD groupings (`Graphs` brackets & letter tokens).
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Tests group normality (Shapiro–Wilk per group), variance homogeneity (Bartlett / Brown–Forsythe), RM sphericity ($\hat{\varepsilon} < 0.75$ triggers `Warn`), REML boundary variance ($\hat{\sigma}^2_{\text{random}} = 0$ `Info` vs optimizer upper search bound `Warn`), and listwise missing-block exclusion counts in non-REML RM/Friedman; strictly `remediation: None`.
- **Edge cases & limits:** Supports [pre-summarized subcolumns](tables.md#subcolumn-modes) (`MeanSdN`, `MeanSemN`, `MeanCvN`) for `OrdinaryAnova` and `BrownForsytheAndWelch` (`ordinary_one_way_from_summary`), omitting Levene/normality checks that require raw replicates; REML handles unbalanced/incomplete subject blocks automatically unless `unstructured` covariance falls back cleanly on collinear/degenerate timepoints (`UnstructuredFallbackReason`). Nonparametric Friedman drops incomplete rows listwise with an audit note.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** NIST StRD ANOVA suite (`nist_strd.rs` >= 12+ LRE); Zar (2010); Welch (1951); Levene (1960) & Brown & Forsythe (1974a,b); Steiger (2004) noncentral-$F$ effect-size CIs; Mauchly (1940); Greenhouse & Geisser (1959); Huynh & Feldt (1976); Patterson & Thompson (1971); Pinheiro & Bates (1996); Kenward & Roger (1997); Fai & Cornelius (1996); Kruskal & Wallis (1952); Friedman (1937); Tukey (1949/1953) & Kramer (1956); Newman (1939) & Keuls (1952); Dunnett (1955, 1980); Games & Howell (1976); Tamhane (1979); Dunn (1964); Piepho (2004) CLD; verified against R 4.5.2 `stats` & `nlme` in `d1_reference_oracles.rs`, `d1_extended_stats_oracles.rs`, `r1011_cld_piepho_oracles.rs`, `r34_unstructured_reml_oracles.rs`, `r35_anova_reml_oracles.rs`, `r36_rm_reml_oracles.rs`.

---

## Two-Way, Three-Way & Multifactor ANOVA / REML {#analysis-factorial-anova}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Fits fixed-effects or repeated-measures factorial linear models and mixed-effects REML models (two-way row-by-column, three-way $2 \times 2 \times K$ in `Grouped` tables, and general $N$-way multifactor ANOVA on `MultipleVariables` sheets) with Type I or Type III marginal sums of squares, interactions, and simple-effects or main-effect post-hoc comparisons. Compatible with `Grouped` and `MultipleVariables` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `factorial-anova`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-factorial-anova)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `two_way_anova` (canonical), `factorial_anova`, or `three_way_anova`.
  - `three_way`: bool (default `false`; expects $4$ grouped dataset columns encoding $2 \times 2$ factors by $K$ row levels).
  - `multifactor_columns`, `response_column`: factor and outcome column indices on `MultipleVariables` sheets.
  - `max_interaction_order`: integer interaction cap (e.g., `2` or `3`).
  - `ss_type`: `type_iii` (default marginal SS for unbalanced designs) or `type_i` (sequential).
  - `repeated_measures`: `none` (default), `column_factor_matched`, `row_factor_matched`, `both_factors_matched`.
  - `mixed_effects_reml`: bool, `df_method` (`kenward_roger` default or `satterthwaite`), `residual_covariance` (`compound_symmetry` default or `unstructured`), `fit_reml_on_missing`: bool (default `true` in REML paths; errors with `InsufficientSampleSize` if missing RM cells exist and `fit_reml_on_missing: false` without unstructured/REML).
  - `compute_effect_sizes`, `multiplicity`, `threshold` (default `0.05`), `report_confidence_intervals`, `control_column`.
- **Reported values:** `AnovaTable` (`factorial-anova`) with main effects, interactions, subject/residual terms, SS, df, MS, $F$ (or scaled Kenward–Roger $F^*$), $P$, partial $\eta^2$ / $\omega^2$; `Diagnostics` (`rm-sphericity`) with Greenhouse–Geisser & Huynh–Feldt $\varepsilon$ on repeated-measures factors; `ParametersAndConfidenceIntervals` & `CovarianceMatrix` for REML variance components / unstructured covariance; `MultipleComparisons` for cell/simple-effect and main-effect comparisons (requiring explicit valid `control_column` when `Dunnett` is chosen).
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Evaluates residual/cell normality and variance checks, sphericity $\varepsilon$ thresholds, REML boundary/convergence diagnostics, dropped empty levels or incomplete RM cells (`remediation: None`).
- **Edge cases & limits:** Strictly rejects pre-summarized subcolumns (`StatsError::RequiresRawReplicates` on `Grouped` tables); compacts empty/fully-excluded factor levels cleanly before Type III effect coding; falls back from `Unstructured` to `CompoundSymmetry` REML when subject covariance is non-positive-definite or under-observed (recording `UnstructuredFallbackReason` in checklist & footnote); rejects missing cells when `fit_reml_on_missing` is false.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Searle (1987); Maxwell & Delaney (2004); Zar (2010); Lindstrom & Bates (1988); Pinheiro & Bates (1996); Kenward & Roger (1997); Fai & Cornelius (1996); verified against R 4.5.2 `aov`/`car`/`nlme` in `d1_reference_oracles.rs`, `d1_edge_matrix.rs`, `r34_unstructured_reml_oracles.rs`, `r35_anova_reml_oracles.rs`, `r36_rm_reml_oracles.rs`.

---

## Nested *t*-Test & Nested One-Way ANOVA {#analysis-nested-comparison}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Fits a hierarchical mixed-effects model separating fixed treatment-group effects from random subcluster (biological unit) variance and technical within-subcluster residual variance, preventing pseudoreplication on clustered experimental designs. Supports two-group nested *t*-test (`t = sqrt(F)` with signed difference) or $k \ge 3$ nested one-way ANOVA with hierarchical post-hoc comparisons. Exclusively compatible with `Nested` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `nested-comparison`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-nested-comparison)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `nested_anova` (canonical), `nested_t`, `nested`.
  - `two_group_t_test`: bool (default `false`; requires exactly $2$ selected treatment groups when `true`).
  - `df_method`: `kenward_roger` (default) or `satterthwaite`.
  - `multiplicity`, `threshold` (default `0.05`), `report_confidence_intervals`, `control_column` (applies when `!two_group_t_test && k >= 3`).
- **Reported values:**
  - `AnovaTable` (`nested-anova`): Among-groups, among-subclusters within groups, and technical residual SS, df (KR or Satterthwaite), MS, $F$ (or signed $t$ and CI difference in `nested_t`), and $P$ values.
  - `ParametersAndConfidenceIntervals` (`variance-components`): REML variance estimates ($\hat{\sigma}^2_{\text{subcluster}}, \hat{\sigma}^2_{\text{error}}$), SD, percentage of total variance, ICC ($\text{ICC}_{\text{subclusters}}$), plus both KR and Satterthwaite denominator df.
  - `MultipleComparisons`: Group-level comparisons using hierarchical group-mean variance $\hat{\sigma}_u^2 (n_{g1}^2 + \dots + n_{gm}^2) / N_g^2 + \hat{\sigma}_e^2 / N_g$.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Checklist evaluates biological-vs-technical clustering ICC (`Pass` when $\text{ICC} > 0.05$, `Info` otherwise) and REML boundary status (zero-boundary $\hat{\sigma}^2_{\text{subcluster}} = 0$ `Info` vs search-limit `Warn`), keeping `remediation: None`.
- **Edge cases & limits:** Unequal technical replicate counts per subcluster and unequal subclusters per treatment group are natively modeled via exact REML rather than unweighted pooling; non-numeric or excluded technical replicates are ignored cleanly.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Zar (2010); Satterthwaite (1946); Kenward & Roger (1997); verified in `d1_reference_oracles.rs`, `r35_anova_reml_oracles.rs`, and `r36_rm_reml_oracles.rs`.

---

## Contingency, Proportions, Odds/Risk Ratios & Agreement {#analysis-contingency}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Evaluates categorical count tables for independence, exact conditional/unconditional $2 \times 2$ association, trend across ordered proportions, paired discordance, inter-rater agreement, and one-sample or multinomial proportion goodness-of-fit. Table compatibility is method-dependent: `Contingency` accepts all methods; `PartsOfWhole` accepts `pearson_chi_square` and `exact_binomial`; `Column` accepts `exact_binomial` only (see [Analysis Registry: `contingency`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-contingency)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `contingency` (canonical), `chi_square`, `fisher_exact`, `barnard_exact`, `stats.barnard_exact`, `cohen_kappa`, `kappa`, `fleiss_kappa`, `exact_binomial`, `binomial`.
  - `method`: `pearson_chi_square` (with `yates_continuity` bool for $2 \times 2$), `likelihood_ratio_g2`, `fisher_exact` ($2 \times 2$ conditional exact + $R \times C$ Freeman–Halton network / deterministic Monte Carlo), `barnard_exact` ($2 \times 2$ unconditional CSM/Boschloo supremum over $\pi \in (0, 1)$), `cochran_armitage_trend` ($2 \times C$ or $R \times 2$), `mcnemar_paired` ($2 \times 2$), `cohen_kappa` (square $k \times k$, with `weighting`: `unweighted`, `linear`, `quadratic`), `fleiss_kappa` ($N$ subjects $\times k$ categories), `exact_binomial` (`null_proportion` $p_0 \in (0, 1)$, default `0.5`).
  - Additional flags: `compute_odds_and_risk_ratios` (Baptista–Pike exact OR CI, Koopman score RR CI, Newcombe Wilson-score RD CI, Altman NNT), `compute_sensitivity_specificity` (sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, LR+ with Wilson CIs), `compute_phi_and_cramers_v` (with exact noncentral-$\chi^2$ CIs), `expected_proportions` (custom non-negative weights for `PartsOfWhole` goodness-of-fit, normalized internally; uniform $1/k$ when `None`).
- **Reported values:** `MainSummary` (`contingency-main`, `parts-gof`), `ParametersAndConfidenceIntervals` (`contingency-ratios`, `contingency-mcnemar`, `kappa-agreement`, etc.), and `Diagnostics` tabs reporting test statistics ($\chi^2, G^2, z, \kappa, \phi, V$), exact/asymptotic *P* values, OR/RR/RD/NNT and diagnostic accuracy CIs, plus Clopper–Pearson, Wilson, and Agresti–Coull binomial intervals.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Flags Cochran's expected-cell rule (expected counts $< 5$ or $< 1$), warns on empty zero margins dropped prior to analysis (`Empty margin reduction`), checks $p_e = 1$ degenerate kappa cases (`ZeroVariance`), and reports sparse count notes with `remediation: None`.
- **Edge cases & limits:** All-zero margin rows/columns are trimmed before association tests (failing with `EmptyInput` or `InsufficientSampleSize` if the reduced table falls below $2 \times 2$); non-integer or negative counts fail table count validation; `CochranArmitageTrend` returns `None` statistics outside $2 \times C$ / $R \times 2$ or at zero variance; large sparse $R \times C$ Fisher exact sums use exact bounded enumeration / deterministic Monte Carlo cleanly.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Pearson (1900); Yates (1934); Wilks (1938); Fisher (1935); Freeman & Halton (1951); Barnard (1945/1947) & Suissa & Shuster (1985); Cochran (1954) & Armitage (1955); McNemar (1947); Baptista & Pike (1977); Koopman (1984); Newcombe (1998); Altman (1998); Clopper & Pearson (1934) & Sterne (1954); Wilson (1927); Agresti & Coull (1998); Cohen (1960, 1968); Fleiss (1971); Fleiss, Cohen & Everitt (1969); Fleiss, Nee & Landis (1979); verified in `d1_reference_oracles.rs`, `d1_extended_stats_oracles.rs` (`statsmodels 0.15.0` unweighted/linear/quadratic `cohens_kappa`), `parity_g8_barnard_pb_mi.rs`, and `wave21_r97_r912_clustering.rs`.

---

## Survival Analysis (Kaplan–Meier & Cox PH) {#analysis-survival}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Fits nonparametric Kaplan–Meier survival curves with cohort log-rank / Gehan–Breslow–Wilcoxon / trend comparisons and hazard ratios, or multivariable semi-parametric Cox Proportional Hazards regression $h(t | X) = h_0(t)\exp(X \beta)$ with Schoenfeld PH diagnostics. Compatible with `Survival` tables (`KaplanMeier`) and `MultipleVariables` tables (`KaplanMeier` via `mv_time_column`, `mv_status_column`, optional `mv_group_column`; `CoxProportionalHazards` via `time_column`, `status_column`, `predictor_columns`; see [Analysis Registry: `survival`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-survival)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `kaplan_meier` (canonical), `survival`, `log_rank`, `cox_ph`, or `cox`.
  - **Kaplan–Meier:** `log_rank_mantel_cox` (bool), `gehan_breslow_wilcoxon` (bool), `trend_test` (Tarone 1975 1-df trend when $\ge 3$ cohorts), `asymmetrical_greenwood_ci` (bool, default Kalbfleisch–Prentice $\ln(-\ln S(t))$ bounds guaranteed in $[0, 1]$ vs plain linear Greenwood), `multiplicity`, `threshold` (default `0.05`), `report_confidence_intervals`, `control_column`, `mv_time_column`, `mv_status_column`, `mv_group_column`.
  - **Cox PH:** `time_column`, `status_column`, `predictor_columns`, `reference_levels`, `tie_method` (`efron` default, `breslow`, `exact`).
- **Reported values:**
  - **Kaplan–Meier:** `MainSummary` (`km-summary`, median survival with Brookmeyer–Crowley 1982 CIs, subjects/events/censored), `NumberAtRisk`, `ModelComparison` (log-rank, Gehan–Breslow–Wilcoxon, trend $\chi^2, \text{df}, P$), `ParametersAndConfidenceIntervals` (Mantel–Haenszel and O/E log-rank hazard ratios with strict estimability checks), `MultipleComparisons` (`survival-pairwise` for $\ge 3$ cohorts), and `fitted_curves` step coordinates.
  - **Cox PH:** `ParametersAndConfidenceIntervals` (`cox-ph` with $\hat{\beta}_j$, $\text{SE}$, Wald $z, P$, hazard ratio $\exp(\hat{\beta}_j)$, Wald CI, plus likelihood-ratio omnibus $\chi^2$), `CovarianceMatrix`, `BaselineSurvival` ($H_0(t), S_0(t)$ at design means), `LogMinusLog` ($\ln(-\ln \hat{S}(t))$ diagnostics), Harrell's $C$-index, and Grambsch–Therneau Schoenfeld proportional-hazards tests.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Reports proportional-hazards Schoenfeld $P$ checks, monotone-likelihood separation / covariate collinearity warnings in Cox PH (suppressing unstable Wald SE/CI entries while preserving omnibus LR *P*), small-event warnings, and Harrell's $C$-index diagnostics (`remediation: None`).
- **Edge cases & limits:** Negative follow-up times or invalid censoring indicators fail validation; zero events in one or both arms make O/E hazard ratio SE ($\sqrt{1/E_A + 1/E_B}$) or Mantel–Haenszel HR non-estimable (`None`); Brookmeyer–Crowley median CI becomes open on the right when $S(t)$ never crosses $0.5$ or its upper bound; complete/partial monotone covariate separation in Cox PH sets `converged = false` cleanly rather than emitting diverging infinite estimates.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Kaplan & Meier (1958); Greenwood (1926); Kalbfleisch & Prentice (2002); Brookmeyer & Crowley (1982); Mantel (1966) & Mantel–Haenszel (1959); Greenland & Robins (1985); Peto & Peto (1972); Gehan (1965); Breslow (1970, 1974); Tarone (1975); Berry, Kitchin & Mock (1991); Cox (1972); Efron (1977); Schoenfeld (1982); Grambsch & Therneau (1994); Harrell et al. (1982); verified against R 4.5.2 `survival 3.8.3` in `d1_reference_oracles.rs`, `d1_poisson_cox_result_sheets.rs`, `d1_edge_matrix.rs`, `r35_survival_twogroup_oracles.rs`, and `r13_2_survival_group_exclusion.rs`.

---

## ROC Curve Analysis {#analysis-roc-curve}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Constructs empirical Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves comparing a negative control distribution against a positive case distribution, estimating trapezoidal AUC, standard error, confidence interval, *P* value vs AUC $= 0.5$, Youden's $J$ optimal threshold, and full cutoff sensitivity/specificity/PPV/NPV/LR+ tables. Compatible with `Column` and `MultipleVariables` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `roc-curve`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-roc-curve)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with canonical key/shorthand `roc`:
  - `ci_method`: `de_long` (default, DeLong et al. 1988 exact structural components) or `hanley_mc_neil` (Hanley & McNeil 1982 exponential approximation). Pairwise DeLong correlated and unpaired two-curve AUC comparisons are also supported in `curvebook-stats::roc`.
- **Reported values:**
  - `MainSummary` (`roc-summary`): AUC, SE, `conf%` AUC CI, *P* value testing $\text{AUC} = 0.5$, sample sizes ($n_{\text{controls}}, n_{\text{cases}}$), optimal cutoff, sensitivity, specificity, and maximum Youden's $J = \text{Sens} + \text{Spec} - 1$.
  - `CurveCoordinates` (`roc-coordinates`): Full threshold table (`Cutoff`, `Sensitivity`, `Specificity`, `1 - Specificity`, `Youden J`, `PPV`, `NPV`, `LR+`) plus `FittedCurveOverlay` points for plotting.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Flags $\text{AUC} < 0.5$ (`Warn` discrimination-direction check assuming higher values represent cases) and warns when $n_{\text{controls}} < 2$ or $n_{\text{cases}} < 2$ (single-subject group disables DeLong variance estimation and switches to Hanley–McNeil SE, Wilson score CI, and exact Mann–Whitney $U$ *P* value); `remediation: None`.
- **Edge cases & limits:** Correctly handles ties at every cutoff using midpoint rank aggregation; `LR+` leaves `None`/empty cell when $\text{Specificity} = 1$; requires at least one valid finite observation in both controls and cases.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** DeLong, DeLong & Clarke-Pearson (1988); Hanley & McNeil (1982); Youden (1950); verified against R 4.5.2 in `d1_reference_oracles.rs` and `audit_cat_roc_pow_fixes.rs`.

---

## Generalized Linear Models (Linear, Logistic, Poisson) {#analysis-generalized-linear-model}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Fits multivariable Generalized Linear Models across Gaussian identity (`linear`), Binomial logit (`logistic`), and Poisson log (`poisson`) exponential-dispersion families with dummy-encoded categorical predictors, optional VIF collinearity metrics, residual diagnostics, and goodness-of-fit statistics. Compatible with `MultipleVariables`, `Xy`, and `Column` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `generalized-linear-model`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-generalized-linear-model)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `glm` (canonical), `linear_glm`, `multiple_linear`, `logistic_glm`, `multiple_logistic`, `poisson_glm`, `multiple_poisson`.
  - `family`: `linear` (default), `logistic`, `poisson`.
  - `response_column`: 0-based dependent variable index.
  - `predictor_columns`: ordered list of covariate / categorical predictor indices.
  - `reference_levels`: list of `(categorical_col_idx, reference_level_label)` overrides for treatment dummy coding.
  - `compute_vif`: bool (default `true` on multivariable designs).
- **Reported values:**
  - **`linear`:** Coefficient estimates, SEs, *t*, *P*, `conf%` *t*-CIs, VIF, Type III partial SS/F/P; $R^2$, adjusted $R^2$, $S_{y.x}$, omnibus *F* and *P*, AIC, AICc, BIC, Durbin–Watson, studentized residuals, leverage, and Cook's distance (`MainSummary`, `ParametersAndConfidenceIntervals`, `Diagnostics`).
  - **`logistic`:** Log-odds $\hat{\beta}_j$, SE, Wald $z, P$, odds ratios $\exp(\hat{\beta}_j)$ with Wald CIs, likelihood-ratio $\chi^2, P$, McFadden / Nagelkerke / Tjur pseudo-$R^2$, AIC, AICc, Hosmer–Lemeshow $\chi^2$ & $P$, ROC AUC, and classification cutoff sweep table.
  - **`poisson`:** Log-rate $\hat{\beta}_j$, SE, Wald $z, P$, incidence rate ratios $\exp(\hat{\beta}_j)$ with Wald CIs (dispersion $= 1$), residual deviance, Pearson dispersion $\chi^2 / \text{df}$, LR $\chi^2, P$, McFadden pseudo-$R^2$, AIC, AICc, and deviance residuals.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Checks rank deficiency/aliased collinear columns via SVD, high multicollinearity (`VIF > 5` / `VIF > 10`), Gaussian residual normality (`Shapiro–Wilk` with `remediation: None`), Albert–Anderson (1984) complete or quasi-complete separation in `logistic` IRLS, Poisson overdispersion/convergence, and listwise complete-case row omissions.
- **Edge cases & limits:** Binary outcomes outside $\{0, 1\}$ fail in `logistic`; negative/non-count outcomes fail in `poisson`; categorical predictors reduced to $< 2$ levels after complete-case filtering raise `ZeroVariance`; requires $n \ge p + 1$ complete rows (at least $3$ rows on `Xy` tables); rejects pre-summarized subcolumns. In `logistic` separation, marks `separation_detected = true` cleanly without unbounded diverging iterations.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** NIST StRD Linear Least Squares (`nist_strd.rs`); Golub (1965) & Björck (1967) QR/SVD linear least squares; McCullagh & Nelder (1989); Albert & Anderson (1984); Hosmer & Lemeshow (1980); verified against R 4.5.2 `stats::lm` and `stats::glm` in `d1_reference_oracles.rs`, `d1_edge_matrix.rs`, and `d1_poisson_cox_result_sheets.rs`.

---

## Multivariate Analysis (PCA, PCR, Correlation, Clustering, MICE) {#analysis-multivariate}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Unifies multivariate exploratory, clustering, supervised principal-component regression, and multiple-imputation pipelines (`Pca`, `CorrelationMatrix`, `Clustering`, `MultipleImputation`). Compatible with `MultipleVariables`, `Xy`, and `Column` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `multivariate`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-multivariate)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `pca` (canonical), `principal_components`, `correlation`, `correlation_matrix`, `clustering`, `kmeans`, `multiple_imputation`, `stats.multiple_imputation`, `mice`.
  - **PCA / PCR:** `standardize` (bool, `true` = correlation PCA, `false` = covariance PCA), `parallel_analysis_seed` (optional Monte Carlo seed for Horn 1965 retention cutoffs), `pcr_outcome_column` (optional target outcome column triggering supervised Principal Component Regression).
  - **Correlation matrix:** `spearman_rank` (bool, `false` = Pearson $r$, `true` = Spearman $\rho$). Also provides standalone Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall $\tau_b$ utilities.
  - **Clustering:** `distance` (`euclidean`, `manhattan`, `cosine`, `pearson_correlation_dissimilarity`), `linkage` (`single`, `complete`, `average` UPGMA, `weighted` WPGMA, `centroid` UPGMC, `median` WPGMC, `ward_d2` Murtagh–Legendre Ward criterion), `k_means_k` (optional $k \ge 2$ partitioning via `k-means++` Arthur & Vassilvitskii 2007), `k_sweep_max` (optional candidate-$k$ WCSS & silhouette sweep).
  - **Multiple imputation:** `imputations_m` ($2..=50$), `max_iters` ($1..=100$), `seed`, `response_column`, `predictor_columns` (Chained Equations with Predictive Mean Matching `MICE PMM`, pooled via Rubin 1987 and Barnard–Rubin 1999 small-sample degrees of freedom).
- **Reported values:**
  - **PCA / PCR:** `MainSummary` (`pca-eigenvalues`, `pcr-summary` with $R^2$, adjusted $R^2$, *F*, RMSE, AIC/BIC), `ParametersAndConfidenceIntervals` (`pca-loadings`, `pcr-predictors` back-transformed to original predictor scale, `pcr-components`), scores/biplot contributions, and `Diagnostics` (`pcr-diagnostics` leverage & Cook's $D$).
  - **Correlation matrix:** Symmetric matrix tabs (`r`, unadjusted *P*, and Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted *q*-values across off-diagonal pairs) plus pairwise sample sizes $n_{ij}$.
  - **Clustering:** `MainSummary` / `ParametersAndConfidenceIntervals` (cluster centroids, assignments, WCSS, mean silhouette), `Diagnostics` (linkage merge schedule, cut silhouettes, cophenetic correlation $r$), and `CovarianceMatrix` (dense distance and cophenetic matrices emitted when $n \le \text{MAX\_CLUSTER\_MATRIX\_TAB\_N}$).
  - **Multiple Imputation:** Pooled variable means and optional pooled OLS regression coefficients, pooled SE, *t*, *P*, `conf%` Barnard–Rubin CIs, and Fraction of Missing Information (`FMI`).
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Flags dense distance-matrix omission for large $n$ (while retaining cophenetic $r$ and linkage tree), cluster separation quality (`silhouette >= 0.25`), Kaiser/parallel component retention, and imputation diagnostics (`remediation: None`).
- **Edge cases & limits:** Correlation matrix evaluates pairwise complete cases cleanly (reporting `NaN` when pairwise $n < 3$ or zero variance and excluding non-estimable pairs from the BH family); clustering, PCA, and MICE enforce complete/finite numerical handling and explicitly reject pre-summarized subcolumns.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Hotelling (1933) & Jolliffe (2002); Horn (1965); Pearson (1896); Fisher (1921); Spearman (1904); Kendall (1938, 1945); Lloyd (1982); Arthur & Vassilvitskii (2007); Rousseeuw (1987); Lance & Williams (1967); Ward (1963); Murtagh & Legendre (2014); Rubin (1987); Barnard & Rubin (1999); van Buuren & Groothuis-Oudshoorn (2011); verified in `d1_reference_oracles.rs`, `d1_edge_matrix.rs`, `parity_g8_barnard_pb_mi.rs`, and `wave21_r97_r912_clustering.rs`.

---

## Simple & Deming Linear Regression {#analysis-linear-regression}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Fits ordinary least-squares simple linear regression $Y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X$ (including ANCOVA homogeneity-of-slopes and intercept comparisons when $\ge 2$ datasets are selected) or Deming Model II orthogonal total least squares accounting for measurement error in both *X* and *Y*. Compatible with `Xy`, `Grouped`, and `MultipleVariables` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `linear-regression`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-linear-regression)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `fit.run` with shorthands `linear` (canonical), `simple_linear`, `linear_regression`, `deming`, or `deming_regression`.
  - `deming_model_ii`: bool (default `false`; uses fixed orthogonal variance ratio $\lambda = 1.0$ with leave-one-out jackknife SEs; custom $\lambda$ ratios are exposed via `curvebook_fit::deming_regression`).
  - `force_through_origin`: bool (default `false`; fixes $\beta_0 = 0, \text{df} = n - 1$).
  - `confidence_bands`, `prediction_bands`: bools enabling Working–Hotelling / Student-*t* confidence and prediction intervals.
  - `interpolate_unknowns`: bool enabling forward ($X$ to $Y$) prediction and exact Fieller inverse calibration ($Y$ to $X$, handling bounded `Finite`, split, or `AllReals` inverse sets).
  - `x_range_filter`: optional inclusive `[x_min, x_max]` predictor filter restricting points entering the fit (`plot_x_min`, `plot_x_max`, `plot_segments` default `100`, hard cap `10,000` control overlay evaluation independently).
- **Reported values:** `MainSummary` (Slope, Intercept, $1/\text{slope}$, $X$-intercept, SEs, `conf%` CIs, $R^2$, Pearson $r$, $S_{y.x}$, $\text{RSS}$, $F$, *P*, Wald–Wolfowitz runs test sorted along $X$, replicate lack-of-fit *F* test), `ModelComparison` (ANCOVA slope homogeneity and intercept/elevation comparisons across multiple datasets), `InterpolatedUnknowns` (`Interpolated X` / `Interpolated Y`), and curve bands.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Notes orthogonal Deming $\lambda = 1.0$ assumption, runs-test departure from linearity, replicate lack-of-fit, and range-filter exclusions (`remediation: None`).
- **Edge cases & limits:** Returns `InsufficientData` when $n \le 2$ (or $n < 1$ when `force_through_origin` with nonzero $X$ variance), rejects non-finite points or zero $X$ variance (all $X = 0$ when forced through origin), and rejects pre-summarized inputs where raw pairs are needed; if `slope == 0` or Deming jackknife variance collapses, $X$-intercept / $1/\text{slope}$ are omitted cleanly (`None`).
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Deming (1943); Linnet (1990) jackknife Deming SEs; Fieller (1954) inverse calibration; Zar (2010) ANCOVA slope/intercept comparison; verified against R 4.5.2 `stats::lm` in `r13_1_d1_oracles.rs`, `d1_nist_and_pharma_oracles.rs`, and `d1_edge_matrix.rs`.

---

## Nonlinear Regression & Custom Equations {#analysis-nonlinear-regression}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Fits built-in parametric models ([Parametric Equations Registry](registry/equations.html)) or sandboxed custom algebraic, piecewise `<A>`/`<B>`, implicit, and first-order ODE equations using trust-region Levenberg–Marquardt, Poisson deviance IRLS, outlier-resistant Cauchy regression, or ROUT outlier elimination, supporting global parameter sharing, hooks, profile-likelihood CIs, model comparison, and unknown interpolation. Compatible with `Xy`, `Grouped`, and `MultipleVariables` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `nonlinear-regression`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-nonlinear-regression); complete algorithmic details in [Curve Fitting Reference](fitting.md)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `fit.run` using shorthand `nonlinear` (canonical), aliases (`nonlinear_regression`, `curve_fit`, `fit`, `custom_equation`, `custom_dsl`), or any built-in equation ID directly as the `kind` shorthand (`log_agonist_vs_response_4pl`, `michaelis_menten`, etc.). Canonical parameter keys (`NonlinearFitSpec`):
  - Model: `equation_id`, `custom_dsl`.
  - Objective & weights: `method` (`least_squares` default, `poisson_deviance`, `robust_cauchy`, `rout_outlier_elimination`), `fdr_q_percent` (default `1.0`, bounded to $(0, 50]$), `weighting` (`none` default, `relative_square`, `relative`, `general_power_y` + `weighting_power`, `inverse_x`, `inverse_x2`, `observed_sd`).
  - Constraints & solver: `parameter_rules` (`scope`: `local`, `shared_global`, `constant`, `hooked_constant`, `per_dataset_constant`, `column_title_constant`, plus `initial_override`, `lower_bound`, `upper_bound`), `max_iters` (default `1000`, `HARD_MAX_ITERS = 50,000`), `x_range_filter`, `y_range_filter`, `plot_function_only`, `plot_x_min`, `plot_x_max`.
  - Uncertainty & diagnostics: `profile_likelihood_ci` (`true` default), `identify_unstable_parameters`, `flag_r_squared_below`, `confidence_bands`, `prediction_bands`, `interpolate_unknowns`, `replicates_lack_of_fit_test`, `normality_of_residuals`, `homoscedasticity_test`, `emit_residuals_tab`, `emit_covariance_tab`.
  - Model comparison: `comparison` (`extra_sum_of_squares_f`, `aicc`, `likelihood_ratio_test`), `alternative_equation_id`, `shared_parameter_comparison`.
- **Reported values:** `ParametersAndConfidenceIntervals` (best-fit estimates, SEs, Venzon–Moolgavkar profile or Wald CIs including `Open` endpoints, dependency $R^2_j$, Hougaard $|g_1|$, parameter notes, plus derived physiological scalars like `EC50`/`t_half`/`Span`), `MainSummary` ($N$, $K_{\text{free}}$, df, unweighted $R^2$ & `rss`, `weighted_ss`, $S_{y.x}$ or `RSDR`, $\text{AIC}_c$, $\text{BIC}$, runs test, replicates lack-of-fit, Shapiro–Wilk/Anderson–Darling/Lilliefors normality, Spearman homoscedasticity), `Residuals`, `CovarianceMatrix`, `ModelComparison`, `InterpolatedUnknowns` (`Interpolated Mean X` / `Interpolated Replicates` with `Extrapolated` flags), and `Diagnostics` (`fit_auc`). See [Curve Fitting Reference](fitting.md#uncertainty-and-diagnostics).
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Under `robust_cauchy`, omits parametric covariance/CIs/bands cleanly (`InferenceAvailability::NotApplicableInRobustMode`); flags `Ambiguous` / `Unstable` fits when Jacobian rank is deficient, `Dependency > 0.9999`, or profile bounds plateau; flags `Dependency > 0.99`, $|g_1| > 1.0$, and unweighted $R^2 < \text{flag\_r\_squared\_below}$ (`remediation: None`).
- **Edge cases & limits:** Honors exact replicate sufficient statistics on [pre-summarized XY subcolumns](tables.md#subcolumn-modes) (`MeanSdN`, `MeanSemN`, `MeanCvN`); enforces strict DSL/ODE compilation and step limits (`MAX_AST_NODES = 4,096`, `MAX_ODE_STEPS = 50,000`; see [Curve Fitting Reference: Caps](fitting.md#custom-dsl-and-ode)).
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** NIST StRD NLS (`nist_strd.rs`), `d1_nist_reparam_builtins.rs`, `d1_nist_and_pharma_oracles.rs`, `d1_non_nist_fitting.rs`, `d1_custom_equations.rs`, `d1_fit_uncertainty.rs`, `r45_robust_suppression.rs`, and `r13_1_d1_oracles.rs` ([Curve Fitting Reference: D1 Verification](fitting.md#oracle-verification)).

---

## Analyze a Stack of *P* Values {#analysis-p-value-stack}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Treats one or more numeric columns containing raw hypothesis-test *P* values $p \in [0.0, 1.0]$ as standalone testing families, returning multiplicity-adjusted *P* values (FWER) or Benjamini–Hochberg / Benjamini–Krieger–Yekutieli / Benjamini–Yekutieli *q*-values (FDR), ascending ranks, and discovery indicators strictly in original row order. Compatible with `Column`, `Xy`, `Grouped`, and `MultipleVariables` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `p-value-stack`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-p-value-stack)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.pvalueStack` using shorthands `pvalue_stack` (canonical), `stats.pvalue_stack`, `p_value_stack`, `pvalues`, `pvaluestack`, `stats.pvaluestack`:
  - `method` (`PValueStackMethod`): `benjamini_hochberg_fdr` (default), `bonferroni`, `holm_bonferroni`, `sidak`, `holm_sidak`, `benjamini_krieger_yekutieli_fdr`, `benjamini_yekutieli_fdr`.
  - `threshold`: strict decision threshold ($\alpha$ for FWER, target FDR $Q$ for FDR) in $(0.0, 1.0)$ (default `0.05`).
  - `column`: optional single 0-based column index override when not using `selected_data_sets`.
- **Reported values:**
  - `MainSummary` (`pvalue-stack-summary`): Method, error-rate family (`FWER` vs `FDR`), threshold, valid hypothesis count $m$, discoveries, non-discoveries, discovery fraction, skipped blank/excluded cells, minimum raw *P*, and minimum adjusted *P*/*q*, plus scalars (`InputCount`, `Discoveries`, `MinRawP`, `MinAdjustedP`, `Threshold`, `TotalInputCount`, `TotalDiscoveries`).
  - `MultipleComparisons` (`pvalue-stack-adjusted`): Original row label, 1-based row index, competition rank, raw *P*, adjusted *P* or FDR *q*, and boolean `Discovery?`.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Documents whether the selected procedure controls FWER or FDR under independence (`Sidak`/`HolmSidak`/`BH`/`BKY`) vs arbitrary dependence (`Bonferroni`/`HolmBonferroni`/`BY`), plus non-numeric text-cell ignores (`remediation: None`).
- **Edge cases & limits:** Rejects raw values outside $[0.0, 1.0]$ or non-finite values with `InvalidParameter` (while skipping blank/excluded cells cleanly), requires threshold strictly in $(0.0, 1.0)$, and rejects pre-summarized subcolumns (`RequiresRawReplicates`) since summary spreads are not independent *P* values. Handles ties accurately in both rank reporting and monotonicity enforcement.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Bonferroni (1936) & Dunn (1961); Holm (1979); Šídák (1967); Holland & Copenhaver (1987); Benjamini & Hochberg (1995); Benjamini & Yekutieli (2001); Benjamini, Krieger & Yekutieli (2006); verified to `TOL = 1e-12` against R 4.5.2 `p.adjust` and closed-form BKY oracles in `r1010_pvalue_stack_oracles.rs`, and against `statsmodels 0.15.0` `multipletests(method="fdr_tsbky")` in `d1_extended_stats_oracles.rs`.

---

## Statistical Power & Sample Size {#analysis-power-analysis}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Computes prospective or post-hoc statistical sample sizes ($n_1, n_2, N$), achievable power ($1 - \beta$), minimum detectable effect size, sensitivity parameter grids, and power-vs-$N$ curves across independent, paired, one-sample, one-way ANOVA, two-proportion, Pearson correlation, goodness-of-fit $\chi^2$, and simple linear regression designs. Accepts any [`TableKind`](tables.md#table-archetypes) and optionally hooks scalar parameters from an `InfoSheet` (see [Analysis Registry: `power-analysis`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-power-analysis)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `power` (canonical), `power_analysis`, `stats.power`, `power_sample_size`:
  - `family` (`PowerTestFamily`): `two_sample_unpaired_t` (default), `two_sample_paired_t`, `one_sample_t`, `one_way_anova`, `two_proportions`, `correlation`, `chi_square`, `simple_linear_regression`.
  - `solve_target` (`PowerSolveTarget`): `sample_size`, `power`, `detectable_effect`.
  - `tail_mode`: `two_sided`, `one_sided_greater`, `one_sided_less` (one-sided directional alternatives are disallowed on inherently non-directional `one_way_anova` and `chi_square`).
  - `alpha` in $(0, 1)$ (default `0.05`); `target_power` in $(0, 1)$ (required for `sample_size` / `detectable_effect`); `sample_size`, optional `sample_size_group2`, and `allocation_ratio` ($k = n_2 / n_1 > 0$).
  - `effect` (`PowerEffectSpec`, supporting standardized `d`, `d_z`, `f`, `h`, `w`, `r`, `r_squared`, `f_squared` or raw means + SD, proportions $p_1, p_2$, or regression slope + $\sigma_x, \sigma_\varepsilon$), `num_groups` ($\ge 2$ for `one_way_anova`), `chi_square_df`, `two_proportions_mode` (`pooled_null_unpooled_alt` Fleiss/G*Power, `unpooled` Wald, `cohens_h` arcsine + `continuity_correction`), `correlation_method` (`fisher_z`, `pwr_hybrid`, `exact_conditional_t`), and optional `info_sheet_id`.
- **Reported values:**
  - `MainSummary` (`power-summary`): Family, solve target, tail mode, $\alpha$, target power, standardized and raw effect sizes, discrete integer $n_1, n_2, N_{\text{total}}$, `achieved_power` at discrete integer $N$, exact `continuous_n` and `power_at_continuous_n`, denominator $\text{df}$, critical threshold, noncentrality parameter $\lambda$, and implied metrics (`p2`, Cohen's $h$, $R^2$).
  - `MultipleComparisons` (`power-sensitivity`): Multi-scenario $(\alpha, 1 - \beta, \text{effect})$ sensitivity grid.
  - `CurveCoordinates` (`power-curve`): Sample-size vs achieved power curve plus `FittedCurveOverlay` and `analyzable_data_sheet`.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Checklist notes discrete rounding uplift between `continuous_n` and integer `n_per_group`, asymptotic vs exact distribution scope (e.g., normal approximation for two proportions vs exact noncentral-$t$/$F$), and invalid effect boundaries (`remediation: None`).
- **Edge cases & limits:** Powered by tail-safe noncentral-$t$, noncentral-$F$, and noncentral-$\chi^2$ distributions and Brent–Dekker root finding (`curvebook_math`); zero standardized effect sizes or $p_1 = p_2$ with `TwoProportions` raise `ZeroVariance` when solving for sample size; `R^2` must lie in $[0, 1)$ and `two_proportions` probabilities in $[0, 1]$ (`InvalidParameter`).
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Cohen (1988); Owen (1965) noncentral-$t$; Fleiss, Tytun & Ury (1980) & Fleiss, Levin & Paik (2003); Chow, Shao & Wang (2008); Fisher (1921); verified against R 4.5.2 `pwr` package benchmarks and noncentral distributions in `power_oracle.rs` and `r35_power_multiplicity_oracles.rs`.

---

## Simple Logistic Regression {#analysis-simple-logistic-regression}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Fits standalone single-predictor binary logistic regression $\ln\!\left(\frac{P(Y=1 \mid X)}{1 - P(Y=1 \mid X)}\right) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X$ directly on single-subcolumn `Xy` tables where $Y_i \in \{0, 1\}$, rejecting non-binary $Y$ values and multi-subcolumn tables with structured errors (see [Analysis Registry: `simple-logistic-regression`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-simple-logistic-regression)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `simple_logistic` (canonical), `simple_logistic_regression`, `stats.simple_logistic`, or `xy_logistic`:
  - `emit_row_classification`: bool (default `true`; emits the `Row Classification` tab with observed $(X_i, Y_i)$, predicted $\hat{P}(X_i)$ with CIs, and automatic out-of-sample predictions for appended $(X_{\text{new}}, \text{blank } Y)$ rows).
  - `confidence_bands`: bool (default `true`; samples two-sided inverse-logit confidence bands along the sigmoid probability curve overlay).
  - `classification_cutoff`: probability threshold in $(0, 1)$ (default `0.5`).
  - `plot_x_min`, `plot_x_max`, `plot_segments` (default `100`, max `10,000`): optional sigmoid probability curve evaluation bounds and resolution.
- **Reported values:**
  - `ParametersAndConfidenceIntervals` (`parameter-estimates`): $\hat{\beta}_0$, $\hat{\beta}_1$, odds ratios $e^{\hat{\beta}_0}, e^{\hat{\beta}_1}$, and $X_{50} = -\hat{\beta}_0 / \hat{\beta}_1$ with asymptotic Fisher-information SEs, asymmetrical profile-likelihood CIs (including propagated odds-ratio and $X_{50}$ profile intervals), and Wald $Z$-tests.
  - `MainSummary` (`goodness-of-fit`): $N$, events/non-events, separation status, null/model deviances ($D_0, D_1$), likelihood-ratio test ($G^2 = D_0 - D_1 \sim \chi^2_1$), $\text{AIC}$, $\text{AIC}_c$, $\text{BIC}$, Tjur's $R^2$, Cox–Snell $R^2$, Nagelkerke $R^2$, McFadden $R^2$, empirical DeLong ROC AUC with SE/CI, and classification accuracy/sensitivity/specificity.
  - `CurveCoordinates` (`roc-curve`): empirical ROC curve thresholds, sensitivity, specificity, and Youden's $J$.
  - `InterpolatedUnknowns` (`row-classification`, optional): observed rows and automatically predicted `(X_new, blank Y)` rows with predicted probabilities and CIs, plus a `FittedCurveOverlay` sigmoid curve for `XY` graphs.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Explicitly detects and reports collinearity (constant $X$), perfect (complete) separation, and quasi-perfect separation in plain language (Albert & Anderson 1984; Heinze & Schemper 2002) with `ChecklistStatus::Violated` rather than reporting diverging parameter estimates; warns when minority event count $< 10$.
- **Edge cases & limits:** Rejects non-binary $Y \notin \{0, 1\}$, all-zero/all-one outcomes, non-finite inputs, $N < 3$, non-`Xy` tables, and multi-subcolumn `Xy` tables; returns open/unbounded profile CIs for $X_{50}$ whenever $G^2 \le \chi^2_{1, 1-\alpha}$.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Hosmer, Lemeshow & Sturdivant (2013); McCullagh & Nelder (1989); Tjur (2009); Albert & Anderson (1984); Heinze & Schemper (2002); Venzon & Moolgavkar (1988); DeLong, DeLong & Clarke-Pearson (1988); verified against R 4.5.2 `stats::glm(..., family = binomial)` and `confint` in `d1_r18_6_simple_logistic.rs`.
## Fit Spline / LOWESS Curve {#analysis-fit-spline-lowess}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Model-free XY curve fitting generating smooth `FittedCurveOverlay` polylines, optional sampled `(X, Y)` coordinate tables, and nonparametric standard-curve unknown interpolation (`Y` from `X` and `X` from `Y`) without assuming a parametric equation. Compatible exclusively with `Xy` tables (see [Analysis Registry: `fit-spline-lowess`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-fit-spline-lowess)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analysis.run`](../commands.md) or `transform.run` with shorthands `fit_spline_lowess` (canonical), `spline_lowess`, `spline`, `cubic_spline`, `natural_cubic_spline`, `akima`, `akima_subspline`, `smoothing_spline`, `lowess`, `point_to_point`, `fit.spline_lowess`:
  - `method` (`SplineLowessMethod`): `NaturalCubicSpline` (default), `AkimaSubspline`, `SmoothingSpline`, `Lowess`, `PointToPoint`.
  - `segment_count`: number of sampled polyline vertices in `[2, 10000]` (default `200`; LOWESS automatically enforces `>= 4 * N`).
  - `smoothing_knots` / `smoothing_df`: knot count (`>= 2`) or explicit effective degrees of freedom ($\text{df} = \text{tr}(S_\lambda) \in [2, G]$) for Reinsch penalized cubic smoothing splines.
  - `lowess_preset` (`Coarse` = `0.75`, `Medium` = `0.50` default, `Fine` = `0.25`), optional `lowess_fraction` override in `(0, 1]`, and `lowess_robustness_iters` (default `3`, max `20`).
  - `plot_x_min`, `plot_x_max`: optional explicit curve evaluation domain overriding observed `[X_min, X_max]`.
  - `emit_curve_coordinates_tab` (`bool`, default `false`): emits a `CurveCoordinates` tab containing the sampled `(X, Y)` vertices.
  - `interpolate_unknowns` (`bool`, default `false`): evaluates $S(x_{\text{unk}})$ for `(X, blank Y)` rows and solves $S(x) = y_{\text{unk}}$ across curve segments for `(blank X, Y)` rows.
- **Reported values:**
  - `MainSummary` (`summary`): Method, active observations $N$, distinct $X$ knots $G$, polyline vertex count, domain bounds, RSS, RMSE, plus effective $\text{df}$ and $\lambda$ (for Smoothing Spline) or span $f$ and robustness passes (for LOWESS), plus hookable scalars (`n_points`, `distinct_x`, `segments`, `rss`, `rmse`, `effective_df`, `smoothing_lambda`, `lowess_span`).
  - `CurveCoordinates` (`curve-coordinates`, optional): sampled `(X, Y)` curve vertices per fitted dataset.
  - `InterpolatedUnknowns` (`interpolated-unknowns`, optional): forward `Y from X` and inverse `X from Y` standard-curve interpolations with multi-crossing reporting for non-monotonic curves.
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Emits a `Warn` checklist diagnostic when `Lowess` is run on $N < 20$ active observations (recommending Natural Cubic Spline, Akima Subspline, or Smoothing Spline for small samples).
- **Edge cases & limits:** Collapses replicate/tied $X$ rows to `(x_g, mean y_g)` for spline/Akima/point-to-point and multiplicity-weighted means for Reinsch smoothing splines; rejects non-finite inputs, `< 2` distinct $X$ values, out-of-range spans/degrees of freedom, and non-`Xy` tables.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** de Boor (1978); Akima (1970); Reinsch (1967); Hutchinson & de Hoog (1985); Cleveland (1979); Brent (1973); verified against R `4.5.2` (`stats::splinefun(..., method="natural")`, `stats::smooth.spline`, `stats::lowess`) and analytical Akima step-overshoot oracles in `crates/transform/tests/d1_r18_7_spline_lowess.rs`.

---

## Levene / Brown–Forsythe Variance Test {#analysis-levene-test}

- **Purpose & compatible tables:** Standalone test of the null hypothesis that the selected columns (groups) have equal population variances. Each selected column of a raw-replicate `Column` table (or each selected numeric variable of a `MultipleVariables` table) is one group; pre-summarized `Column` subcolumns are rejected because absolute deviations need individual replicates (see [Analysis Registry: `levene-test`](registry/tables.html#analysis-kind-levene-test)).
- **Engine command & canonical options/defaults:** Run via [`analysis.run`](../commands.md) or `stats.run` with shorthands `levene` (canonical), `levene_test`, `stats.levene`, `levene_median`, `brown_forsythe_variance`, `brown_forsythe_levene`, `variance_homogeneity`, `equal_variance_test` (all median-centered), or `levene_mean` (mean-centered):
  - `center` (`LeveneCenter`): `median` (default; Brown–Forsythe) or `mean` (Levene's original test).
  - `selected_data_sets`: the columns to compare (empty means every column; on `MultipleVariables` tables, every numeric variable).
- **Reported values:**
  - `MainSummary` (`levene-summary`): method, centre, number of groups $k$, total $N$, $F$, $\text{DFn} = k - 1$, $\text{DFd} = N - k$, *P* value, and the decision at the analysis alpha.
  - `DescriptiveSummary` (`levene-groups`): per-group $n$, centre (median or mean), mean absolute deviation, and SD.
  - Scalars: `F`, `DFn`, `DFd`, `P value`, `Groups`, `Total N`, and per-group `N`, `Center`, `Mean abs deviation` (keyed by column index).
- **Assumptions & QOL-7 diagnostics:** Checklist reports the decision (variances differ vs. equal variances not rejected), warns when any group has fewer than five values, notes that mean-centered deviations are sensitive to skewed data, and lists excluded and ignored text or non-finite cells.
- **Edge cases & limits:** Fewer than two groups or any group with $n < 2$ returns `InsufficientSampleSize`; zero within-group spread of the absolute deviations (for example constant groups, or every group of size two) returns `ZeroVariance` instead of an undefined $F$; non-`Column`/`MultipleVariables` tables return `IncompatibleTable`; blank, excluded, text, and non-finite cells are not observations.
- **Published D1 references & oracle verification:** Levene (1960); Brown & Forsythe (1974); Zar (2010, ch. 10); verified through `Session::execute` in `crates/engine/tests/r19_2_levene_engine.rs` against `scipy.stats.levene` (SciPy 1.18.1) and R 4.5.2 `anova(lm(|x - c| ~ g))` reference values, matching the stats-level oracles in `d1_extended_stats_oracles.rs`.

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/fitting.html

# Curve Fitting & Nonlinear Regression Reference

This reference documents CurveBook's parametric linear and nonlinear regression algorithms, residual weighting schemes, global parameter sharing and constant constraints, profile-likelihood uncertainty, R13.1 diagnostic safeguards, model comparison, unknown interpolation, custom equation DSL, and adaptive ODE solver. For the full compiled catalog of built-in equations, parameters, and solver defaults, see the [Parametric Equations Registry](registry/equations.html). For sheet-level analysis execution and table compatibility, see [Statistical Analyses (`#analysis-nonlinear-regression`)](analyses.md#analysis-nonlinear-regression), [Linear Regression (`#analysis-linear-regression`)](analyses.md#analysis-linear-regression), [Simple Logistic Regression (`#analysis-simple-logistic-regression`)](analyses.md#analysis-simple-logistic-regression), and the [Command Reference](../commands.md).

## Fitting Methods & Estimation Objectives {#fitting-methods}

Nonlinear regression fits a parametric model $y = f(x; \theta) + \varepsilon$ over active (non-excluded) observations via [`analyze.run`](../commands.md), `fit.run`, or `analysis.add` (`nonlinear` / `AnalysisKind::NonlinearRegression`). Observations may come from raw replicates or [pre-summarized XY subcolumns](tables.md#subcolumn-modes) (`MeanSdN`, `MeanSemN`, `MeanCvN`), and can be filtered by predictor interval using `x_range_filter`.

> [!NOTE]
> Under weighted least squares, `PoissonDeviance`, or replicate-moment weighting, `weighted_ss` is the objective minimized by the optimizer, while reported `rss` and unweighted $R^2 = 1 - \text{rss} / \text{TSS}$ remain expressed in original response $Y$ units (Motulsky & Christopoulos 2004).

### 1. Least Squares (`method: "least_squares"`)

Minimizes the weighted sum of squared residuals:

$$SS_w(\theta) = w_1 (y_1 - \hat{y}_1)^2 + w_2 (y_2 - \hat{y}_2)^2 + ... + w_N (y_N - \hat{y}_N)^2$$

- **Core optimizer:** Trust-region Levenberg–Marquardt (Levenberg 1944; Marquardt 1963; Moré 1978 / MINPACK-1 `lmder`) using column-scaled QR decomposition on the augmented Jacobian $[J; \sqrt{\lambda} D]$, quadratic trust-region step updates ($\rho \ge 10^{-4}$ acceptance, contraction in $[0.1, 0.5]$, expansion up to $\text{max}(\delta, 2 |D p|)$), and active-face projection onto box constraints.
- **Tolerances & budgets:** Relative residual reduction `ftol = 1e-15`, parameter step `xtol = 1e-14`, projected gradient cosine `gtol = 1e-13` (and stall check `stall_gtol = 1e-4`), default `max_iters = 1000` (`HARD_MAX_ITERS = 50000`).
- **Warm start & rescue:** Before or during difficult starts, when `use_simplex_warm_start` is active (default `true`), bounded Nelder–Mead simplex optimization (Nelder & Mead 1965; Lagarias et al. 1998) locates an initial basin or rescues non-finite / stalled starts.
- **Jacobians:** Built-in models supply analytical derivatives $df / d\theta_j$ where available; models without analytical gradients (including all custom DSL equations) use central finite differences $h = 10^{-6} \cdot \text{max}(|\theta_j|, 1)$, switching to interior one-sided differences $h = 1.5 \times 10^{-8} \cdot \text{max}(|\theta_j|, 1)$ at an active bound (Nocedal & Wright 2006).

### 2. Poisson Deviance (`method: "poisson_deviance"`)

For non-negative integer or count data $y_i \ge 0$ with strictly positive predicted mean $\hat{\mu}_i = f(x_i; \theta) > 0$, minimizes exact Poisson log-likelihood deviance (McCullagh & Nelder 1989):

$$D(\theta) = 2 \cdot [ y_1 \ln(y_1 / \hat{\mu}_1) - (y_1 - \hat{\mu}_1) ] + ... + 2 \cdot [ y_N \ln(y_N / \hat{\mu}_N) - (y_N - \hat{\mu}_N) ]$$

where terms with $y_i = 0$ contribute $2 \hat{\mu}_i$ smoothly via `deviance_bd0`.

- **Solver:** Iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS; Green 1984) assigning working weights $1 / \hat{\mu}_i$ around inner trust-region Levenberg–Marquardt updates until relative deviance change drops below $10^{-10}$.
- **Domain guards:** Negative observed counts ($y_i < 0$) raise `FitError::ImpossibleWeights`, and custom Gaussian `weighting` choices are ignored in favor of exact Poisson variance $V(\mu) = \mu$.
- **Inference:** Dispersion is fixed at $\phi = 1$, using asymptotic Fisher information covariance, normal two-sided $z$ quantiles for curve bands, and exact Poisson log-likelihood $\text{AIC}_c$ and $\text{BIC}$.

### 3. Robust Cauchy Regression (`method: "robust_cauchy"`)

Outlier-resistant Lorentzian M-estimator minimizing the logarithmic loss (Motulsky & Brown 2006):

$$L(\theta) = \ln(1 + (r_1 / \text{RSDR})^2) + ... + \ln(1 + (r_N / \text{RSDR})^2)$$

solved by Cauchy IRLS around the Robust Standard Deviation of Residuals (`RSDR`), defined from the $68.27\text{th}$ percentile of weighted residual magnitudes scaled by $\sqrt{N / (N - K_{\text{free}})}$. Points remain in the dataset without binary deletion.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Under `robust_cauchy`, parametric standard errors, confidence intervals, parameter dependency, Hougaard skewness, residual SD ($S_{y.x}$), $\text{AIC}_c$, $\text{BIC}$, studentized residuals, replicate lack-of-fit tests, and confidence/prediction bands are **intentionally suppressed** (`InferenceAvailability::NotApplicableInRobustMode` — empty cells / `Open` CIs), because standard Gaussian linearization covariance is invalid under non-quadratic Cauchy loss. Best-fit parameters, unweighted $R^2$, and `RSDR` remain reported. Use `rout_outlier_elimination` when parametric inference on clean inliers is required.

### 4. ROUT Outlier Elimination (`method: "rout_outlier_elimination"`)

Implements the three-stage ROUT procedure of Motulsky & Brown (2006):

1. **Robust Cauchy fit:** Fit the model with `robust_cauchy` to locate a resistant baseline and compute `RSDR` on base-weighted residuals $r_{w,i} = \sqrt{w_i} (y_i - \hat{y}_i)$, ensuring heteroscedastic weighting schemes (such as `relative_square` $1/Y^2$) map residuals onto a uniform scale before testing.
2. **FDR screening over extreme tail:** Evaluate two-sided Student-$t$ $P$ values against `RSDR` ($t_i = |r_{w,i}| / \text{RSDR}$) and apply Benjamini–Hochberg (1995) step-up FDR control **only** across the top $30\%$ of observations furthest from the curve (`start = floor(0.70 * N)`). The remaining lower $\approx 70\%$ of residuals are never tested (`q_value = 1.0`, `is_outlier = false`).
3. **Least-squares refit:** Re-optimize retained non-outlier points using ordinary or weighted least squares, seeded from the robust Cauchy parameters.

- **Parameter constraint:** `fdr_q_percent` is specified in percentage points (default `1.0` for $Q = 1\%$) and must satisfy $0 < Q \le 50$ in nonlinear regression (compare [univariate column outlier detection](analyses.md#analysis-outlier-detection), which allows $(0, 100]$).
- **Empty/insufficient inliers:** If ROUT excludes too many points to retain residual degrees of freedom, the solver returns `FitError::InsufficientData` or surfaces a non-converged warning; excluded outlier coordinates and $q$-values are tabulated in the diagnostics sheet without mutating the source [`DataSheet`](concepts.md#cell-exclusions).

### Optimizer Status Outcomes (`FitStatus`)

| Status | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Converged` | Gradient, step, or objective criteria satisfied with identifiable full-rank Jacobian |
| `Ambiguous` | Converged objective but rank-deficient Jacobian, collinearity `Dependency > 0.9999`, or unbounded identifiability plateau |
| `HitMaxIters` | Iteration cap reached before strict stopping tolerance |
| `Stalled` | Trust-region radius or projected step cannot achieve further reduction (`stall_gtol`) |
| `Diverged` | Objective failed to remain finite or exceeded numerical limits |

## Weighting Schemes & Replicate Summary Moments {#weighting-and-moments}

The `weighting` field (`WeightingScheme`) scales residual errors prior to least-squares and Cauchy/ROUT fitting (ignored by `poisson_deviance`; explicit cell-level weights, when attached, take precedence over the global scheme). See also [Parametric Equations Registry: Weighting Schemes](registry/equations.html#weighting-schemes).

| Canonical Key | Formula | Typical Error Model & Guard |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `none` | $w_i = 1$ | Homoscedastic uniform absolute SD across $Y$ |
| `relative_square` | $w_i = 1 / Y_i^2$ | Constant relative `%CV` scatter; undefined if any $Y_i = 0$ |
| `relative` | $w_i = 1 / |Y_i|$ | Poisson-like variance proportional to mean response; undefined if any $Y_i = 0$ |
| `general_power_y` | $w_i = 1 / |Y_i|^k$ | Power variance via finite `weighting_power` ($k$); undefined if $Y_i = 0$ when $k > 0$ |
| `inverse_x` | $w_i = 1 / |X_i|$ | Scatter proportional to $\sqrt{|X|}$; undefined if any $X_i = 0$ |
| `inverse_x2` | $w_i = 1 / X_i^2$ | Relative predictor-magnitude scatter; undefined if any $X_i = 0$ |
| `observed_sd` | $w_i = 1 / \text{SD}_i^2$ | Pre-summarized empirical variance; requires $\text{SD}_i > 0$ at every active row |

Any non-finite, zero-denominator, or overflowing weight produces `FitError::ImpossibleWeights`.

### Replicate Summary Subcolumns (`MeanSdN`, `MeanSemN`, `MeanCvN`)

When the source XY table uses a [pre-summarized subcolumn mode](tables.md#subcolumn-modes) (`MeanSdN`, `MeanSemN`, `MeanCvN`) and `weighting` is `none` (or on pre-summarized inputs without explicit weights and not using `observed_sd`), the solver reconstructs exact replicate-sufficient statistics from `(mean_i, sd_i, n_i)`:

- Each row's weighted residual scales by $\sqrt{w_i \cdot n_i}$.
- Total sample size sums $N = n_1 + ... + n_M$.
- Pooled within-row replicate variance contributes $w_i (n_i - 1) \text{SD}_i^2$ into total `weighted_ss` and unweighted `rss`, matching an equivalent raw-replicate fit identically for least-squares estimates, parameter SEs, $\text{AIC}_c$, and replicate lack-of-fit tests (Motulsky & Christopoulos 2004).

Under `observed_sd`, each pre-summarized row contributes one summary point weighted by $1 / \text{SD}_i^2$ (requiring finite $\text{SD}_i > 0$).

## Parameter Scopes, Bounds & Dynamic Hooks {#parameter-scopes}

Each entry in `parameter_rules` (`ParameterRule`) targets a case-insensitive model parameter `name` (`ParametricModel::param_names`) and controls initial guess, box constraints, sharing across datasets, or constant fixation (`ParameterScope`).

| Canonical `scope` | Behavior & Free Parameters Consumed |
| :--- | :--- |
| `local` | Default; fits an independent parameter value separately for each active dataset |
| `shared_global` | Pools all selected datasets to optimize a single shared parameter (`is_shared = true`) |
| `constant` | Fixes the parameter to a finite scalar `value` across all datasets ($0$ free parameters) |
| `hooked_constant` | Resolves a finite scalar from an upstream `InfoSheet` constant (`info_constant`) or up-to-date `ResultSheet` scalar (`result_scalar`); fails cleanly if missing, non-finite, or `Dirty` |
| `per_dataset_constant` | Supplies dataset-indexed `(data_set_index, value)` fixed constants (`per_dataset_constants`); datasets omitted from the list remain free `local` parameters |
| `column_title_constant` | Parses a finite numeric constant from each dataset column header (supports scientific notation and unit suffixes such as `M`, `mM`, `uM`, `nM`, `pM`, `fM`, `%`, `s`, `ms`, `min`, `h`, `Hz`, `deg`; fails if unparseable) |

- **Initial guesses (`initial_override`) & bounds (`lower_bound`, `upper_bound`):** When `initial_override` is omitted, deterministic model heuristics compute dataset-aware initial guesses (or pooled guesses for `shared_global`). Box bounds must be finite with $\text{lower} \le \text{upper}$ and are intersected with intrinsic domain bounds (e.g., positive rate constants). Setting $\text{lower} = \text{upper}$ converts a free slot into a fixed constant consuming $0$ free parameters.
- **Default model rules:** Certain models supply `default_parameter_rules` when no user rule overrides them—for example, centered polynomials fix `XCenter` to the active predictor sample mean $\bar{x}$ to preserve Jacobian conditioning.

## Parameter Uncertainty, Diagnostics & R13.1 Safeguards {#uncertainty-and-diagnostics}

### Profile-Likelihood & Wald Confidence Intervals

- **Wald asymptotic covariance:** $\text{Cov}(\hat{\theta}) = s_w^2 (J^T J)^{-1}$ where $s_w^2 = SS_w / \text{df}$ ($\text{df} = N - K_{\text{free}}$) for least squares, or $\text{Cov}(\hat{\theta}) = (J^T W J)^{-1}$ ($W = \text{diag}(\hat{\mu}_i)$) for Poisson deviance. Symmetric Wald intervals use Student $t_{\text{df}, \alpha/2}$ (least squares) or normal $z_{\alpha/2}$ (Poisson).
- **Venzon–Moolgavkar (1988) profile-likelihood intervals (`profile_likelihood_ci: true`, default):** For each free parameter $\theta_j$, nuisance parameters $\theta_{-j}$ are re-optimized via reduced trust-region LM (`run_reduced_lm_with_domain`, tolerance `ftol = 1e-12`, `xtol = 1e-12`) across an outward bracket scan refined by Brent root finding (`rel_tol = 1e-7`) to solve:

$$SS_{\text{prof}}(\theta_j) = SS_{\text{min}} \cdot (1 + \frac{1}{\text{df}} F_{1 - \alpha}(1, \text{df}))$$

(or deviance increase $\Delta D(\theta_j) = \chi^2_{1, 1 - \alpha}$ in `poisson_deviance`). If the profiled objective fails to reach the critical threshold before hitting a boundary, search horizon, or flat plateau, the endpoint reports `CiBound::Open` (`open` / `unbounded`), alerting users without truncating to symmetric Wald approximations (Bates & Watts 1988; Seber & Wild 1989).

### Hougaard Skewness ($g_1$)

When $1 \le K_{\text{free}} \le 10$, $\text{df} > 0$, and the fit is identifiable, `compute_hougaard` evaluates Hougaard's (1985) third-order skewness measure $g_1$ per parameter from central second-derivative tensor approximations:

- $|g_1| < 0.1$: effectively linear behavior (Wald and profile CIs agree closely).
- $0.1 \le |g_1| < 0.25$: mild parameter-effects nonlinearity.
- $0.25 \le |g_1| \le 1.0$: substantial skewness; asymmetric profile-likelihood intervals are materially more accurate than symmetric intervals.
- $|g_1| > 1.0$: extreme nonlinearity; triggers a diagnostic checklist entry (`QOL-7`, `remediation: None`).

### Collinearity & Fit Identifiability (`identify_unstable_parameters`)

Variance-inflation collinearity per free parameter is reported via Bates & Watts dependency:

$$R_j^2 = 1 - \frac{1}{(J^T J)_{jj} \cdot [(J^T J)^{-1}]_{jj}}$$

- `Dependency > 0.99`: emits a collinearity warning on the parameter and checklist.
- `FitIdentifiability::Ambiguous` (`FitStatus::Ambiguous`, `ParameterNote::Unstable`, checklist metric `"Dependency > 0.9999 or rank-deficient Jacobian"`): raised when rank-revealing QR detects numerical rank deficiency, $R_j^2 > 0.9999$ (`MAX_DEPENDENCY = 1 - 1 / 10000`), or profile-likelihood intervals return `CiBound::Open` on unidentifiable asymptotes/EC50 plateaus (for instance, sparse dose-response curves lacking upper/lower concentration coverage per Sebaugh 2011).

### Residual Diagnostics, Range Filters & Threshold Alerts

- **Inclusive predictor filter (`x_range_filter`):** Restricts fit observations to active rows satisfying $X \in [x_{\text{min}}, x_{\text{max}}]$ (unbounded on omitted sides) while optionally evaluating curve overlays over an independent `[plot_x_min, plot_x_max]` display range. Counts points excluded by the range filter cleanly.
- **Unweighted $R^2$ alert (`flag_r_squared_below`):** Optional threshold in $[0, 1]$ emitting an `R squared below threshold` diagnostic checklist entry (`ChecklistStatus::Warn`, `remediation: None`) whenever unweighted $R^2$ drops below threshold.
- **Internally studentized residuals:** $e_i = r_{w,i} / (s_w \sqrt{1 - h_{ii}})$ using tangent-plane leverage $h_{ii} = J_i (J^T J)^{-1} J_i^T$ (Cook & Weisberg 1982) when identifiable and $K_{\text{free}} \le 64$.
- **Replicates lack-of-fit test:** Partitions residual variance/deviance across exact replicate predictor groups into `Pure Error` and `Lack of Fit`, returning an $F$-statistic and $P$ value (honoring weighting, Poisson deviance, and replicate summary moments).
- **Runs test:** Wald–Wolfowitz runs test sorted along ascending $X$, combined across datasets in global fits.
- **Normality & homoscedasticity battery:** Shapiro–Wilk (falling back to D'Agostino–Pearson $K^2$ outside SW range), Anderson–Darling, and Lilliefors Kolmogorov–Smirnov on weighted/Pearson residuals, plus Spearman rank correlation of $|r_{w,i}|$ vs $\hat{y}_i$ ($n \ge 4$).
- **Confidence & prediction bands + AUC:** Delta-method mean confidence bands and observation prediction bands sampled over `curve_overlay_segments` (`256` by default; [Graphs Reference](graphs.md)), plus fitted-curve vs empirical trapezoidal Area Under the Curve (`fit_auc`).

> [!NOTE]
> Following `QOL-7`, every assumption checklist item emitted by CurveBook sets `remediation: None` and reports purely objective metrics and limitations without recommending alternative models or transformations ([Quality of Life Capabilities](qol.md#active-qol)).

## Model Comparison & Unknown Interpolation {#comparison-and-interpolation}

### Comparing Models (`comparison`)

1. **Nested Extra-Sum-of-Squares $F$-test (`extra_sum_of_squares_f` / `shared_parameter_comparison`):** Compares a simpler constrained/null model (`alternative_equation_id` or globally shared parameters via `SharedGlobal`) against the fuller model ($\text{df}_1 > \text{df}_2$):

$$F = \frac{(SS_{\text{null}} - SS_{\text{alt}}) / (\text{df}_{\text{null}} - \text{df}_{\text{alt}})}{SS_{\text{alt}} / \text{df}_{\text{alt}}}$$

Under `poisson_deviance` or `likelihood_ratio_test`, performs an asymptotic deviance difference $\chi^2$ Likelihood Ratio Test (comparing $\Delta D$ against $\chi^2_{\Delta \text{df}}$). Emits a `ModelComparison` tab with $F$ / $\chi^2$, $\text{df}$, $P$ value, preferred model label, and percentage difference in residual SD.
2. **Corrected Akaike Information Criterion (`aicc`):** Evaluates small-sample corrected AIC for identical active observations and weights (Burnham & Anderson 2002):

$$\text{AIC}_c = N \ln\left(\frac{SS_w}{N}\right) + 2 (K + 1) + \frac{2 (K + 1)(K + 2)}{N - K - 2}$$

(using $-2 \ln L + 2K + \frac{2K(K+1)}{N - K - 1}$ under exact Poisson log-likelihood $\ln L$, where $K$ excludes fixed constants), alongside $\Delta \text{AIC}_c$, normalized Akaike weights $w_{\text{alt}}, w_{\text{null}}$, and evidence ratio. Unavailable (`None`) in `robust_cauchy` mode.

### Forward Prediction & Inverse Interpolation (`interpolate_unknowns`)

When `interpolate_unknowns` is enabled, unpaired `(X, blank)` rows are predicted forward ($\hat{Y}$) and `(blank, Y)` rows are inverted numerically ($\hat{X}$) along each fitted dataset's curve via bracketed Brent + damped Newton root search:

- **Confidence intervals & modes (`Mean` vs `Replicates`):** Delta-method curve uncertainty $\sigma_{\text{mean}}^2(x) = g(x)^T \text{Cov}(\hat{\theta}) g(x)$ (where $g(x)$ is the parameter gradient of $f(x; \hat{\theta})$) yields the curve-mean band (`Interpolated Mean X` when $Y$ represents an observed single/averaged mean), while adding observation scatter $\sigma_{\text{pred}}^2(x) = \sigma_{\text{mean}}^2(x) + s_w^2 / w(x)$ yields single-replicate inverse prediction intervals (`Interpolated Replicates`) whenever active data include replicate scatter ($s_w > 0$). Forward and inverse intervals propagate SEs via $\text{SE}(\hat{X}) = \sigma / |df / dX|$ evaluated at $\hat{X}$.
- **Extrapolation & non-finite guards:** Any inverse or forward row with predictor outside $[X_{\text{min}}, X_{\text{max}}]$ or target $Y$ outside the curve's monotonic image sets an explicit `Extrapolated` warning flag (or `Empty` when no real root exists, e.g., $Y$ beyond a 4PL asymptote).

## Custom Equation DSL & First-Order ODE Models {#custom-dsl-and-ode}

User-defined nonlinear models compile through `CompiledDslModel::compile` (`custom_dsl`) into a stack-based sandboxed bytecode VM implementing `ParametricModel`. Custom models use central finite-difference Jacobians and support explicit equations, dataset-branch selectors, implicit roots, initial-value rules, derived transforms, and first-order ODEs.

### Grammar, Sections & Precedence

Equations are newline-delimited statements organized into optional `[Equation]` (default), `[InitialValues]`, and `[Transforms]` sections. Line comments start with `;`, `//`, or `#`.

**Operator precedence (highest to lowest):**
1. Parentheses `(...)`, numeric literals, variable/parameter identifiers, and function calls `f(...)`
2. Exponentiation `^` or `**` (right-associative; binds tighter than prefix unary operators, so `-X^2` parses as `-(X^2)` while `X^-2` parses as `X^(-2)`)
3. Prefix unary `+`, `-`, `!` (`NOT`)
4. Multiplicative `*`, `/`, `%` (left-associative)
5. Additive `+`, `-` (left-associative)
6. Comparisons `==`, `=`, `!=`, `<>`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`
7. Logical `&&` (`AND`), then `||` (`OR`)

**Statement forms:**
- **Explicit assignment:** `Y = Bottom + (Top - Bottom) / (1 + 10^((LogEC50 - X) * HillSlope))` (or a bare expression rhs).
- **Local helper variables:** `span = Top - Bottom` prior to the target `Y = ...` line.
- **Conditional piecewise branching:** `IF(cond, then_expr, else_expr)`.
- **Dataset-specific lines (`<A>`, `<B>`, `<A:C>`, `<2>`):** Prefix lines with angle-bracket column letters (`A`..`Z`.. or 1-based dataset indices) or ranges to apply distinct expressions or parameter assignments across datasets in a shared fit. Unscoped free identifiers become optimizable parameters; dataset-scoped assignments restrict parameters cleanly.
- **Initial-value rules (`[InitialValues]`):** Supply deterministic starting formulas using built-in summary tokens calculated from active `(X, Y)` points: `YMIN`, `YMAX`, `XMIN`, `XMAX`, `XATYMIN`, `XATYMAX`, `XMID`, `YMEAN`, `YMEDIAN`, `XMEAN`, `XMEDIAN`, `YAT0`, `SLOPE`, etc.
- **Derived scalar transforms (`[Transforms]`):** Post-fit algebraic expressions (e.g., `EC50 = 10^LogEC50`) evaluated at converged estimates and emitted into `derived_scalars` and summary tabs.
- **Built-in constants & predictors:** Predictor `X` (or `T` for ODE time axis; multi-predictor `X0`, `X1`, ...), dependent response `Y`, mathematical constants `PI`, `E`, `LN2`, `LN10`, `LOG10E`, `LOG2E`, `SQRT2`, `PHI`.

### Built-In DSL Functions

| Category | Supported Identifiers (Case-Insensitive) |
| :--- | :--- |
| Elementary & arithmetic | `abs`, `sqrt`, `cbrt`, `exp`, `exp10`, `ln` (`loge`), `log` (`log10`), `log2`, `pow(a,b)`, `hypot(a,b)`, `min(a,b)`, `max(a,b)`, `clamp(x,lo,hi)` |
| Rounding & sign | `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `trunc`, `sign` (`sgn`) |
| Trigonometric & inverse | `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin`, `acos`, `atan` (`arctan`), `atan2(y,x)` |
| Hyperbolic & inverse | `sinh`, `cosh`, `tanh`, `asinh`, `acosh`, `atanh` |
| Error & normal | `erf`, `erfc`, `normcdf` (`phi`), `norminv` (`probit`) |
| Gamma, Beta & Bessel | `gamma`, `lngamma` (`lgamma`), `beta(a,b)`, `digamma` (`psi`), `besselj0` (`j0`), `besselj1` (`j1`), `besseljn` (`jn`), `bessely0` (`y0`), `bessely1` (`y1`), `besselyn` (`yn`), `besseli0` (`i0`), `besseli1` (`i1`), `besselk0` (`k0`), `besselk1` (`k1`) |
| Hypergeometric | `hyp1f1` (`m(a,b,z)`), `hyp2f1(a,b,c,z)`, `confluent_u` (`u(a,b,z)`) |

### Implicit Equations (`LHS = RHS`)

Any `[Equation]` target with `Y` appearing on both sides (or an algebraic equation where `LHS` is not plain `Y`) compiles as an implicit root problem $F(X, Y; \theta) = \text{LHS} - \text{RHS} = 0$:

- Scans multi-decade, scale-augmented positive and negative probe grids outward from $0$ to bracket a sign change, then refines via safeguarded Brent root finding (`rel_tol = 1e-13`, with `[0, root]` tight re-bracketing near zero).
- Falls back to damped Newton iteration when no sign-change bracket is found. Returns `None` (domain failure) if residual $|F| > \text{tol}$ or non-finite.

### First-Order ODE Models (`dY/dX` / `dY/dT` / `D(Y, X)`)

Single-equation first-order ODEs specify a derivative line (`dY/dX = -k * Y`, `dY/dT = r * Y * (1 - Y / K)`, or `D(Y, X) = ...`) paired with an initial condition (`Y(0) = Y0` or `Y(t0) = expr`, defaulting to $t_0 = 0$ if `Y0 = ...` is given):

- **Integrator:** Adaptive embedded 5(4) Dormand–Prince RK45 (`Dormand & Prince 1980`) with mixed step-error control $\text{err} \le \text{atol} \cdot y_{\text{ref}} + \text{rtol} \cdot \text{max}(|y|, |y_{\text{new}}|)$ (`rtol = 1e-8`, Hairer, Nørsett & Wanner 1993 §II.4), supporting both forward ($t_{\text{end}} > t_0$) and backward ($t_{\text{end}} < t_0$) sweeps.
- **Trajectory reuse cache:** Observations are sorted per dataset along ascending $X$, allowing continuous trajectory frontier advancement and reuse (`MAX_CACHED_ODE_TRAJECTORIES = 4`, `MAX_CACHED_ODE_KNOTS = 4,096`) across curve points and overlays.

### Sandboxed DSL & ODE Resource Caps

All custom equations execute inside strict static compile-time and runtime limits to prevent unbounded recursion or runaway ODE steps:

| Resource Limit Constant | Value | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `MAX_DSL_SOURCE_BYTES` | `1,048,576` | Maximum custom equation source size (`1 MiB`) |
| `MAX_DSL_LINES` | `16,384` | Maximum source lines per equation |
| `MAX_PARSE_DEPTH` | `128` | Maximum nested parenthesis/call AST recursion depth |
| `MAX_AST_NODES` | `4,096` | Maximum AST nodes per equation |
| `MAX_TOTAL_OPCODES` | `100,000` | Maximum compiled VM opcodes across all programs/init/transforms |
| `MAX_TOTAL_DATASET_INDICES` | `50,000` | Maximum `<...>` dataset selector indices |
| `MAX_DATASET_CLASSES` | `4,096` | Maximum distinct `<...>` dataset branch programs |
| `MAX_BESSEL_ORDER` | `100,000` | Maximum integer order $\|n\|$ for `jn` / `yn` |
| `MAX_VM_STEPS` | `100,000` | Maximum bytecode steps per scalar evaluation |
| `MAX_ODE_STEPS` | `50,000` | Maximum adaptive RK45 steps per single curve point |
| `MAX_ODE_VM_OPS_PER_EVAL` | `5,000,000` | Maximum VM ops per single ODE trajectory evaluation |
| `DEFAULT_MAX_ODE_STEPS_PER_FIT` | `300,000` | Global per-fit RK45 step budget (scaled by `clamp(datasets.len(), 1, 4)`) |
