## Published D1 References & Oracle Verification {#oracle-verification}

Every fitting algorithm and built-in curve model is verified offline under CurveBook's clean-room **Decision D1** policy against public reference corpora and primary statistical literature:

- **NIST StRD Nonlinear Least Squares (`nist_strd`, `d1_nist_reparam_builtins`):** Certified parameter estimates, asymptotic SEs, residual sums of squares, and residual standard deviations across Lower, Average, and Higher difficulty benchmarks with both `start_1` and `start_2` starting guesses (including logarithmic response transformations for the `Nelson` model), plus algebraic NIST StRD reparameterization checks across 18 user-facing built-in pharmacology, kinetics, growth, Gaussian, Boltzmann, power-series, and polynomial equation IDs.
- **Pharmacology, Biochemistry, Radiobiology & Growth Oracles (`d1_r18_3_extended_equations`):** 4PL/5PL log- and linear-concentration dose-response (`Motulsky & Christopoulos 2004`; `Gottschalk & Dunn 2005`; `Liao & Liu 2009`), Gaddum–Schild competitive antagonism and unity-slope `pKB` (`Arunlakshana & Schild 1959`; `Colquhoun 2007`), Black–Leff operational partial agonism and receptor depletion (`Black & Leff 1983`), Cheng–Prusoff and two-site receptor binding (`Cheng & Prusoff 1973`), Swillens ligand-depletion total saturation (`Swillens 1995`), Christopoulos–Kenakin allosteric modulator titration (`Christopoulos & Kenakin 2002`), Michaelis–Menten / Hill allosteric / Haldane substrate inhibition / Morrison tight-binding enzyme kinetics (`Cornish-Bowden 1974`; `Morrison 1969`), multi-phase exponential decay and two-phase association, association–dissociation binding, `Verhulst (1838)` logistic, `Hodgkin & Huxley (1952)` Boltzmann sigmoid, `Gompertz (1825)`, `Watts & Bacon (1974)` smooth hyperbolic hinge, `Limpert et al. (2001)` log-Gaussian and area-parameterized lognormal, `Weibull (1951)` peaks, and the complete 6-form Linear–Quadratic radiobiology family (`Chadwick & Leenhouts 1973`; `Brenner 2008`) verified against `R 4.5.2` `stats::nls` / `stats::lm`.
- **Fit Uncertainty, ROUT & Comparison Oracles:** High-precision `mpmath 1.3.0` (80/120-digit decimal equality) and `R 4.5.2` (`stats::nls`, `stats::glm`, `stats::lm`) verification for Venzon–Moolgavkar (1988) profile-likelihood and Poisson deviance intervals (`CiBound::Open` boundary checks), Bates & Watts (1988) / Seber & Wild (1989) linearization covariance and Hougaard (1985) skewness, Cook & Weisberg (1982) leverage residuals, Burnham & Anderson (2002) $\text{AIC}_c$ weights, Motulsky & Brown (2006) ROUT `Q = 1%` detection on raw and weighted curves, Sebaugh (2011) sparse-curve identifiability detection, Deming (1943) / Linnet (1990) jackknife Model II regression, Brent (1973) implicit root precision over 400 orders of magnitude, and Hairer, Nørsett & Wanner (1993) RK45 ODE parameter estimation.
- **Model-Free Spline & LOWESS Oracles (`d1_r18_7_spline_lowess`):** Dedicated XY `FitSplineLowess` curves (Natural Cubic Spline `de Boor 1978`, Akima Subspline `Akima 1970`, Reinsch Smoothing Spline `Reinsch 1967` / `Hutchinson & de Hoog 1985`, Cleveland LOWESS `Cleveland 1979`, and dense data-space point-to-point resampling with nonparametric unknown interpolation; see [Fit Spline / LOWESS Curve](analyses.md#analysis-fit-spline-lowess)) verified against `R 4.5.2` (`stats::splinefun`, `stats::smooth.spline`, `stats::lowess`) and analytical Akima step-overshoot oracles.

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/graphs.html

# Graphs, Page Layouts & Export Capabilities

CurveBook compiles every graph specification (`GraphSheet`) and multi-panel composition (`LayoutSheet`) into a device-independent vector intermediate representation (`ChartScene`, `crates/chart`), guaranteeing identical geometry across desktop canvas rendering, SVG, `%PDF-1.7`, PNG/TIFF rasterization, and ECMA-234 Enhanced Metafiles (`.emf`).

See [Command Reference](../commands.md), [Automation: MCP](automation/mcp.md), [Analysis Kinds Registry](registry/tables.html#analysis-kinds), and [Parametric Equations Registry](registry/equations.html) for graph/layout and overlay parameters.

---

## Graph Families & Accepted Table Types (`GraphKind`) {#graph-families}

CurveBook exposes eight `GraphKind` families (`crates/doc/src/graph.rs`), each bound to compatible `DataSheet` or `ResultSheet` inputs:

| `GraphKind` Family | Accepted Sources | Built-In Visual Representations (`GraphicalDataObject` / Layout) |
|---|---|---|
| `Xy` | `Xy`, `MultipleVariables` | Scatter symbols, connecting lines (`PointToPoint`, `Staircase`, Fritsch–Carlson / Steffen `MonotonicCubicSpline`, `AkimaSpline`), longitudinal replicate trajectories (`IndividualReplicateTrajectories` spaghetti plots), error envelopes, fitted curve & confidence/prediction band overlays (`FittedCurveOverlay`), AUC shading, before-after connections. |
| `Column` | `Column`, `Nested` | Column/vertical or horizontal (`CartesianOrientation::Horizontal`) bars with error bars, superimposed replicate dots (`DeterministicBeeswarm` or `AlignedColumn`), mean/median summary lines, before-after paired trajectories, box-and-whisker (`Tukey1_5Iqr`, `MinToMax`, `Percentile10To90`, `Percentile5To95`, `Percentile2_5To97_5`, `Percentile1To99`), kernel violin plots, and truncated/truncated+raw combinations. |
| `Grouped` | `Grouped`, `Nested` | Vertical or horizontal (`CartesianOrientation::Horizontal`, including back-to-back stacked Population Pyramids) bars/boxes/violins/points arranged via `GroupedArrangement` (`Interleaved`, `Separated`, `Stacked`, `Superimposed`) for two-way and three-way designs. |
| `Contingency` | `Contingency` | Grouped count bars, stacked count bars, and `100%` normalized fraction stacked bars (`PartsOfWholeLayout` / categorical layout). |
| `PartsOfWhole` | `PartsOfWhole` | `Pie`, `Donut` (annular cutout with optional center total), `StackedFractionBar` (`100%` horizontal bar), and `Waffle10x10` (`10×10` grid colored by rounded percentage). |
| `Survival` | `Survival`, `Survival` `ResultSheet` | Kaplan–Meier curves rendered in `SurvivalDisplayMetric` (`PercentSurvival`, `PercentCumulativeEvent`, or `FractionSurvival`) as `staircase` steps or point-to-point polylines, censored-subject tick marks, selectable Greenwood error display (`ConfidenceInterval95` bands or `Sem`), median survival crosshairs, and aligned **Number at Risk** tables. |
| `MultipleVariables` | `MultipleVariables` | Bubble/scatter encoding via `MultivariateGraphEncoding` mapping categorical/continuous columns independently to X, Y, `ColorChannelMapping`, `SizeChannelMapping`, or marker symbol/split panels. |
| `Diagnostic(DiagnosticPlotKind)` | `ResultSheet` / specialized inputs | Exploratory & regression diagnostic plots: `Heatmap` (continuous ramp + configurable `HeatmapLabelSpec` row/column labels & `0°`/`45°`/`90°` angles, optionally auto-created from `transform.run` with `create_graph: true`), `Volcano` ($-\log_{10} P$ / adjusted $q$ vs. effect fold change), `BlandAltman` (bias & limits of agreement), `RocCurve` (sensitivity vs. $1 - \text{specificity}$ + diagonal reference), `ForestPlot` (regression estimates or pre-summarized `Grouped`/`Column` study bounds `UpperLowerLimits`/`MeanLowHigh` with optional pooled diamond and reference lines), `ResidualPlot` (residuals vs. fitted/order), and `NormalQqPlot` (sample vs. Blom normal quantiles). |

---

## Series Styling, Error Bars & Overrides {#series-styling}

- **Series Controls (`SeriesSpec`):** Per-dataset visibility, label, colour with RGBA opacity/alpha, secondary `y2_axis` assignment, marker shape (`MarkerShape` circles/squares/triangles/diamonds/crosses), fill mode (`MarkerFillMode` solid/open/translucent), marker size in points, stroke dash style (`LineDashStyle` solid/dashed/dotted/dash-dot), summary measure (`SummaryMeasure::{Mean, Median, GeometricMean}`), connecting curve style (including `ReplicateLineMode::IndividualReplicateTrajectories` for longitudinal trajectories), composite horizontal/point nudging (`offset` `{ x_data, x_pt, y_pt }`, with `x_data` included in auto-axis bounds), optional bar width/border overrides (`bar_width_override_pt`, `bar_border_width_pt`), independent `show_raw_data` & fitted-curve overlay visibility (so subset-filtered fits draw cleanly without duplicate markers), and `all_series: true` batch updates across all datasets in a graph (`graph.setSeries`).
- **Error Bars (`ErrorBarSpec`):** Configurable `ErrorBarMetric`:
  - `Sd` ($\pm 1\text{ SD}$, $n - 1$ denominator)
  - `Sem` ($\pm 1\text{ SEM} = \text{SD}/\sqrt{n}$)
  - `ConfidenceInterval95` (two-sided $95\%$ Student-*t* interval around the sample mean)
  - `InterquartileRange` (asymmetric $[Q_1, Q_3]$ quartiles)
  - `Range` (`[min, max]`)
  - `ExplicitSubcolumns` (pre-summarized bounds read directly from `MeanSdN`, `MeanSemN`, `MeanCvN`, `MeanLowHigh`, `UpperLowerLimits`, or `MedianIqr` subcolumns)
  with directional options (`ErrorBarDirection::{Both, UpperOnly, LowerOnly}`) and selectable end caps/stroke patterns. On log scales, non-positive lower error bounds clamp safely to the axis floor and increment `ScaleDiagnostics::log_error_bars_clamped`.
- **Per-Point Overrides (`PointStyleOverride`):** Targets `(series_index, point_index, optional subcol)` (`graph.formatSelectedPoints`) to highlight, restyle, or hide single replicates without mutating upstream cell data; exact `subcol` rules take precedence over wildcard overrides.

---

## Axis Scales, Broken Axes & Frames {#axes-and-scales}

### The Seven Axis Scales (`AxisScale` / `GraphAxisScale`) {#axis-scales}

Configured per axis (`x_axis`, `y_axis`, secondary `y2_axis` in `crates/doc/src/graph.rs`, `crates/chart/src/scales.rs`):

| Scale Variant | Forward Mapping | Valid Domain |
|---|---|---|
| `Linear` | $x$ | All finite real numbers |
| `Log10` | $\log_{10}(x)$ | Strictly positive $x > 0$ |
| `Log2` | $\log_2(x)$ | Strictly positive $x > 0$ |
| `Ln` | $\ln(x)$ | Strictly positive $x > 0$ |
| `Logit(LogitDomain)` | $\ln\!\left(\frac{p}{1 - p}\right)$ (unit `[0, 1]` or `[0, 100]`% domain) | Strictly open interior $0 < p < 1$ (or $0 < p < 100$) |
| `Probit` | $\Phi^{-1}(u / 100)$ | Strictly open percentage interior $u \in (0, 100)$ |
| `Reciprocal` | $1 / x$ (with direction reversal option) | Non-zero $x \ne 0$ |

Observations outside a non-linear axis domain (or non-finite points) are safely omitted and counted in `ScaleDiagnostics` (`non_positive_log_skipped`, `out_of_domain_logit_skipped`, `out_of_domain_probit_skipped`, `zero_reciprocal_skipped`, `non_finite_skipped`) rather than collapsing or panicking. Each segment generates at most `MAX_TICKS_PER_SEGMENT = 256` ticks using `TickLabelFormat` (`Decimal`, `AbsoluteDecimal` for unsigned back-to-back pyramid magnitudes, `PowerOfTenSuperscript`, `ScientificE`, `Antilog`, `EngineeringSi`, `Categorical`), paired with per-axis `TickDirection` (`Outside`, `Inside`, `Both`, `None`) and `show_tick_labels` visibility toggles.

### Discontinuous / Broken Axes (`AxisSegment`) {#broken-axes}

Every axis (`AxisSpec::segments`) supports **`1` to `3` contiguous `AxisSegment` ranges** (`MAX_SEGMENTS_PER_AXIS = 3`), each specifying its `[min, max]` interval and proportional visual share, separated by `gap_width_pt` with a selectable `BreakOrnament` (`DoubleSlash`, `Zigzag`, `BlankGap`). Series bars, lines, and points clip cleanly at break boundaries.

### Frame Presets, Thresholds & Additional Ticks {#frames-and-ticks}

- **`FramePreset`:** `OpenL` (default left-and-bottom L frame), `OffsetRangeTufte` (`DEFAULT_AXIS_OFFSET_PT = 6.0` pt offset range-trimmed spines), `PlainBoxed` (4-sided box), `DualYSecondaryRight` (primary left *Y* paired with secondary right `y2_axis`), and `OriginCrossing` (axes intersecting at `(0, 0)`).
- **`AxisThreshold` & `AdditionalTick`:** Horizontal/vertical dashed or shaded threshold bands (`graph.setAxes`), custom labelled tick marks (`graph.setAdditionalTicks`), and vertical reference gridlines (for example null-effect lines on `ForestPlot`).
- **Canvas & Paper Backgrounds (`paper_fill`, `background_fill`):** Solid fills or transparent (`None`) plot/page fills (`graph.setStyle` / **Format Graph › Page**), enabling axis-free transparent foreground overlays and insets in multi-panel layouts.

---

## Annotations, Pairwise Brackets, Piepho CLD & Live TeX Equations {#annotations-and-significance}

- **Geometric & Text Annotations (`GraphAnnotation`):** Lines, arrows, rectangles, ellipses, shaded spans, free-form rich text callouts (subscripts/superscripts, Greek Unicode, **Info constant hooks** `{{Info:Key}}` and **Result scalar hooks** expanded automatically), and legend placement (`LegendSpec`).
- **Live Embedded Result Tables (`GraphAnnotation::EmbeddedResultTable` & `LayoutItem::LiveTable`):** Reactive rectangular cell slices (`selected_rows`, `selected_cols`) pasted directly from a `ResultSheet` (`edit.pasteResultTable`) with configurable `EmbeddedTableStyle` (`transpose`, `show_column_titles`, `show_row_titles`, `bold_headers`, `font_size_pt`, `outer_border_width_pt`, `gridline_width_pt`, `border_color`, `fill_color`), re-evaluating via the DAG across RGBA, SVG, `%PDF-1.7`, and `.emf`.
- **Embedded Raster Images (`GraphAnnotation::EmbeddedImage` & `LayoutItem::EmbeddedImage`):** Content-addressed `ProjectImageAsset` items inserted from **PNG**, **JPEG**, or **TIFF** payloads (`graph.insertImage`, `layout.insertImage`, `edit.pasteImage`, `graph.updateImage`, `layout.updateImage`) with `CropInsetsPt`, `ImageBorderSpec`, `rotation_deg`, and `lock_aspect_ratio`. SVG image payloads (`<svg`/`<?xml`) are rejected under clean-room/licence policy and zero remote URL fetches are performed; decoding enforces `MAX_IMAGE_ASSET_BYTES = 32 MiB`, `MAX_IMAGE_DIM_PX = 16,384` px, and `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = 67,108,864` total pixels per asset and per compiled layout.
- **Live TeX Best-Fit Model Equations (`QOL-16` / `R10.19`):** `GraphAnnotation::ModelEquation` (`graph.addAnnotation` kind `model_equation`, `ui.graph.insertModelEquation`) links a graph directly to a `LinearRegression`, `NonlinearRegression`, or `PassingBablok` `ResultSheet` dataset. Supports `EquationDisplayMode::Symbolic` or `EquationDisplayMode::Substituted` (refreshing coefficients automatically on fit recalculation) and renders using two-dimensional Knuth TeXbook Appendix G math box typesetting (`crates/chart/src/equation_box.rs`: stacked `\frac`/`\dfrac`/`\tfrac`/`\binom`, `\sqrt` with vinculum, stacked super/subscripts, scaled delimiters `\left...\right`, Greek parameters).
- **Pairwise Significance Brackets & Compact Letter Display (`PairwiseDisplayMode`):**
  - `BracketsOnly`: Horizontal/stepped comparison brackets (`PairwiseBracketSpec`) with `BracketStyle` and `BracketLabelMode` (stars `*`..`****`/`ns`, formatted *P*-value, or custom text).
  - `CompactLetterDisplayOnly` (`graph.setCompactLetterDisplay`): Computes exact minimal equivalence letter sets (`"a"`, `"ab"`, `"b"`, ...) directly from pairwise comparison significance records using Piepho's (2004) insert-and-absorb plus sweeping algorithm (`CldOrdering::{DescendingMean, AscendingMean}`), placing conflict-free letter annotations above bars/boxes/violins.
  - `BracketsAndCompactLetterDisplay`: Renders both non-overlapping brackets and compact letters simultaneously.

---

## Colour Palettes, Colormaps & CVD Preview {#palettes-and-cvd}

- **Qualitative Scientific Palettes (`PaletteId`, `crates/palette`):** `OkabeIto` (default CVD-safe 8-colour palette), `PaulTolBright`, `PaulTolMuted`, `PaulTolHighContrast`, `PaulTolVibrant`, and `MonochromePrint`.
- **Continuous Colormaps (`ColormapId`):** Perceptually uniform Oklab-interpolated ramps (`Viridis`, `Cividis`, `Plasma`, `DivergingBlueRed`, `Grayscale`) plus custom user stops up to `MAX_CUSTOM_STOPS = 256` and discrete sampling up to `MAX_DISCRETE_SAMPLES = 4,096`.
- **Live CVD & Grayscale Canvas Preview (`QOL-9`):** Applies Machado (2009) physiologically validated colour-vision-deficiency transformation matrices (`CanvasPreviewFilter::{Normal, Deuteranopia, Protanopia, Tritanopia, GrayscalePrint}`, serialized `"grayscale"` for grayscale print) in the viewport rasterizer (`crates/render`) without altering stored graph specs or exported vector files.

---

## Batch Creation & Selective Style Inheritance (`graph.create`, `graph.applyStyleFrom`) {#style-inheritance}

- **Batch One-Graph-Per-Data-Set (`graph.create`):** Passing `one_per_data_set: true` (plus optional shared `y_axis_title`) atomically creates one single-series `GraphSheet` per dataset from any `DataSheet` or transform `ResultSheet` (`Transpose`, `Normalize`, `SelectAndTransform`), checking `MAX_SHEETS_PER_PROJECT` before mutating the document.
- **Multi-Target Style Cloning (`graph.applyStyleFrom`):** `apply_style_from_selective` (`crates/doc/src/graph.rs`) copies selected styling facets (axis scales/ticks/frame, palette/series styling, fonts, error bar defaults, legend placement, or canvas preset dimensions) from a donor `GraphSheet` onto one target or multiple `target_sheet_ids` in a single atomic undo step while preserving each target's upstream data bindings, series titles, and fitted overlays.

---

## Page Layout Composition (`LayoutSpec`) {#page-layouts}

`LayoutSheet` composes publication multi-panel figures (`MAX_LAYOUT_ITEMS = 64` per page):

- **Physical Units & Presets:** Coordinates and margins in `PhysicalUnit` (`Points`, `Millimeters`, `Inches`), supporting `JournalWidthPreset` (`SingleColumn85Mm`, `SingleColumn89Mm`, `OneAndHalfColumn120Mm`, `OneAndHalfColumn136Mm`, `DoubleColumn174Mm` default, `DoubleColumn183Mm`, `LetterPortrait`, etc.), `FigureCanvasPreset` (`SingleColumn88mm`, `ColumnAndHalf130mm`, `DoubleColumn180mm`, `FullPagePortrait`, `Slide16x9`, `PosterPanel`), `PageOrientation` (`Portrait`, `Landscape`), and `CanvasResizeMode` (`KeepTypographyPt` to preserve exact `pt` sizes & line weights when resizing, vs. `ProportionalScale`).
- **Panel Arrangement, Equalization, Z-Order & Badges:** Embedded `LiveGraph` panels, `LiveTable` blocks, `EmbeddedImage` items, shared origin alignment (`layout.alignOrigins`), plot-scale equalization (`layout.equalizeScaling` with `EqualizeScaleMode::{MatchSmallest, MatchLargest, ExplicitPercent}` normalizing inner `plot_rect_pt` scaling ratios within `<= 0.25 pt`), Z-order stacking (`layout.reorderPanel`: `bring_to_front`, `bring_forward`, `send_backward`, `send_to_back`), transparent foreground overlays/insets (`paper_fill: None`, hidden axis ticks/labels), decorative shapes/text headers, and automatic `PanelBadgeStyle` (`UpperCaseLetters` `"A", "B", ...`, `LowerCaseLetters` `"a", "b", ...`, or `None`).

---

## Publication Preflight & Export Capabilities & Limits {#export-capabilities}

### Canvas Print Preflight (`graph.preflightCheck`, `QOL-8`) {#preflight}

`preflight_check_scene` inspects compiled `ChartScene` primitives prior to export and emits non-blocking warnings when:

- Any visible text element or subscript/superscript span renders below `5.0 pt` (`min_font_size`)
- Any stroked path renders below `0.25 pt` (`hairline_stroke`)
- Text anchor or bounding box clips outside the canvas or clip rectangle (`text_outside_canvas`)

### Supported Export Formats & Hard Safety Limits {#export-formats}

| Format | Engine Commands | Capabilities & Options | Enforced Limits |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SVG 1.1** (`curvebook-svg`) | `export.svg`, `graph.exportSvg` | Exact cubic/quadratic paths, CSS/attribute styling, `pretty`, `include_xml_declaration`, `include_metadata`, `embed_fonts` (when runtime TTF faces present), `outline_text` glyph paths, coordinate `precision` (`0..=6`, default `3`). Validated structurally via `validate_svg_structure`. | Finite bounds, precision capped at `6` |
| **`%PDF-1.7` Vector** (`curvebook-pdf`) | `export.pdf`, `graph.exportPdf` | Zlib-compressed vector streams (`compress_streams`), selectable Core-14 WinAnsi + Adobe Symbol text or optional embedded TrueType / `outline_text` vector glyphs, alpha ExtGState transparency, sRGB / CMYK / Grayscale colour spaces (`PdfColorSpace`), multi-page compilation, physical `trim_pt` / `bleed_pt` boxes, BiDi RTL reordering. | `MAX_PDF_PAGES = 64` pages, `MAX_PDF_TOTAL_PRIMITIVES = 500,000` primitives, `MAX_PDF_OUTPUT_BYTES = 32 MiB` |
| **PNG & TIFF Raster** (`curvebook-render`) | `export.png`, `export.tiff`, `graph.exportPng` | 4x4 subpixel coverage antialiasing (`BEZIER_FLATNESS_TOL_PX = 0.15`), DPI-based or explicit pixel sizing, physical `pHYs` / TIFF resolution metadata (`dpi`), TIFF compression (`None`, `Lzw`, `Deflate`). Aspect ratio is strictly preserved on DPI scaling; oversize uniform targets return an explicit limit error rather than stretching dimensions. | `MAX_RASTER_DIM_PX = 16,384` px per side, `MAX_RASTER_PIXELS = 67,108,864` total pixels (`8192 × 8192` equivalent) |
| **Windows Enhanced Metafile `.emf`** (`curvebook-render`) | `graph.exportEmf`, `layout.exportEmf` | Clean-room little-endian ECMA-234 vector records (`MM_ANISOTROPIC`, 0.01 mm `rclFrame`, 20 twips/pt logical precision, `EMR_POLYBEZIERTO`, Unicode `EMR_EXTTEXTOUTW`, optional BGRA DIB fallback raster). | Finite positive dimensions fitting 32-bit EMF `nBytes` |

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/qol.html

# Calculators & Quality-of-Life Capabilities

CurveBook augments its statistical and graphing core with non-destructive workflow tools and live diagnostics designed to keep raw measurements intact, maintain reproducible provenance, and surface assumption evidence cleanly.

---

## Selection Quick Statistics {#quick-statistics}

Selecting a single cell or rectangular range `[r0..=r1, flat0..=flat1]` in any `DataSheet` computes live summary statistics over all included finite numeric values inside the selection (`SelectionQuickStats` / `GridQuickStats` in `crates/ui-egui/src/grid_view.rs`):

- **Computed fields:** `selected_cells` (total cell count in selection), `n` (active finite numeric values), `excluded` (count of excluded cells inside the selection), `sum`, `mean`, `sd` (sample standard deviation, $n - 1$ denominator; `None` when $n < 2$), `sem` ($\text{SD}/\sqrt{n}$; `None` when $n < 2$), `median`, `min`, and `max`.
- **Filtering semantics:** Excluded cells (`excluded: true`), blank cells, text cells, and non-finite values are excluded from `n` and every summary moment without altering document state.

---

## Active Quality-of-Life Capabilities (`R9`) {#active-qol}

| ID | Capability | Engine / UI Seam | Scope & Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| **QOL-1** | **Non-destructive table archetype conversion** | `table.convertArchetype` | Converts `DataSheet` layouts among `Column`, `Grouped`, `Xy`, `MultipleVariables`, and `Contingency` with a non-mutating `ConversionPreview` (`preserved_cells`, `dropped_cells`, `preserved_exclusions`, `warnings`, `lossy`), preserving `excluded` flags and remapping `CellExclusionNote`s. Lossy conversions require explicit `allow_lossy: true`. |
| **QOL-2** | **96/384-well microplate & tidy long-to-wide reshape** | `table.importPlateMap`, `table.importTidyLong` | Maps `8×12` and `16×24` plate grids or tidy long observational records directly into typed `Xy`, `Column`, or `Grouped` replicate subcolumns during import or paste. |
| **QOL-3** | **Auditable cell exclusion reasons & provenance tags** | `table.excludeCellsWithReason`, `table.exclusionAuditReport` | Attaches sparse `(reason_tag, note, timestamp_utc)` `CellExclusionNote` records alongside boolean `excluded` masks without changing numerical results or requiring reasons on plain `Cmd/Ctrl+E` toggles. |
| **QOL-4** | **Side-by-side split workspace** | `ui.split.toggle` (and inspector/workspace layout) | Docks a live `Graph` or `Result` pane adjacent to the active `Data` or `Result` sheet so cell edits, exclusions, and analysis/fit parameter updates re-render immediately through the reactive DAG. |
| **QOL-5** | **Two-way data-to-graph point brushing** | `SourceCellId` metadata on `ChartScene` | Links plotted point glyphs (`sheet_id, row, col, subcol`) with source grid cells for hover inspection, split-pane highlighting, jumping to source coordinates, and context-menu observation exclusion/inclusion. |
| **QOL-6** | **One-click statistical reporting generator** | `result.generateReport` | Produces deterministic, read-only ICMJE/ARRIVE-aligned statistical methods and summary paragraphs in `plain`, `markdown`, or `latex` directly from stored `AnalysisSpec`, `DataSheet`, and `ResultSheet` values without modifying numbers. |
| **QOL-7** | **Diagnostics-only inline assumption banners** | `ResultSheet::checklist`, `ui.result.inspectDiagnostics` | Summarizes executed assumption checks (normality, variance homogeneity, sphericity, proportional hazards, separation, collinearity, lack of fit, runs) with status (`Pass`, `Warn`, `Fail`, `Inconclusive`, `NotApplicable`), diagnostic statistics, and methodological limits. Strictly **diagnostics-only**: never recommends alternative tests, ranks procedures, or triggers automatic exclusions/remediations. |
| **QOL-8** | **Journal figure dimension & typography lock presets** | `graph.applyCanvasPreset`, `layout.applyCanvasPreset`, `graph.preflightCheck` | Resizes graphs and page layouts to standard publication column targets (`88 mm`, `130 mm`, `180 mm`, full page, `16:9`, poster) with `CanvasResizeMode::KeepTypographyPt` keeping point typography and hairline strokes intact, plus export preflight warnings below `5.0 pt` text or `0.25 pt` strokes. |
| **QOL-9** | **Live CVD & grayscale canvas preview** | `CanvasPreviewFilter` (`ui.previewFilter.set`) | Applies Machado (2009) `Deuteranopia`, `Protanopia`, `Tritanopia`, or `GrayscalePrint` viewport filters non-destructively on the rendered canvas without modifying stored figure colours or exported files. |
| **QOL-12** | **Categorical & continuous analysis completions** | [Analysis Kinds Registry](registry/tables.html#analysis-kinds) | Adds `ResultTabKind::MultipleComparisons` post-hoc tabs inside `FactorialAnova`, weighted Cohen's $\kappa$ (`Unweighted`, `Linear`, `Quadratic`) & Fleiss' $\kappa$, inverted Altman `NNTB`/`NNTH` bounds from Newcombe RD CIs, McNemar discordant-pair OR CIs, custom expected proportions for `PartsOfWhole` $\chi^2$ GOF, exact one-sample Binomial & paired Sign tests, exact $\chi^2$ `sd_ci`, and direct `MeanSdN` / `MeanSemN` support in two-group and one-sample *t*-tests. |
| **QOL-14** | **Seeded randomization, subset sampling & distribution generation** | `table.randomizeGroups`, `table.randomSampleRows`, `table.simulateDistributions` | Performs deterministic seeded complete or permuted-block group randomization (writing ARRIVE randomization keys into `InfoSheet`), uniform/stratified $k$-of-$N$ sampling without replacement, and seeded univariate distribution simulation over `DeterministicRng`. |
| **QOL-16** | **Live $\TeX$ model equation annotations** | `graph.addAnnotation` (`model_equation`), `ui.graph.insertModelEquation` | Places symbolic or live coefficient-substituted $\TeX$-subset regression equations on fitted `XY` graphs (`R10.19` Knuth TeXbook Appendix G 2D box typesetting across screen, SVG, PDF, and EMF), updating automatically when upstream fits recalculate. |

> [!NOTE]
> Instant table-free distribution/Bayesian calculators (`QOL-13`) and wet-lab molarity/dilution/radiochemical calculators (`QOL-15`), along with standalone browser-folder WASM collaboration extensions (`QOL-10`, `QOL-11`), are deferred outside the Beta release scope and are not registered as active commands.

See [Graphs & Page Layouts](graphs.md), [Analysis Kinds Registry](registry/tables.html#analysis-kinds), and [Command Reference](../commands.md) for command arguments and rendering details.

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/files.html

# Files, Persistence, Crash Recovery & Interchange Formats

CurveBook stores studies in deterministic archives and directories, protects unsaved edits with a CRC-checked Write-Ahead Log (WAL), enforces explicit schema-version safety guards against accidental downgrades/overwrites, and imports delimited and project interchange formats strictly at bounded format edges.

See [File Formats Specification](../file-formats.md) and [JSON Schemas](../schemas/document.schema.json) for wire-level definitions.

---

## Native Project Containers & Templates {#native-formats}

### `.curvebook` Deterministic ZIP Archive {#curvebook-zip}

A `.curvebook` file (`ArchiveKind::Project`) is a standard ZIP container compressed reproducibly with deterministic entry order, timestamps, and CRC-32 validation (`crates/format/src/archive.rs`):

| Entry Path | Contents | Integrity / Limits |
|---|---|---|
| `manifest.json` | `ArchiveManifest`: `format: "curvebook-archive"`, `schema_version`, `kind`, `title`, `document_crc32`, per-sheet descriptors (`id`, `section`, `title`, `csv_path`, `crc32`), and `assets` descriptors (`asset_id`, `media_type`, `pixel_size`, `asset_path`, `crc32`). | Validated against `archive-manifest.schema.json` and checked against `document_crc32`. |
| `document.json` | Canonical 2-space-indented `ProjectDocument` JSON (`schema_version = CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`; `image_assets[].bytes` omitted inline). | Validated against `document.schema.json`, finite floats, dimensions, and acyclic DAGs. |
| `sheets/<id>.csv` | RFC-4180 CSV snapshots for every `DataSheet` (`*` marks excluded cells). | Per-sheet CRC-32 recorded in `manifest.json`. |
| `assets/<asset_id>.<ext>` | Content-addressed binary PNG/JPEG/TIFF payloads referenced by `GraphAnnotation::EmbeddedImage` and `LayoutItem::EmbeddedImage`. | `MAX_IMAGE_ASSET_BYTES = 32 MiB`, `MAX_RASTER_PIXELS = 67_108_864`, CRC-32 + SHA-256 verified against `asset_id` and image header. |

**Archive Safety Limits (`ZipLimits::default()` & `archive.rs`):** `MAX_ARCHIVE_FILE_BYTES = 128 MiB`, `MAX_ZIP_ENTRIES = 4,096`, `MAX_ZIP_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES = 128 MiB`, `MAX_ZIP_ENTRY_BYTES = 64 MiB`, strict path sanitization rejecting `..` traversal, absolute paths, and symlink escapes. All disk writes go through atomic temp-file write + rename (`platform_write_atomic`).

### `.curvebook.d/` Unpacked Project Directory {#unpacked-dir}

CurveBook also supports reading and writing unpacked, Git-friendly project directories (`.curvebook.d/`, via `open_project_unpacked_dir` / `save_project_unpacked_dir` / `is_unpacked_project_dir`):

- Mirrors the exact `.curvebook` internal layout (`manifest.json`, 2-space-indented `document.json`, `sheets/<id>.csv`, `assets/<asset_id>.<ext>`) directly on disk for clean line-by-line version-control diffs.
- Preserves non-archive repository files (such as `.git/`, READMEs, or notes) while pruning stale sheet CSVs and image assets tracked by previous manifests.
- Enforces strict root canonicalization, symlink boundary checks, `ZipLimits`, and CRC-32 verification on load.

### `.cbtemplate` Reusable Templates {#cbtemplate}

Saving a template (`project.saveTemplate` -> `.cbtemplate`, `ArchiveKind::Template`) calls `strip_project_data_for_template`, which clears project-specific raw table cell observations and cached computed `ResultSheet` tab numbers while preserving:

- Table archetypes, column headers, subcolumn layouts, and `=` Calculated Variable formulas
- `InfoSheet` constants (`HookSource` targets)
- Complete `AnalysisSpec` pipelines, parameter rules/sharing, `GraphSpec` styling/axes/equations, `LayoutSpec` panel geometry, and referenced embedded image assets (unreferenced assets dropped)

Instantiating (`project.instantiateTemplate`) creates a fresh independent project ready for incoming data.

### Complete-Workspace Sharing vs. Linked Data {#sharing}

A `.curvebook` archive embeds all `DataSheet` values, exclusion notes, `InfoSheet` constants, `ResultSheet` outputs, `GraphSheet`s, and `LayoutSheet`s inside a single self-contained file for collaborator sharing. Projects referencing external disk imports via `ImportLinkSpec` retain provenance metadata; headless/MCP opens under `--workdir` reject stored external link escapes outside the allowed workspace root.

---

## Schema Versioning & Forward-Overwrite Refusal {#schema-versioning}

| Format / Record | Current Version Constant | Migration & Safety Rule |
|---|---:|---|
| Project / Template (`document.json`, `manifest.json`) | `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 7` | Migrations (`migrate_document_json`, `VersionStep`) automatically upgrade schemas `0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7`. Files with `schema_version > CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` fail on open with `UnsupportedSchemaVersion` (`unsupported_version`). |
| User Preferences (`preferences.json`) | `CURRENT_PREFERENCES_VERSION = 1` | Unknown extension fields preserved via `additionalProperties`; `version > 1` triggers warning/refusal without silent overwrite. |
| Recovery WAL (`ops.journal` & `curvebook.lock`) | `CURRENT_JOURNAL_VERSION = 2`<br>`CURRENT_LOCK_VERSION = 1` | Strict NDJSON line validation, per-record CRC-32 checking, and CRC-verified `v1` to `v2` upgrade in memory before replay. |

**Forward-Overwrite Guard:** Before writing to an existing `.curvebook`, `.cbtemplate`, or `.curvebook.d/` target (`save_project_file`, `save_template_file`, `save_project_unpacked_dir`), CurveBook inspects the existing target's metadata on disk and **refuses to overwrite** any file or directory carrying `schema_version > CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION`, leaving newer collaborator files intact byte-for-byte.

---

## WAL Crash Recovery (`CrashRecoveryJournal`) & Autosave {#crash-recovery}

Desktop GUI sessions (`curvebook`, unless `CURVEBOOK_NO_PREFS=1` is set) attach a directory-backed WAL `CrashRecoveryJournal` (`crates/format/src/recovery.rs`) under the platform recovery directory (or `<portable>/curvebook-data/recovery/`):

| Recovery File | Purpose | Limits & Integrity |
|---|---|---|
| `curvebook.lock` | `JournalLockLease` (`owner_id`, `host_id`, `acquired_epoch_ms`, `ttl_ms`) preventing concurrent journal corruption across active processes. | Automatically detects expired leases and dead local PIDs on the same host for safe reclaim (`is_dead_same_host_owner`), or isolates parallel instances into separate directories. |
| `snapshot.curvebook` | Full periodic baseline archive snapshot written on open and at structural/checkpoint commands (`command_requires_wal_checkpoint`, or bounded journal rotation). | Same CRC-32 & archive limits (`64 MiB` web storage JSON cap). |
| `ops.journal` | Append-only NDJSON log of `JournalOpRecord { format_version, seq, crc32, command_json }` (`CURRENT_JOURNAL_VERSION = 2`; `v1` records upgrade in memory after CRC-32 verification before replay) flushed after mutating engine commands. | `MAX_JOURNAL_BYTES = 32 MiB`, `MAX_JOURNAL_LINE_BYTES = 16 MiB`, `MAX_JOURNAL_RECORDS = 65,536`. Tail truncation or CRC-32 mismatch stops replay cleanly at the last valid record and emits `JournalRecoveryWarning` diagnostics. |

---

## Supported Interchange Formats & CSV Parsing Rules {#interchange-and-csv}

All import and export adapters register through `FormatRegistry` (`crates/format/src/registry.rs`):

- **Supported Imports:**
  - `.curvebook` (native project archive) and `.curvebook.d/` (unpacked directory)
  - `.cbtemplate` (native template archive)
  - `.csv` / `.tsv` / delimited text (`table.importCsv`, `table.paste`)
  - `.pzfx` XML files (`table.importPzfx`, parsing tables, subcolumn modes, row/column titles, `Excluded="1"` masks, and Info constants strictly at the format boundary)
  - `.prism` ZIP containers (`table.importPrism`, bounded ZIP reader extracting tabular CSVs, optional table/info metadata JSON, or embedded XML tables while emitting non-fatal `ImportWarning` entries for unrecognized binary or script chunks)
  - `.xlsx` workbooks (`table.importXlsx`, bounded OOXML spreadsheet reader importing worksheet tables while emitting non-fatal `ImportWarning` entries for skipped archive parts or unsupported elements)
- **Import Warnings & Replace-or-Merge Behavior:**
  - Non-fatal `ImportWarning` entries produced by `.pzfx`, `.prism`, and `.xlsx` imports (e.g., skipped archive parts) are surfaced in the desktop **Import Warnings** panel (reopenable from the status bar or **File › Import › Import Warnings…**) and exposed via `ui.inspect`.
  - When importing `.prism`, `.pzfx`, or `.xlsx` into an open project that has unsaved changes or existing sheets, CurveBook prompts before replacing the workspace, offering **Add to current project** (`merge: true`) alongside **Open as new project** (`merge: false`).
- **Supported Exports:**
  - `.curvebook`, `.curvebook.d/`, `.cbtemplate`
  - Table delimited export (`table.exportCsv` / `export_datasheet_to_csv`), **Export All Data Tables…** (`ui.export.allTablesCsv`, folder picker writing one delimited file per `DataSheet`, named from the sanitized table title), Result sheet single-tab or tidy delimited export (`analysis.exportCsv`), and Result sheet structured JSON (`analysis.exportJson`)
  - Publication figures: **SVG**, **`%PDF-1.7`**, **PNG**, **TIFF**, and ECMA-234 **`.emf`** ([Graphs & Export Capabilities](graphs.md#export-capabilities))
  - **Save Methods Report…** (`result.generateReport`): writes `plain`, `markdown`, or `latex` analytical methods summaries, with output format selected by file extension (`.txt`, `.md`, `.tex`).

### CSV / TSV Parsing & Formatting Rules (`CsvOptions`) {#csv-rules}

- **Limits:** `MAX_CSV_FILE_BYTES = 64 MiB`, `MAX_IMPORT_CELLS = 10,000,000` dense cells.
- **RFC-4180 Quotes & BOM:** Strips leading UTF-8 BOM (`\u{FEFF}`), honors standard double-quote escaping (`""`), and preserves embedded newlines within quoted fields.
- **Auto-Detection (`CsvOptions::detect`):** Inspects the first `10` non-empty lines to distinguish `\t` (TSV), `;` (European CSV with `,` decimal), and `,` (standard CSV with `.` decimal). Presets include `CsvOptions::csv()`, `CsvOptions::tsv()`, and `CsvOptions::european_csv()`.
- **Exclusion Syntax & Missing Sentinels:** When `parse_asterisk_exclusions == true` (default), numeric tokens prefixed with `*` (e.g., `*4.52`) import as excluded numeric cells (`Cell { value: Number(4.52), excluded: true }`). Empty cells and recognized missing sentinels (e.g., `NA`, `NaN`, `null`) map cleanly to `CellValue::Empty`.
- **Default CSV / TSV Export Behavior:** `analysis.exportCsv` defaults to exporting all result tabs in tidy format using `,` as the delimiter and the active locale preset's decimal separator (or a single selected tab when `tab_id` or `tab_index` is specified). `table.exportCsv` uses the same delimiter and decimal separator choices, and saving with a `.tsv` extension automatically selects the tab (`\t`) delimiter.

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/automation/mcp.html

# MCP Server Reference

CurveBook exposes its calculation, graphing, inspection, and UI automation surface over the Model Context Protocol (`MCP`, JSON-RPC 2.0). The stdio transport works identically with headless documents or attached to a live desktop window started with `--control <port>`.

For first-time client configuration snippets and verification steps, see [MCP setup for beginners](../../mcp-for-beginners.md). For complete machine-generated tool schemas, annotations, prompts, and resources, see the [MCP Tools & Surface Registry](../registry/mcp-tools.html) and [Engine Command Registry](../registry/commands.html).

## Transports and Wire Framing

`curvebook-cli mcp` reads and writes JSON-RPC 2.0 messages on standard input and standard output:

- **NDJSON framing:** One compact UTF-8 JSON object per line, terminated by `\n`.
- **Content-Length framing:** `Content-Length: <n>\r\n\r\n` header followed by `<n>` UTF-8 JSON payload bytes.

Both framing modes are auto-detected per incoming request. Payloads larger than `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` (`16 MiB`) return JSON-RPC error `-32600` (`Invalid Request`), and the server safely drains up to `MAX_DRAIN_BYTES` (`64 MiB`) to recover framing boundaries. JSON-RPC batch request arrays accept up to `MAX_BATCH_LEN` (`256`) elements (empty or oversized batches return `-32600`). Protocol revisions `2024-11-05` and `2025-03-26` are negotiated on `initialize`.

Supported JSON-RPC methods: `initialize`, `shutdown` (marks the connection shutting down so subsequent operational requests return `-32600`), `ping`, `notifications/initialized`, `notifications/cancelled`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`, `resources/read`, `prompts/list`, and `prompts/get`. In single-threaded stdio mode, `notifications/cancelled` applies to queued/batched requests (pre-cancelling matching request IDs processed later in a JSON-RPC batch) and cooperates with in-process `CancellationRegistry` handles.

Single-call `initialize` request and response syntax:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"client","version":"1.0.0"}}}
```

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{"tools":{"listChanged":true},"resources":{"subscribe":false,"listChanged":false},"prompts":{"listChanged":false}},"serverInfo":{"name":"curvebook","version":"<version>"},"instructions":"..."}}
```

## Attachment Modes and Filesystem Policy

| Mode | Command syntax | Session backing |
|---|---|---|
| Headless stdio | `curvebook-cli mcp [--workdir <dir>]` | In-process `engine::Session` |
| Live-attach stdio | `curvebook-cli mcp --control-port <port> [--control-token <token>]` | Forwarded over loopback `127.0.0.1:<port>` to running desktop `curvebook --control <port>` |
| Strict GUI-only (in-process) | `curvebook-cli mcp --gui-only [--workdir <dir>]` | In-process `UiApp` exposing only the `gui` toolset |
| Strict GUI-only (live-attach) | `curvebook-cli mcp --control-port <port> --gui-only` | Attached to a `--gui-only` desktop control listener |

Pass `--workdir <dir>` to confine all filesystem reads, saves, exports, and external delimited-file links inside `<dir>` using canonicalized containment checks (`ErrorCode::PathEscape` if violated). `--workdir` and `--control-port` (including `CURVEBOOK_CONTROL_PORT`) are mutually exclusive and fail immediately with exit code `2`, because `--workdir` cannot confine file operations executed inside a live-attached desktop host process.

Environment variables for live-attach connections:

- `CURVEBOOK_CONTROL_PORT`: Loopback TCP control port (`1..=65535`); overridden by `--control-port`.
- `CURVEBOOK_CONTROL_TOKEN`: Bearer authentication token; overridden by `--control-token`, or auto-discovered from the per-port `control-<port>.token` file written by the desktop listener.
- `CURVEBOOK_CONFIG_DIR`: Overrides the platform configuration directory searched for `control-<port>.token`.
- `CURVEBOOK_CONTROL_IO_TIMEOUT_MS`: Loopback TCP read/write I/O timeout in milliseconds (`100..=600_000` ms; defaults to 30 s for standard RPCs and 120 s for heavy operations such as `doc.export`, `command.batch`, `engine.execute`, imports, and renders; TCP connect uses a fixed 2 s timeout).

## Core Tools and Dynamic Toolsets

On startup in normal mode, `tools/list` exposes the core MCP tools immediately (`doc_inspect`, `open_file`, `save_file`, `command_list`, `command_run`, `command_batch`, `render_preview`, `export`, `list_toolsets`, `enable_toolset`). `command_batch` accepts up to `MAX_BATCH_COMMANDS` (`1024`) command steps per call. Call `list_toolsets` and `enable_toolset` to load per-command tools grouped by engine `CommandGroup` or to toggle the `gui` toolset dynamically (which emits `notifications/tools/list_changed`).

Each tool carries standard MCP `annotations` derived from its typed `Effects` mask:

- `readOnlyHint`: `true` when the operation neither mutates the document nor alters UI/toolset state (`CHANGES_UI_STATE`), discards data, writes the filesystem, or launches subprocesses.
- `destructiveHint`: `true` when `MAY_DISCARD_DATA` or `WRITES_FILESYSTEM` is set (file-writing tools can overwrite existing targets on disk).
- `idempotentHint`: `true` when repeated calls with identical parameters produce the same state (`IDEMPOTENT`).
- `openWorldHint`: `true` when `Effects` includes `READS_FILESYSTEM`, `WRITES_FILESYSTEM`, or `LAUNCHES_PROCESS`, and `false` for pure in-memory tools (CurveBook performs zero outbound network requests).

Single-call `tools/call` request and response syntax (`doc_inspect`):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"doc_inspect","arguments":{"include_cells":false}}}
```

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"title\":\"Untitled Project\",\"schema_version\":7,\"file_path\":null,\"dirty\":false,\"total_sheet_count\":0,\"active_sheet_id\":null,\"family_anchor_sheet_id\":null,\"sheets\":{\"data\":[],\"info\":[],\"analyses\":[],\"graphs\":[],\"layouts\":[]},\"variables\":{\"info_constants\":[],\"result_scalars\":[]},\"hooks\":[],\"analyses\":[],\"graphs\":[],\"layouts\":[]}"}],"isError":false,"structuredContent":{"title":"Untitled Project","schema_version":7,"file_path":null,"dirty":false,"total_sheet_count":0,"active_sheet_id":null,"family_anchor_sheet_id":null,"sheets":{"data":[],"info":[],"analyses":[],"graphs":[],"layouts":[]},"variables":{"info_constants":[],"result_scalars":[]},"hooks":[],"analyses":[],"graphs":[],"layouts":[]}}}
```

In `--control-port` live-attach mode, calling `doc_inspect` without `sheet_id` always returns `mode: "live_attach"`, `control_port`, the live desktop `snapshot`, and top-level project summary fields (regardless of `include_cells`); supplying `sheet_id` returns the targeted sheet detail (with optional `include_cells` previews) plus `mode` and `control_port`.

Exact schemas, annotations, and single-call JSON request/response examples for every core tool, every dynamic `CommandGroup` toolset, and the `gui` toolset are published in the [MCP Tools & Surface Registry](../registry/mcp-tools.html).

## Resources and Prompts

- **Resources (`resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`, `resources/read`):** Exposes `sheet://<id>` (`application/json`) for every sheet in the active project, `result://<id>` (`application/json`) for computed `ResultSheet` outputs, and URI templates (`sheet://{id}`, `result://{id}`) via `resources/templates/list`. Disabled under `--gui-only` (`resources/list` and `resources/templates/list` return empty lists; `resources/read` fails with `gui_only_violation`).
- **Prompts (`prompts/list`, `prompts/get`):** Built-in structured prompts (`dose_response_curve_fit`, `choose_two_group_test`, `publication_figure_checklist`) provide parameterised analysis checklists tailored to either standard mode or `--gui-only` mode.

Single-call `resources/read` syntax:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"resources/read","params":{"uri":"sheet://data-1"}}
```

## Strict `--gui-only` Policy {#gui-only}

Under `--gui-only` (`GuiOnlyPolicy::Strict`), `tools/list` exposes only the interactive `gui` toolset (`ui_inspect`, `ui_screenshot`, `ui_pointer_gesture`, `ui_type_text`, `ui_press_key`, `ui_invoke_menu`, `ui_switch_tab`, `ui_answer_dialog`). Calling `resources/read` returns JSON-RPC error `-32600` (`Invalid Request`) with `data.code: "gui_only_violation"`. Calling any non-`gui` tool (`command_run`, `command_batch`, `enable_toolset`, `doc_inspect`, `open_file`, `save_file`, `export`, `render_preview`) returns a `tools/call` result with `isError: true` and `structuredContent.code: "gui_only_violation"` (or JSON-RPC `-32600` if surfaced as a protocol-level error).

## Structured Error Payloads

Tool execution failures set `result.isError: true` and emit a structured JSON object matching `StructuredErrorPayload`: `code`, `category`, `message`, `retryable`, `remediation`, and `details` (`command_batch` adds `failed_index`, `failed_command_id`, and `error`). For the full catalog of `ErrorCode` variants, see [Control Protocol & Batch Reference](control-and-batch.md#error-codes).

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/automation/cli.html

# CLI Reference (`curvebook-cli`)

`curvebook-cli` is the headless command-line runner and stdio MCP entry point for CurveBook. Command names, usage lines, flags, defaults, and exit codes in the [CLI Reference Registry](../registry/cli.html) and in `curvebook-cli --help` are generated from the same typed Rust catalog (`cli_catalog.rs`).

## Global Syntax and Options

Single-call top-level invocation forms:

```sh
curvebook-cli <command> [args]
curvebook-cli <command-id> [--in <file>] [--out <file>] [--workdir <dir>] [--json] [--<param> <val> ...]
curvebook-cli --help
curvebook-cli --version
```

- `-h`, `--help`, `help [subcommand]`: Print the command catalog or subcommand flag help and exit with `0`.
- `-V`, `--version`, `version`: Print the `curvebook-cli` package version and exit with `0`.

## Subcommands Summary

Every built-in subcommand accepts `-h` / `--help` and follows deterministic single-call flag syntax:

- `info <file> [--json]` — Inspect tables, info sheets, analyses, graphs, and layouts in an archive or project file.
- `commands [--group <group>] [--json]` — List registered engine commands with schemas, effects, and shortcuts (see the [Engine Command Registry](../registry/commands.html)).
- `<command-id> [--in <file>] [--out <file>] [--workdir <dir>] [--json] [--<param> <val> ...]` — Invoke any registered engine command directly with schema-typed flags (`--no-<param>` negates booleans).
- `run <script> [--workdir <dir>] [--json]` — Execute an NDJSON or JSON-array command stream headlessly (`-` reads `stdin`).
- `batch <manifest> [--workdir <dir>] [--json]` — Execute a `curvebook.batch.v1` manifest headlessly (see [Control Protocol & Batch Reference](control-and-batch.md#batch-manifest)).
- `convert <in> <out> [--format <fmt>] [--sheet <id>] [--dpi <u16>] [--pdf-version <1.4|1.7>] [--ttf-font <path>] [--json]` — Convert archives, `.curvebook.d/` unpacked directories, templates, or interchange data files, or export tables and figures.
- `export <in> (<out> | --out <out>) [--format <fmt>] [--sheet <id>] [--dpi <u16>] [--pdf-version <1.4|1.7>] [--ttf-font <path>] [--json]` — Export a specific table, graph, layout, or project to SVG, PDF, EMF, PNG, TIFF, CSV, TSV, JSON, `.curvebook`, or `.curvebook.d`.
- `bench <file> [--json]` — Measure parse, recalculation, scene compilation, and export timings on a project file.
- `perf [--json] [--require-release]` — Run synthetic performance budget checks.
- `mcp [--control-port <port>] [--gui-only] [--workdir <dir>] [--control-token <token>]` — Start the stdio [MCP Server](mcp.md).

Full argument, flag, default value, and option descriptions for every subcommand live in the generated [CLI Reference Registry](../registry/cli.html).

## Direct Command Flag Mapping

When invoking an engine command ID directly on the command line (for example `curvebook-cli sheet.createData --in proj.curvebook --out proj.curvebook --kind xy`), CLI flags are validated against the command's JSON parameter schema:

- String, integer, float, and array parameters accept `--<param> <value>` or `--<param>=<value>` (JSON arrays/objects are parsed when the schema expects structured fields).
- Boolean parameters accept `--<param>` (sets `true`), `--<param>=true|false`, or `--no-<param>` (sets `false`).
- Unknown parameters, wrong types, or `--workdir` path escapes fail immediately before mutation with exit code `2`.

## Exit Codes and Structured JSON Errors {#exit-codes}

| Code | Constant | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | `EXIT_OK` | Command completed cleanly. |
| `1` | `EXIT_RUNTIME` | I/O error, archive/format error, solver/math failure, or engine runtime error. |
| `2` | `EXIT_USAGE_OR_POLICY` | Invalid CLI syntax, unknown flag/command, malformed batch schema, or `--workdir` containment violation. |
| `130` | `EXIT_INTERRUPTED` | Cancelled or interrupted (`SIGINT` / `ErrorCode::Cancelled`). |

Passing `--json` before `--` guarantees that failures write a structured JSON `CliErrorEnvelope` (`{"error":{"code","category","message","retryable","remediation","details"}}`) to standard output rather than plain text on standard error.

## Format and PDF Options

For interchange format descriptors and accepted file extensions (`.curvebook`, `.curvebook.d`, `.cbtemplate`, `.pzfx`, `.prism`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.svg`, `.pdf`, `.emf`, `.png`, `.tiff`, `.json`), see the [Formats & Schemas Registry](../registry/formats.html) and [Files, Import & Export](../files.md). PDF export defaults to version `1.7` (`--pdf-version 1.4|1.7`) and accepts `--ttf-font <path>` for TrueType subset embedding.

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/automation/control-and-batch.html

# Control Protocol, Batch Format & Engine Errors

CurveBook supports three scriptable interfaces alongside MCP: a loopback JSON-lines `--control` channel attached to a desktop window, standalone `run` command scripts, and `curvebook.batch.v1` manifests. Every engine command identifier follows the stability contract documented in [Command IDs](../../command-ids.md).

## Loopback Desktop Control Protocol (`--control`)

Launch the desktop GUI with `--control <port>` (optionally paired with `--gui-only` or `--control-token <token>`) to bind a loopback TCP JSON-lines listener on `127.0.0.1:<port>`. Non-loopback bindings are never opened.

- **Framing:** One UTF-8 JSON object per line terminated by `\n`, bounded by `MAX_CONTROL_LINE_BYTES` (`16 MiB`).
- **Authentication:** Supply the bearer token via `"auth"` handshake or per-request `"token"` field (`--control-token`, `CURVEBOOK_CONTROL_TOKEN`, or the `control-<port>.token` file).
- **Dispatch key:** Requests accept `"method"` or its alias `"op"`.

Single-call request and response syntax:

```json
{"id":1,"op":"command.run","command":"sheet.createData","params":{"kind":"xy","replicates":3,"title":"Data 1"}}
```

```json
{"id":1,"ok":true,"result":{"command_id":"sheet.createData","mutated":true,"message":"created data table sheet","payload":{"sheet_id":"data-1","title":"Data 1","kind":"xy","info_sheet_id":"info-1","graph_sheet_id":"graph-1"}},"error":null}
```

Built-in control methods: `"auth"`, `"ping"`, `"command.list"`, `"command.run"`, `"command.batch"`, `"engine.execute"`, `"doc.inspect"`, `"doc.export"`, `"render.svg"`, `"render.pdf"`, `"render.preview"`, `"ui.state"` (alias `"state.snapshot"`), `"app.quit"`, the interactive `ui.*` GUI actions (`ui.inspect`, `ui.screenshot`, `ui.pointer_gesture`, `ui.type_text`, `ui.press_key`, `ui.invoke_menu`, `ui.switch_tab`, `ui.answer_dialog`), plus any registered engine or `ui.*` command ID passed directly as `"method"`/`"op"`.

When started with `--gui-only`, direct engine commands (`command.run`, `command.batch`, `engine.execute`), `doc.inspect`, `doc.export`, and `render.*` are rejected with `gui_only_violation` so external agents drive the desktop exclusively through the `ui.*` surface.

## Batch Manifest Format (`curvebook.batch.v1`) {#batch-manifest}

A `curvebook.batch.v1` manifest is a deterministic JSON document validated strictly against the JSON Schema (`additionalProperties: false`) published in the [Formats & Schemas Registry](../registry/formats.html#schema-batch-v1) before any operation runs. Execute a manifest with `curvebook-cli batch <manifest> [--workdir <dir>] [--json]`.

Single-call manifest structure (top-level keys):

```json
{"schema":"curvebook.batch.v1","project":"in.curvebook","inputs":[{"csv":"assay.csv","sheet":"data-2","kind":"xy"}],"commands":[{"cmd":"fit.run","id":"step-1","params":{"source_sheet_id":"data-2","sheet_id":"fit-1","equation_id":"log_agonist_vs_response_4pl"}}],"exports":[{"out":"out.curvebook","format":"curvebook"},{"sheet":"graph-1","out":"out.svg","format":"svg"}]}
```

- `schema`: Required constant `"curvebook.batch.v1"`.
- `project` / `template`: Mutually exclusive optional source project path or `.cbtemplate` template path (omit both to start from a blank session).
- `inputs`: Optional ordered list of delimited imports using canonical keys (`path`/`file` or inline `csv`/`tsv`; optional `sheet`, `kind`, `subcolumn_mode`, `delimiter`, and `decimal_separator`).
- `commands`: Optional ordered list of command steps, each naming the command via `cmd` (accepted aliases: `command`, `method`), with optional `id` and canonical `snake_case` `params` object.
- `exports`: Optional ordered list of project saves or table/figure exports using canonical keys (`out`/`path`; optional `format`, `sheet`, `dpi`, `pretty`, `tab_index`, `pdf_version`, `ttf_font`). Pass `format: "curvebook"` or `"curvebook.d"` to write the resulting project archive or unpacked directory.

## `run` Script Format

`curvebook-cli run <script> [--workdir <dir>] [--json]` accepts either newline-delimited JSON objects (NDJSON) or a JSON array of command step objects (`{"cmd":"...","id":"...","params":{...}}`, accepting `cmd`, `command`, or `method`). Passing `-` reads the script from `stdin`.

## Engine Error Codes and Categories {#error-codes}

Engine, MCP, and CLI errors carry stable machine-readable `ErrorCode` variants classified into seven `ErrorCategory` values (`input`, `state`, `format`, `io`, `policy`, `compute`, `internal`) and an explicit `retryable` boolean flag (`StructuredErrorPayload` / `StructuredCliError`). See the complete generated `ErrorCode` table in the [Tables & Error Codes Registry](../registry/tables.html#error-codes).

## Command ID Stability Rules

Command IDs used in scripts, batch manifests, and MCP `command_run` calls remain stable across minor releases. See [Command IDs](../../command-ids.md) for naming, command aliases, and canonical `snake_case` parameter schema compatibility guarantees.

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/settings.html

# Settings, Shortcuts & Languages

CurveBook stores interface preferences and custom keyboard bindings locally in plain versioned JSON files with zero remote syncing or cloud accounts.

---

## Preference Keys & Storage Paths {#preferences}

Desktop GUI settings persist in `preferences.json`, governed by [`docs/schemas/preferences.schema.json`](../schemas/preferences.schema.json) (`CURRENT_PREFERENCES_VERSION = 1`, `MAX_PREFERENCES_FILE_BYTES = 4 MiB`):

| Key | JSON Type | Allowed Values / Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | integer (`0..=1`) | Schema version (`1` written by current CurveBook; files with `version > 1` are refused rather than overwritten). |
| `locale` | string \| `null` | BCP-47 UI locale code (e.g., `"en"`, `"de"`, `"pt-BR"`, `"ar"`). Defaults to `"en"` when omitted or `null`. |
| `theme` | string \| `null` | Desktop theme mode: `"light"`, `"dark"`, or `"high-contrast"`. |
| `shortcuts` | object \| `null` | Map of `command_id` -> key-combo string (e.g., `{"ui.gallery.toggle": "Ctrl+Alt+G"}`), merged atop default bindings. |

Forward-compatible extension keys (`additionalProperties: true`) are preserved on deserialize/upgrade; corrupt `preferences.json` or `shortcuts.json` files emit a stderr warning and fall back cleanly to built-in defaults rather than blocking startup.

### Storage Paths & Environment Overrides {#storage-paths}

By default (unless overridden), `curvebook` resolves configuration (`preferences.json`, `shortcuts.json`) and recovery (`recovery/`) paths (`apps/curvebook/src/main.rs`) in priority order:

1. `--portable-dir <dir>` CLI flag -> `<dir>/curvebook-data/`
2. `CURVEBOOK_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable -> `<CURVEBOOK_CONFIG_DIR>/`
3. Portable marker file `portable.txt` located beside the `curvebook` binary -> `<exe_dir>/curvebook-data/`
4. **Platform Standard Directories:**
   - **macOS:** `~/Library/Application Support/CurveBook/` (both preferences and recovery)
   - **Windows:** `%APPDATA%\CurveBook\` (preferences/shortcuts) and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CurveBook\` (recovery data)
   - **Linux & FreeBSD:** `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/curvebook/` (fallback `~/.config/curvebook/`) and `$XDG_DATA_HOME/curvebook/` (fallback `~/.local/share/curvebook/`), with strict UID `0700` fallback validation when `$HOME` is unset.

Setting `CURVEBOOK_NO_PREFS=1` (or `true`/`yes`/`on`) runs in stateless mode without loading or writing preferences, shortcuts, or recovery journals.

---

## Keyboard Shortcut Customization {#keyboard-shortcuts}

All engine commands (`cmd::registry()`) and interactive UI commands (`UI_COMMANDS`) register customizable bindings in `ShortcutRegistry` (`crates/ui-egui/src/menus/shortcuts.rs`):

- **Context Scoping (`ShortcutScope`):** Bindings declare `Global`, `ResultSheet`, or `NonResultSheet` scope so context-sensitive shortcuts (such as `Cmd/Ctrl+T` switching parameters on a `ResultSheet` vs. creating a data table elsewhere) coexist without false conflicts.
- **Persistence & Conflict Detection:** Overrides save atomically to `preferences.json` (`shortcuts` map) and `shortcuts.json`, enforce conflict detection across overlapping `ShortcutScope`s, and can be reset individually or wholesale to defaults (`shortcuts.reset_all()`).

---

## UI Locales & Beta Translation Status (`[Draft]`) {#locales}

CurveBook's i18n catalog (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n.rs`) provides full key coverage across every supported BCP-47 locale (`LOCALES`, verified at zero missing keys via `cargo xtask i18n-report`):

| Region / Group | Locale Codes | Script Direction | Beta Review Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **English** | `en` | LTR | Primary reviewed source (`English (en)`) |
| **Tier-1 Scientific** | `de`, `es`, `fr`, `ja`, `ko`, `pt-BR`, `zh-CN`, `zh-TW` | LTR | Marked **`[Draft]`** in Beta pending native-speaker scientific review |
| **Tier-2 European** | `it`, `nl`, `pl`, `ru`, `tr` | LTR | Marked **`[Draft]`** in Beta pending native-speaker scientific review |
| **Right-to-Left (RTL)** | `ar`, `he` | RTL | Catalog & PDF/SVG BiDi ready; desktop GUI picker deferred to `1.0` (`normalize_beta_gui_locale` falls back to `"en"` in Beta) |

- **`[Draft]` Beta indicator:** Every non-English entry in the UI locale picker appends `[Draft]` (`<Autonym> (<code>) [Draft]`) to indicate machine-drafted translations awaiting community/native review.
- **Locale normalization (`normalize_locale`):** Regional variants normalize cleanly onto supported tags (e.g., `en-US` -> `en`, `zh-Hans` -> `zh-CN`, `zh-Hant` -> `zh-TW`, `pt` -> `pt-BR`). See [Localization Architecture](../localization.md).

---

## Right-to-Left (RTL) & Bidirectional Text {#rtl-mirroring}

Full desktop GUI layout mirroring (`ar` and `he`, `is_rtl_locale == true`) is deferred to **`1.0`** under `R12.5`. In **Beta**, the desktop **View › Language** picker exposes only active LTR/CJK locales (`BETA_ACTIVE_LOCALES`), and `normalize_beta_gui_locale` falls back cleanly to `"en"` if an RTL code is loaded from `preferences.json`.

Unicode bidirectional visual run reordering (`reorder_visual_bidi` in `curvebook-text`) remains active for multi-script figure labels and PDF/SVG exports, while the `ar`/`he` translation entries and horizontal layout mirroring primitives (`mirror_x_for_rtl` in `crates/ui-egui`) remain built in ahead of `1.0` enablement.

---

## Locale Number, Tick & Delimiter Formatting {#locale-formatting}

UI locale selection integrates with `LocaleNumberPolicy` (`crates/text/src/number.rs`) and `CsvOptions` defaults without altering stored `f64` values or numerical computations:

- **Decimal & Thousands Formatting:** Continental European locales default cleanly to `,` decimal display and `;`-delimited regional CSV presets (`CsvOptions::european_csv()`), while English/CJK locales default to `.` decimals and `,`-delimited CSVs.
- **Statistical Precision:** Internally, every transform, statistical hypothesis test, nonlinear solver, and Monte Carlo RNG evaluates over IEEE-754 double-precision values independent of active display locale.

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/privacy-security.html

# Privacy, Security, Licensing & Clean-Room Policy

CurveBook is engineered for confidential laboratory and clinical research data: the desktop application, headless CLI, MCP server, and statistical libraries run offline on your machine with zero telemetry and zero network egress.

See the public [Privacy Policy](https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/privacy.html), [Security Policy](../../SECURITY.md), and [Licence & Attribution Policy](../licences.md).

---

## Zero Telemetry & Zero Network Egress {#zero-egress}

CurveBook's application binaries (`curvebook`, `curvebook-cli`) and core libraries contain **no** network clients, **no** crash reporters, **no** usage analytics, and **no** background update checks:

- **Offline enforcement:** Enforced in CI via `cargo xtask telemetry`, checking source code and dependency trees for telemetry, HTTP client crates, or remote calls.
- **No external telemetry in documentation:** The documentation site uses pure static HTML/CSS with strict Content-Security-Policy (`default-src 'none'`), `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, zero `<script>` tags, zero `<form>` elements, zero cookies, and zero third-party web fonts.
- **Updates:** Because shipped binaries make zero outbound HTTP requests, updates are installed manually from verified release downloads ([Get Started & Installation](get-started.md#updating)).

---

## Local IPC, MCP Confinement & Trust Boundaries {#local-security}

### `--workdir` Filesystem Confinement (CLI & MCP) {#workdir-confinement}

- Launching `curvebook-cli mcp --workdir <dir>` or `curvebook-cli ... --workdir <dir>` confines every file read, write, archive open, external import link, and figure export strictly inside the canonicalized `<dir>` boundary (`crates/engine/src/path_policy.rs`, `crates/mcp/src/formats.rs`).
- Relative escape segments (`..`), absolute paths outside `<dir>`, and symlinks resolving outside `<dir>` fail with `ErrorCode::PathEscape` (`path_escape`) without creating missing parent directories.
- Without `--workdir`, commands execute with your OS user account permissions (`Unconstrained local-user mode`); AI assistants and untrusted MCP prompts should always run with `--workdir <dir>` (see [Automation: MCP](automation/mcp.md)).

### Loopback-Only `--control` Socket {#control-socket}

When enabled via `--control <port>` (or `CURVEBOOK_CONTROL_PORT`, `port` in `1..=65535`):

- Binds strictly to **`127.0.0.1:<port>`** (loopback interface only — never `0.0.0.0` or external NICs).
- Authenticates JSON-lines commands with a constant-time bearer token (`CURVEBOOK_CONTROL_TOKEN` environment variable recommended; passing `--control-token` on the CLI exposes the secret in `ps` process listings and triggers a stderr warning).
- Combining `--gui-only` blocks direct non-GUI engine mutations (`ErrorCode::GuiOnlyViolation`) so external automation drives only interactive GUI actions.

---

## GitHub Pages & GitHub Releases Policies {#pages-and-releases}

- **GitHub Pages:** Serves static documentation (`docs/index.html`, `docs/privacy.html`, `docs/manual/`) directly via GitHub infrastructure with zero application tracking, zero analytics beacons, and strict zero-script rendering (`privacy.html` documents GitHub hosting metadata policies).
- **GitHub Releases & Build Attestations:** Every Beta release package and `SHA256SUMS.txt` is published through GitHub Actions (`release-scan` security gate) and receives a keyless OIDC/Sigstore build provenance attestation (`actions/attest-build-provenance`, documented in [Releasing](../release/releasing.md)). Attestation calls run strictly inside CI workflows (`id-token: write`, `attestations: write`), adding zero network behavior to compiled CurveBook binaries.

---

## Licensing, Dependencies & Attributions {#licensing}

- **Dual Licence:** CurveBook source code is dual-licensed under **`MIT OR Apache-2.0`** ([Cargo.toml](../../Cargo.toml), [NOTICE](../../NOTICE)).
- **Permissive Dependency Allowlist:** Checked continuously via `cargo deny check` (`deny.toml`) and `cargo xtask licenses`, allowing only permissive SPDX licences (`MIT`, `Apache-2.0`, `BSD-2-Clause`, `BSD-3-Clause`, `ISC`, `Zlib`, `Unicode-3.0`, `CC0-1.0`) and prohibiting all copyleft dependencies (`GPL-*`, `AGPL-*`, `LGPL-*`). See [Licence & Attribution Policy](../licences.md).
- **Release Notices:** Every release includes `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.html` alongside [`ATTRIBUTION.md`](../../ATTRIBUTION.md) and [`NOTICE`](../../NOTICE). CurveBook repositories and binaries contain **zero bundled binary font files** (`cargo xtask assets`); custom builds using `CURVEBOOK_FONTS_DIR` embed only explicitly supplied `OFL-1.1` font files.

---

## Clean-Room Implementation Statement {#clean-room}

CurveBook is an original clean-room scientific software suite. Statistical methods, nonlinear least-squares solvers, distribution evaluators, vector graphics renderers, file container parsers, and user interface components are implemented independently in Rust from published peer-reviewed academic literature (`D1` citations documented in the numerical modules, [Analysis Kinds Registry](registry/tables.html#analysis-kinds), and [Parametric Equations Registry](registry/equations.html)), validated against public NIST StRD and open-source reference oracles, and verified continuously via `cargo xtask brands`, `cargo xtask cleanroom`, and `cargo xtask citations`. Support for `.pzfx` and `.prism` files is implemented purely at the external file-format import boundary (`crates/format`).

---

## Vulnerability Reporting {#security-reporting}

Security vulnerabilities, crash bugs, parser exploits, path-escape bypasses, or archive integrity defects should be reported following [SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md). In-scope threat boundaries include:

- Untrusted `.curvebook`, `.cbtemplate`, `.csv`, `.pzfx`, or `.prism` archive/file parsing (bounded ZIP, XML, cell-count, and float-finite checks)
- Path traversal or symlink escape across `--workdir` or unpacked `.curvebook.d/` saves
- Loopback `--control` token validation and `--gui-only` enforcement
- PDF / SVG / PNG / TIFF / EMF export integer/pixel/memory resource limits.

---

Canonical URL: https://hausergroup.github.io/curvebook/manual/latest/troubleshooting.html

# Troubleshooting, Error Codes & Known Issues

Use this reference to diagnose installation warnings, font discovery issues, MCP/CLI confinement errors, WAL crash recovery messages, structured `ErrorCode` diagnostics, and Beta known issues.

---

## Installation & OS Security Prompts {#install-issues}

### macOS Gatekeeper / Quarantine {#macos-gatekeeper}

- Beta universal `.dmg` releases are Developer ID signed and Apple-notarized (`R8.10`). If Gatekeeper flags a file copied across unsigned local media, confirm checksum and provenance with [Get Started: Verifying Checksums & Build Attestations](get-started.md#verifying-downloads), and ensure `CurveBook.app` lives inside `/Applications` with clean extended attributes.
- If `curvebook-cli` reports `command not found` in Terminal, verify `/Applications/CurveBook.app/Contents/MacOS` is on `PATH` ([Get Started: macOS](get-started.md#install-macos)).

### Windows SmartScreen & Smart App Control {#windows-smartscreen}

- **Defender SmartScreen ("Windows protected your PC"):** Beta Windows `.msi` installers (`x64`, `arm64`) are **unsigned** until `R8.11`. After verifying `SHA256SUMS.txt` and `gh attestation verify` against `HauserGroup/curvebook` ([Get Started: Verification](get-started.md#verifying-downloads)), select **More info** -> **Run anyway**.
- **Windows 11 Smart App Control (Enforcement Mode):** Smart App Control blocks unsigned installers and executables automatically without a bypass prompt; signed Windows releases (`R8.11`) or a signed Microsoft Store MSIX distribution (`R8.9`) will address this after Beta.
- **Cross-context duplicate MSI error:** Upgrading or switching between per-user (`Programs\CurveBook`) and machine-wide (`ALLUSERS=1`) installs requires uninstalling the opposite-scope installation first ([Windows installation policy](get-started.md#install-windows)).

### Linux AppImage & Missing FUSE v2 (`libfuse2`) {#linux-fuse}

If running `.AppImage` fails with `dlopen(): error loading libfuse.so.2` or `AppImages require FUSE to run`:

1. Extract the AppImage without FUSE and execute directly:

```sh
./curvebook-<version>-linux-x86_64.AppImage --appimage-extract
./squashfs-root/AppRun
```

2. Headless CLI/MCP binaries sit inside `squashfs-root/usr/bin/curvebook-cli` and require no FUSE or display server once extracted. Ensure the AppImage has executable permissions (`chmod +x`).

---

## Fonts & Rendering Issues {#fonts-and-rendering}

- **Missing CJK / RTL / Special Mathematical Glyphs:** Because CurveBook ships zero bundled font binaries in the repository, it relies on host OS TrueType/OpenType system fonts. On minimal Linux/FreeBSD desktops or headless servers lacking `NotoSansCJK` or `DejaVuSans`, install system fonts or point `CURVEBOOK_FONTS_DIR` to a folder of `.ttf`/`.otf` faces (or pass `--ttf-font <path>` to `curvebook`).
- **Preflight warnings (`min_font_size`, `hairline_stroke`, `text_outside_canvas`):** Run `graph.preflightCheck` or switch [`CanvasResizeMode`](graphs.md#page-layouts) to `KeepTypographyPt` when shrinking canvases for narrow journal columns so labels stay $\ge 5.0\text{ pt}$ and strokes stay $\ge 0.25\text{ pt}$.

### GPU & Graphics Initialization (macOS Metal / `wgpu`) {#gpu-graphics}

The CurveBook desktop window renders through `eframe` and `wgpu` (Metal on macOS, DirectX 12/Vulkan on Windows, Vulkan/OpenGL on Linux). On older macOS releases, legacy Intel/AMD Macs without full native Metal support, virtualized desktops, or systems with outdated GPU drivers, startup or resizing may fail with a `wgpu` graphics initialization error (`RequestAdapterError`, `RequestDeviceError`, `CreateSurfaceError`, `NoSurfaceFormatsAvailable`) or a runtime `GPU device lost` / surface-lost diagnostic.

To resolve or work around GPU driver incompatibilities:

1. **Verify OS and GPU driver support:** On macOS, update to a supported macOS release with native Metal GPU acceleration (or enable host 3D/Metal acceleration in VM settings). On Windows and Linux, install current Vulkan, DirectX 12, or OpenGL graphics drivers.
2. **Try a `wgpu` backend or adapter override from a terminal:**

   ```sh
   WGPU_BACKEND=gl curvebook
   ```

   You can also test `WGPU_BACKEND=metal` (macOS), `WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan`, or `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` (Windows), or allow fallback/non-compliant adapters where available:

   ```sh
   WGPU_ALLOW_UNDERLYING_NONCOMPLIANT_ADAPTER=1 curvebook
   ```

3. **Use CPU-only CLI / MCP mode as a fallback:** `curvebook-cli` and `curvebook-cli mcp` (as well as `curvebook --headless-once`) run all statistical analyses, curve fitting, and SVG/PDF/PNG/TIFF figure exports on the CPU without requiring a GPU or Metal driver.

---

## MCP, CLI & `--control` Automation {#mcp-and-cli}

- **`path_escape` under `--workdir`:** All path parameters (`path`, `out`, `image_path`, stored `ImportLinkSpec` targets) must resolve strictly inside `--workdir` without `..` traversal or external symlinks. Pass paths relative to `--workdir` (e.g., `"study.curvebook"`, `"exports/figure.pdf"`).
- **MCP client connection failures:** `curvebook-cli mcp` reserves `stdout` strictly for JSON-RPC 2.0 frames and prints human diagnostics to `stderr`. Never wrap `curvebook-cli mcp` in shell profiles that print banners to `stdout`. See [Automation: MCP](automation/mcp.md).
- **`--control` binding errors:** `--control <port>` accepts `1..=65535` (port `0` is rejected) and binds strictly to `127.0.0.1`. Set `CURVEBOOK_CONTROL_TOKEN` in the environment instead of `--control-token` CLI flags.
- **`gui_only_violation`:** When `--gui-only` is active, direct engine tools (`analyze.run`, `table.setCell`, `project.save`, etc.) are blocked by policy; drive interactions via `ui.*` / GUI action primitives.

### MCP client cannot connect {#mcp-connection}

Start by checking whether the MCP client can launch the configured server process, then check the protocol handshake.

1. **Use absolute paths for the binary and for `--workdir`.** Set `"command"` to the full path of `curvebook-cli` (for example `./target/release/curvebook-cli` after running `cargo build --release -p curvebook-cli`, or `/Applications/CurveBook.app/Contents/MacOS/curvebook-cli` on macOS) and pass `--workdir` as a full path to a directory that already exists (`mkdir -p /path/to/your/data-folder`). Relative paths resolve against whatever working directory the client happens to start the process in, which is usually not your project folder. A missing or unreadable `--workdir` makes the server exit before the handshake with `usage error: --workdir ... is inaccessible` (exit status `2`).
2. **Do not rely on `PATH` (fixes `command not found` / `ENOENT`).** Applications started from the macOS Dock or Finder, or from a desktop launcher on Linux or Windows, do not inherit the `PATH` of your interactive shell, so a bare `curvebook-cli` that works in a terminal can fail to start from the client. Use the full path (for example the output of `command -v curvebook-cli`, or the absolute path to `target/release/curvebook-cli` from a checkout build). The same applies to wrappers such as `cargo run`; prefer the built binary.
3. **Add `"type": "stdio"` if your client asks for it.** Some clients require an explicit transport on each server entry and ignore or reject entries without one:

   ```json
   {
     "mcpServers": {
       "curvebook": {
         "type": "stdio",
         "command": "/absolute/path/to/curvebook-cli",
         "args": ["mcp", "--workdir", "/path/to/workspace"]
       }
     }
   }
   ```

4. **"No tools available" or a missing server usually means the process did not start.** Run the exact configured command by hand in a terminal, with the same arguments, and read its standard error. A usage or `--workdir` error prints one line to stderr and exits non-zero; a healthy server prints nothing and waits for input. Then confirm the handshake by sending the requests below (output abbreviated):

   ```sh
   printf '%s\n' \
     '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"check","version":"0"}}}' \
     '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}' \
     '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' \
     | /absolute/path/to/curvebook-cli mcp --workdir /path/to/workspace
   ```

   Expect two JSON lines: the `initialize` result (`serverInfo.name` is `"curvebook"`) and a `tools/list` result containing the tool list. These responses confirm that the configured binary starts and handles basic discovery. Next check the client configuration, its protocol logs, and whether it needs restarting after a configuration change.
5. **Keep stdout clean.** Stdout carries the protocol. Wrappers must send banners and diagnostics to stderr. Normal Cargo progress messages already use stderr; `cargo run -q` reduces that noise but cannot repair a wrapper that writes to stdout. Prefer the built binary for a stable launch command.
6. **Source build fails on older Rust versions.** Run `rustc --version` and `cargo --version` inside the repository to verify both report `1.99.1` or newer ([development prerequisites](../development.md#prerequisites)).

Errors that appear after a successful connection:

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| Tool result with `code: "path_escape"` (`category: "policy"`) | `--workdir` is set and the requested path is outside it (absolute path elsewhere, `..`, or a symlink out). Move the file inside the workdir or widen `--workdir`. |
